items.title: Post-disaster disease management and quality of life among individuals with geriatric rheumatoid arthritis after the 2023 Türkiye earthquakes: a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: This study was conducted to examine disease management and quality of life among geriatric rheumatoid arthritis patients who survived the devastating earthquakes that occurred in Turkey in 2023. This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted in a university hospital in southern Türkiye between July and August 2024. The study was completed with 145 geriatric rheumatoid arthritis patients. Data were collected using a Personal Information Form, the Rheumatoid Arthritis Quality of Life Scale (RAQoL), and the 6-Item Self-Efficacy Scale for Chronic Disease Management (SEMCD-6). Geriatric rheumatoid arthritis patients were found to be able to use their medications 1.59 ± 2.33 months after the earthquake and to have their first checkup 6.06 ± 4.92 months later. The participants' total mean RAQoL score was 17.99 ± 7.72, and the mean SEMCD-6 score was 3.97 ± 1.94. Following the 2023 earthquakes in Turkey, geriatric rheumatoid arthritis survivors experienced problems with access to healthcare, disease management, and quality of life. In this sense, the study findings support the need to strengthen post-disaster healthcare delivery for chronic patients. Key Points • Following the devastating earthquakes that struck Türkiye in 2023, geriatric RA survivors were unable to take their medications or see a doctor for a significant period. • Following the earthquakes, it was observed that elderly RA patients had inadequate disease management and a poor quality of life. • The limitations imposed by both advanced age and the chronic nature of RA necessitate the establishment of an effective disaster management system.

items.title: Anti-TNF tapering in rheumatoid arthritis: a retrospective real-world cohort study with long-term follow-up.
items.abstract: To evaluate the outcomes of anti-tumour necrosis factor (anti-TNF) tapering in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients in routine clinical practice and to explore the feasibility of achieving sustained remission after biologic reduction and factors associated with successful tapering. Clinical data from RA patients treated with anti-TNF agents between 2005 and 2021 were reviewed. Among these, patients who achieved sustained DAS28 remission on two consecutive assessments 6 months apart underwent structured dose tapering by increasing the dosing interval (except for infliximab in which the dose was decreased). The tapering protocol reduced the dose first to two-thirds, and subsequently to half if tolerated. Failure was defined as re-escalation, discontinuation, or switch to another biologic due to flare. Descriptive analyses were conducted to explore the characteristics of subjects who underwent anti-TNF tapering. Kaplan-Meier survival and Cox proportional hazards analyses identified predictors of successful tapering. From a total of 668 RA patients treated with anti-TNF agents between 2005 and 2021, 119 who achieved sustained DAS28 remission underwent dose tapering. At 6 months, 85% of patients were able to maintain tapering, at 12 months 72%, and at 3 years 26%. Methotrexate (MTX) co-prescription was associated with a significantly lower risk of tapering failure (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.39-0.94, p=0.03). Neither age, sex, nor smoking status predicted tapering outcome. Smoking and increasing age showed a trend to reduced maintenance of dose tapering. Anti-TNF tapering can be achieved in real-world RA care, although long-term remission remains rare. Tapering can be maintained in most individuals at 6 and 12 months, but by 3 years, less than one-third are able to sustain tapering. Concomitant MTX improves tapering durability, while other factors, such as age, sex, and smoking status, did not significantly impact outcomes. Key Points • Longstanding remission can be achieved in around one fifth of individuals given anti-TNF therapies for rheumatoid arthritis in a real-world setting. • Reducing the dose of anti-TNF therapy can be maintained in most patients for a year but only around a quarter can maintain dose reduction for three years. • Taking methotrexate alongside anti-TNF therapy is associated with a greater chance of maintaining anti-TNF dose reduction.

items.title: The miR-505-5p/CYP3A4 axis associates with colchicine resistance in familial mediterranean fever.
items.abstract: Colchicine is the first-line treatment for familial Mediterranean fever (FMF); however, a subset of patients develops colchicine resistance, the molecular mechanisms of which remain poorly understood. Recently, miR-505-5p was identified as one of the most significantly upregulated microRNAs in colchicine-resistant FMF patients, suggesting a potential influence in resistance. This study investigated the potential involvement of the miR-505-5p/CYP3A4 axis in colchicine resistance. After HEPG2 cell transfection with pre-miR-505-5p or anti-miR-505-5p, miR-505-5p and CYP3A4 expression were analyzed by quantitative real-time PCR, while CYP3A4 protein levels were evaluated by immunoblotting. Direct targeting of CYP3A4 by miR-505-5p was confirmed using a 3'UTR luciferase reporter assay. A colchicine-resistant HepG2 (cr-HepG2) cell line was established through repeated intermittent exposure to increasing colchicine concentrations and MDR transporter activity to assess resistance phenotype. CYP3A4 enzymatic activity were measured using fluorescence-based assay. Effects of miR-505-5p on CYP3A4 were examined following transfection with miR-505-5p mimic or anti-miR-505-5p inhibitor in cr-HepG2 cell line. Colchicine-resistant cells displayed increased MDR1 expression and enhanced MDR transporter activity, supports the resistant phenotype. crHepG2 cells exhibited significantly increased miR-505-5p expression accompanied by reduced CYP3A4 mRNA expression and enzymatic activity. Luciferase reporter assays demonstrated that miR-505-5p directly binds the CYP3A4 3'UTR, and mutation of the predicted binding site abolished this interaction. Overexpression of miR-505-5p significantly reduced CYP3A4 mRNA and protein expression, as well as enzymatic activity. Conversely, miR-505-5p inhibition increased CYP3A4 activity in colchicine-resistant cells. This study identifies CYP3A4 as a direct target of miR-505-5p and demonstrates that dysregulation of the miR-505-5p/CYP3A4 axis modulates to colchicine resistance. miR-505-5p represents a promising biomarker for colchicine resistance in FMF and other colchicine-treated inflammatory diseases.

items.title: LncRNA PCAT19 is associated with Th17/Treg balance potentially via the miR-17-5p/STAT3 axis in systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex systemic autoimmune disease characterized by immune dysregulation, especially the imbalance of T helper 17 (Th17)/regulatory T (Treg) cells. The purpose of this study was to investigate the clinical diagnostic significance of PCAT19 in SLE patients and elucidate its molecular mechanism regulating immune balance in SLE. A total of 40 SLE patients and 35 healthy controls were enrolled in this study. qRT-PCR was used to detect the expression levels of PCAT19, miR-17-5p and STAT3 in serum and CD4 + T cells. ROC curve was applied to analyze the diagnostic value of PCAT19 for SLE. Flow cytometry was performed to determine the proportions of Th17 and Treg cells in CD4 + T cells. ELISA was used to measure the concentrations of related cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-17, IL-10, TGF-β). Dual-luciferase reporter assay, Ago2 RIP assay and RNA Pull‑down assay were conducted to verify the targeted regulatory relationships in the PCAT19/miR-17-5p/STAT3 axis. The expression of PCAT19 was upregulated in the serum of SLE patients, with an AUC of 0.853, a sensitivity of 75.0% and a specificity of 82.9% for SLE diagnosis, and its high expression was positively correlated with the SLEDAI score. PCAT19 was also overexpressed in CD4 + T cells of SLE patients, and silencing PCAT19 reversed the Th17/Treg imbalance, reduced the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-17) and increased the levels of anti-inflammatory cytokines (IL-10, TGF-β) in CD4 + T cells. PCAT19 may function as a potential sponge of miR-17-5p, as suggested by dual-luciferase reporter, Ago2 RIP assay and RNA Pull‑down assay. Inhibition of miR-17-5p attenuated the effect of PCAT19 silencing on Th17/Treg balance. PCAT19 may serve as a potential diagnostic biomarker for SLE. PCAT19 may be involved in the dysregulation of Th17/Treg balance via a putative miR-17-5p/STAT3 axis; however, due to the cross-sectional and in vitro nature of this study and the lack of a bidirectional miR-17-5p add-back rescue experiment, and further in vivo and rescue studies are warranted. Not applicable.

items.title: Osteogenic plasticity of fibroblast-like synoviocytes in rheumatoid arthritis: signaling pathways, epigenetic regulation, and future perspectives.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a multifaceted systemic inflammatory disorder marked by persistent synovial inflammation, resulting in joint degradation and considerable morbidity. This review explores the potential for fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLSs) within the rheumatoid synovium to differentiate into osteoblasts, contributing to bone formation and repair. FLSs, which have similar properties as mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), show abnormal proliferation and activation in RA under the influence of inflammatory mediators and signaling pathways, such as Wnt/β-catenin, Mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), Fibroblast growth factor (FGF), Notch, Nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB), and Transforming growth factor-β/Bone morphogenetic protein (TGF-β/BMP). Dysregulation and imbalance of these pathways impair osteoblast differentiation and promote osteoclastogenesis, leading to aggravated bone resorption and tissue damage. These pathways may impact the ratio of activity between osteoblasts and osteoclasts, raising the potential of targeted therapeutic strategies to restore this balance. BMPs and MAPK also have dual roles in promoting osteoblast differentiation but also contribute to the inflammatory environment in advanced stages of RA. Dysregulation in these signaling pathways causes the FLS-expressed RANKL to enhance osteoclastogenesis and may contribute to RA development. By steering FLS towards osteoblast differentiation, we could enhance bone formation and reduce bone erosion in RA patients. Understanding the complicated signaling networks that control FLS behavior in RA could reveal new treatment routes, potentially redirecting hyperactive FLS toward an osteoblast phenotype.

items.title: Increased patellar tendon and plantar fascia stiffness in radiographic axial spondyloarthritis: a cross-sectional ultrasonography and shear-wave elastography study.
items.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate multiple entheseal sites using ultrasonography and shear-wave elastography (SWE) in patients with radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (r-axSpA). Patients aged 18-65 years fulfilled the 2009 ASAS classification criteria for r-axSpA and healthy volunteers were enrolled. Twelve entheseal sites were assessed bilaterally: the triceps tendon, quadriceps tendon, proximal and distal patellar tendon insertions, Achilles tendon, and plantar fascia. The Madrid Sonographic Enthesitis Index (MASEI) was used to quantify entheseal pathology. SWE measurements were obtained from each tendon; the patellar tendon, Achilles tendon, and plantar fascia were each divided into proximal, middle, and distal thirds. Intra- and inter-rater reliability were assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). 36 patients with r-axSpA and 35 healthy controls were included. The total MASEI score was significantly higher in the r-axSpA group (25.27 ± 10.94 vs. 10.25 ± 5.43, p < 0.001). SWE revealed significantly increased stiffness at the bilateral patellar tendon and plantar fascia, the left triceps tendon, and the middle portion of the left Achilles tendon in patients compared to controls. SWE stiffness showed no consistent correlations with demographic or clinical variables; only isolated, unilateral weak-to-moderate correlations were observed with disease duration, BASFI, and MASEI at specific entheseal sites (rho = 0.33-0.52; all p < 0.05). SWE measurements showed good-to-excellent intra-rater (ICC 0.841-0.999) and moderate-to-excellent inter-rater reliability (ICC 0.640-0.999) across all evaluated entheses. Tendon stiffness assessed by SWE is increased at multiple entheseal sites in r-axSpA, extending beyond the Achilles tendon to the patellar tendon and plantar fascia. The limited and site-specific correlations with clinical and sonographic measures can suggest that SWE may provide complementary information on entheseal involvement, although its relationship with disease characteristics requires further investigation.

items.title: Muscle strength is more closely associated with functional disability than skeletal muscle mass index in patients with systemic sclerosis.
items.abstract: We compared the associations of muscle strength and skeletal muscle mass with functional disability and health-related quality of life (QOL) in patients with systemic sclerosis (SSc). This retrospective single-center study included 84 patients with SSc. Muscle strength was measured using a hand-held dynamometer (HHD), and skeletal muscle mass was assessed using skeletal muscle mass index (SMI). Associations with the Health Assessment Questionnaire Disability Index (HAQ-DI) and EQ-5D-5L were assessed using Spearman's correlations. Correlation differences were evaluated using a paired bootstrap. Multivariable linear regression included continuous HHD and SMI, age, sex, interstitial lung disease, digital ulcers and modified Rodnan skin score. Both HHD and SMI correlated with HAQ-DI and EQ-5D-5L. HHD showed a stronger negative correlation with HAQ-DI than SMI ( ρ  = -0.5698 vs. -0.3342; difference, -0.2356; 95% confidence interval (CI), -0.4161 to -0.0665). For EQ-5D-5L, the correlation difference was not statistically significant ( ρ  = 0.4751 vs. 0.2964; difference, 0.1787; 95% CI, -0.0082 to 0.3758). HHD remained associated with HAQ-DI ( p  = 0.00012) and EQ-5D-5L ( p  = 0.0059) after adjustment, whereas SMI did not. HHD was more strongly correlated with functional disability than SMI and remained associated with both outcomes after adjustment. These findings support muscle strength assessment when evaluating functional status in SSc.

items.title: Real-World Sinonasal Outcomes of Mepolizumab in Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis.
items.abstract: To evaluate the real-world effectiveness of mepolizumab on sinonasal symptoms, endoscopic disease severity, olfactory function, and OCS use in patients with EGPA and CRSwNP, and to explore potential predictors of sinonasal response. We performed a retrospective single-center study including 21 adult patients with EGPA-associated CRSwNP treated with mepolizumab 300 mg every 4 weeks for at least 12 months. All patients received intranasal mometasone furoate; concomitant OCS and immunosuppressive therapy were allowed. Sinonasal outcomes were assessed at baseline and follow-up using SNOT-22, NPS, and Sniffin' Sticks Identification Test-16 (SSIT-16). Blood eosinophil count (BEC), OCS use, and potential predictors of response were also analyzed. After 12 months, mepolizumab significantly reduced BEC from 940 to 60 cells/μL (p < 0.00001), improved SNOT-22 from 55 to 21.5 (p < 0.0005) and NPS from 5 to 2 (p < 0.005), and increased SSIT-16 from 6 to 11 (p < 0.005). SNOT-22 improved significantly at 6 months, with further improvement at 12 months. At 12 months, 76.2% of patients achieved the SNOT-22 MCID, 85.7% reached good symptom control, and 42.9% became normosmic; anosmia decreased from 76.2% to 38.1%. OCS use declined from 80.9% to 28.6%, with a median dose reduction from 5 mg to 0. ANCA positivity and a higher number of previous sinus surgeries were associated with poorer sinonasal response. In this real-world EGPA cohort, mepolizumab significantly improved sinonasal quality of life, endoscopic polyp burden, olfactory function, and OCS dependence over 12 months. These findings support IL-5 blockade as an effective therapeutic option for sinonasal manifestations of EGPA-associated CRSwNP.

items.title: Design of the international '100 DU' study and development of the Systemic Sclerosis Impact of Digital Ulcer (SSiDU) questionnaire.
items.abstract: Previous systemic sclerosis (SSc)-digital ulcer (DU) clinical trials have primarily focused on DU clinician assessment of occurrence and healing, with comparatively little emphasis on how patients 'feel' and 'function' (central to drug approval). Our primary aim is to further elaborate and validate a novel SSc-DU patient-reported outcome (PRO) instrument to capture the multifaceted severity and impact of SSc-DU. The Systemic Sclerosis Impact of Digital Ulcer questionnaire is designed to capture the multifaceted severity and impact of SSc-DU. Our preliminary item bank (comprising 29 items) is grounded within our previous qualitative research, which was developed through an iterative process, including field-testing through expert review and one-to-one cognitive debriefing interviews. The 100 DU multicentre, longitudinal study shall recruit 100 SSc patients with active (ischaemic, extensor and calcinosis-related) DU from international (UK, USA, Canadian and Australian) centres. Our study design shall facilitate the comprehensive capture of patient-reported, clinician-assessed and imaging (photography and microvascular) data. Our pragmatic study design shall include clinician assessments (at baseline and weeks 6 and 20) and benefit from self-administered questionnaire completion at home by patients (including remotely at weeks 1 and 12). Prospective anchor/retrospective anchor questions will be used to establish Patient Acceptable Symptom States/Minimum Clinically Important Differences. Psychometric testing shall adhere to Outcome Measures in Rheumatology (OMERACT) principles. Baseline nailfold capillaroscopy (NFC) thermographic assessments shall provide insights into DU aetiopathogenic drivers. The study has UK Health Research Authority (HRA) approval (IRAS 359781); local Principal Investigators (PIs) will secure site-specific approvals. Findings will be disseminated through conferences, peer-reviewed publications and patient-led organisations. ISRCTN17000942.

items.title: Mechanobiology Informed Target Qualification for Rheumatoid Arthritis Drug Discovery.
items.abstract: Mechanical responsiveness is increasingly linked to rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but does not itself establish a drug target or intervention direction. This critical narrative review uses targeted, selective retrieval rather than a systematic search or meta-analysis to evaluate the contribution of mechanical context to preclinical target qualification. Selected human, cellular, and animal studies are interpreted through five questions: CONTEXT, CAUSALITY, PHARMACOLOGY, ACCESS, and VALUE. RA fibroblast responses vary with loading and inflammatory conditions; in contrast, Piezo1 findings in arthritis and periodontal bone loss suggest that intervention direction requires cell-specific testing. YAP/TAZ and adherens-junction signaling warrant further mechanistic validation, while redox studies caution against assuming a uniform benefit across joint compartments. We propose experiments and advance, refine, or pause decisions that can be revised by orthogonal perturbation and exposure data. This unvalidated framework is a research aid and does not guide clinical treatment.

items.title: Temporal misalignment in rheumatoid arthritis: a model linking microbial metabolic rhythms, circadian clocks, and inflammatory timing.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) exhibits pronounced time-of-day variation in inflammatory activity, including nocturnal cytokine elevation and early-morning symptom exacerbation. Although circadian disruption, gut microbial alterations, and immune dysregulation have each been implicated in RA, these processes have largely been studied as temporally independent phenomena. Here, we propose the temporal misalignment model, which reframes RA inflammatory timing as a disturbance in the relative timing among gut microbial metabolic rhythms, host circadian clocks, and immune effector processes. The model distinguishes three measurable dimensions of temporal organisation: inter-system phase relationships, oscillatory amplitude relevant to temporal coupling, and cross-system coherence. Microbiota-associated metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan-related metabolites, and bile acids are proposed as candidate mediators because they exhibit time-of-day variation and can modulate host clock-related pathways, although direct evidence for such coupling in human RA remains limited. The model predicts that cross-system temporal abnormalities may precede clinically apparent RA, contribute to heterogeneity in chronotherapy response, and propagate downstream when microbial rhythmicity is experimentally perturbed. Crucially, restoration of microbial rhythmicity without corresponding realignment of host clock, immune, and inflammatory timing would challenge the proposed causal framework. By treating temporal relationships as measurable biological variables, the temporal misalignment model extends existing neuroendocrine and gut-joint frameworks and provides a falsifiable basis for time-resolved mechanistic studies in RA.

items.title: Multi-cohort and single-cell multi-omic analyses reveal multicellular mechanotransduction-immune remodeling in rheumatoid arthritis synovium.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) synovitis integrates immune-cell recruitment, stromal remodeling and persistent inflammation, but its relationship with tissue mechanotransduction remains unclear. We investigated whether RA involves coordinated remodeling of multicellular mechanotransduction-immune programs. We constructed a 327-gene mechanotransduction compendium and used GSE89408 synovial transcriptomes from healthy controls (n = 28), patients with osteoarthritis (n = 22) and patients with RA (n = 152) for discovery. Candidates prioritized through RA-versus-Healthy and RA-versus-OA contrasts were evaluated in three patient-independent cohorts using validation-only random-effects meta-analysis. Co-expression networks, consensus clustering, locked external mapping, single-cell RNA sequencing, cell-cell communication inference, virtual knockout and single-cell chromatin-accessibility analyses (11 RA donors and one OA reference; no healthy controls) resolved network, cellular and regulatory contexts. Selected gene-expression findings were examined by quantitative PCR in independent healthy (n = 20) and RA (n = 25) synovial tissues and by overexpression and siRNA-mediated knockdown in synovial fibroblasts. In unadjusted bulk-tissue profiles, RA synovium showed higher expression-based scores for integrin-extracellular matrix sensing and nuclear LINC programs but lower scores for focal-adhesion force-transmission and Hippo-YAP/TAZ-associated genes. Composition adjustment attenuated several of these associations. Nine candidates met the prespecified meta-analysis criteria and mapped to four co-expression modules associated with adaptive and innate immune programs, cell cycling and mechanotransduction-related expression scores. Tissue qPCR reproduced the predicted expression directions. Two molecular states with distinct inflammatory and mechanotransduction-associated expression features were recovered in external cohorts. In exploratory analyses, TLN2 and NRXN1 expression was inversely associated with inflammatory mediators and DAS28. Exploratory single-cell analyses localized the programs to fibroblast, myeloid, lymphoid and proliferating states and inferred differences in fibroblast-myeloid communication potential. Perturbing TLN2 or NRXN1 altered selected ECM-associated transcripts and COL1A1 protein, with corresponding changes in Matrigel invasion within one donor, while transcription-factor perturbation supported candidate FOXP2-NRXN1, NFIX-NRXN1/TLN2 and FOS-TLN2 expression relationships. Patient-derived multi-omic and experimental evidence supports coordinated transcriptional remodeling of a multicellular mechanotransduction-immune network associated with RA synovial heterogeneity.

items.title: Differential Modulation of MicroRNAs (miRNAs) in Patients With Systemic Sclerosis-Associated Skeletal Muscle Loss.
items.abstract: This study aims to evaluate the differential expression of selected microRNAs (miRNAs) in patients with systemic sclerosis and investigate their association with skeletal muscle loss.  This retrospective observational study reviewed the medical records of patients with systemic sclerosis treated at a tertiary care teaching hospital between January 2024 and December 2024. Age- and sex-matched healthy individuals served as controls. Clinical data, skeletal muscle index (SMI), and handgrip strength were obtained from medical records. At the same time, archived serum samples were analyzed for the expression of selected miRNAs (miR-21, miR-29, miR-133a, and miR-206) using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Comparative analyses were performed between patients with and without skeletal muscle loss and between patients and healthy controls. Correlation and receiver operating characteristic curve analyses were conducted to evaluate the association and diagnostic performance of miRNAs.  A total of 110 participants were included, comprising 70 patients with systemic sclerosis and 40 healthy controls. Patients with systemic sclerosis demonstrated significant dysregulation of miRNA expression compared with healthy controls. Profibrotic miR-21 and muscle-associated miR-206 were significantly upregulated, whereas antifibrotic miR-29 and muscle-regulatory miR-133a were significantly downregulated, particularly among patients with skeletal muscle loss. Altered miRNA expression showed significant correlations with reduced SMI and handgrip strength. The miRNAs showed moderate discriminatory ability for prevalent skeletal muscle loss in this sample.  Differential modulation of miRNAs is significantly associated with skeletal muscle loss in systemic sclerosis. These findings suggest that selected miRNAs may serve as promising noninvasive biomarkers for early detection and monitoring of muscle involvement and may represent potential therapeutic targets for preventing muscle wasting in systemic sclerosis.

items.title: Cyclophosphamide modulates renal GSK-3β and NF-κB p65 expression in MRL/lpr mice with lupus nephritis.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is a renal manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) in which immune-complex deposition and inflammation can result in renal tissue damage. The expression of GSK-3β and NF-κB p65 was analyzed in MRL/lpr mice during the development of LN and after cyclophosphamide (CTX) administration. In the longitudinal component, MRL/lpr and C57BL/6 mice were assessed at 12, 16, 20, 24, and 28 weeks of age (n=5 per group). A total of 10 MRL/lpr mice were assigned to untreated LN and CTX treatment intervention cohorts, with five C57BL/6 mice serving as controls. Starting at week 16, intraperitoneal CTX was given once a week, while LN and C57 mice were given saline. Serum, urine, and renal tissue were collected for ELISA, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and pathological assessment at the end of 12 weeks. Across the age series, MRL/lpr mice had greater urinary protein excretion, higher ANA and dsDNA concentrations, and worsening renal morphology with immune-complex deposition. Renal GSK-3β and NF-κB p65 expression also increased ( P < 0.05). CTX did not significantly change 24-hour urinary protein excretion, but it was accompanied by lower ANA and dsDNA concentrations, less severe renal pathological changes and immune-complex deposition, and reduced renal GSK-3β and NF-κB p65 gene and protein expression ( P < 0.05). These observations place the GSK-3β/NF-κB p65 axis alongside the inflammatory phenotype and CTX response in this model; they do not establish a direct causal pathway. Whether CTX changes this pathway directly, or whether the expression pattern follows improvement in the renal inflammatory environment, requires dedicated intervention experiments.

items.title: Comparative cardiovascular safety of febuxostat, allopurinol, and benzbromarone in Taiwanese patients with gout: a retrospective time-varying exposure analysis.
items.abstract: The comparative cardiovascular safety of urate-lowering therapies in patients with gout remains controversial. Our previous network meta-analysis suggested a directionally lower cardiovascular risk with benzbromarone than with febuxostat or allopurinol, but direct head-to-head evidence between benzbromarone and febuxostat was limited. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the National Taiwan University Hospital integrated Medical Database. Adults with gout treated with febuxostat, allopurinol, or benzbromarone between July 31, 2016 and August 31, 2023 were included. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of myocardial infarction and stroke. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular death. Cox proportional hazards models with time-varying exposure were used to evaluate the time to first occurrence of events. The cohort comprised 3,240 patients, with a median follow-up duration of 4.41 years; 151 patients experienced MACE. All-cause mortality rates per 1,000 person-years were 17.99 overall and 11.31, 25.85, and 9.72 in the benzbromarone, febuxostat, and allopurinol fixed-exposure groups, respectively. In fully adjusted time-varying model using benzbromarone as the reference, no statistically significant difference in MACE was detected for allopurinol (HR 1.63, 95% CI 0.85-3.13) or febuxostat (HR 1.17, 95% CI 0.81-1.69). Febuxostat was associated with higher all-cause mortality than benzbromarone (HR 1.52, 95% CI 1.13-2.04), and allopurinol was associated with higher stroke risk than benzbromarone (HR 2.02, 95% CI 1.04-3.92). No statistically significant difference was observed in MACE. However, relative to benzbromarone, febuxostat and allopurinol were associated with higher all-cause mortality and higher stroke risk, respectively. No statistically significant difference in MACE was detected for allopurinol or febuxostat compared with benzbromarone.In secondary outcomes, febuxostat was associated with higher all-cause mortality and allopurinol with higher stroke risk relative to benzbromarone.A time-varying exposure approach may better reflect real-world treatment switching among urate-lowering therapies in patients with gout.

items.title: Anti-Ro52-positive antisynthetase syndrome mimicking tuberculosis in a high-burden setting: a delayed diagnosis with therapeutic success.
items.abstract: Antisynthetase syndrome (ASS) is a rare autoimmune condition characterized by interstitial lung disease (ILD), myositis, arthritis and characteristic cutaneous features. In tuberculosis (TB)-endemic regions, its diagnosis may be delayed owing to overlapping clinical features. We report a 52-year-old woman presenting with a 6-month history of fever and progressive dyspnoea, initially treated as recurrent respiratory infection and later empirically started on antitubercular therapy (ATT). Despite multiple hospital visits and antibiotic courses, her symptoms persisted. Imaging revealed features suggestive of ILD. Further evaluation at our centre uncovered inflammatory arthritis, myalgia, Raynaud phenomenon, elevated creatine kinase (CK) and strongly positive anti-Ro52 antibodies. Antinuclear antibody indirect immunofluorescence demonstrated a cytoplasmic staining pattern. A diagnosis of antisynthetase syndrome was made. The patient responded well to immunosuppressive therapy with azathioprine and corticosteroids, with normalization of CK levels and clinical stabilization. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of ASS in TB-endemic regions, where empirical ATT may delay appropriate diagnosis and management. Early recognition of autoimmune features in ILD is crucial to prevent morbidity.

items.title: Recurrent Fever with TBK1 and NLRP1 Variants of Uncertain Significance.
items.abstract: Recurrent febrile episodes accompanied by variants of uncertain significance (VUS) require cautious genotype-phenotype interpretation. We describe a 48-year-old Turkish woman with approximately monthly febrile abdominal episodes lasting 3-4 days. MEFV sequencing was nondiagnostic, and no pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were identified in TNFRSF1A, MVK, or NLRP3. A broad sequencing panel identified heterozygous TBK1 c.1093 A > G [p.(Arg365Gly)] and NLRP1 c.1175 C > T [p.(Pro392Leu)] variants, both classified as VUS in the laboratory report. Following colchicine initiation at 0.5 mg twice daily, no further attacks were reported over approximately 14 months. C-reactive protein decreased from 127 to 4.67 mg/L initially, but subsequent values ranged from 8.21 to 14.4 mg/L, consistent with sustained clinical attack suppression without sustained biochemical normalization. The phenotype supported a familial Mediterranean fever spectrum diagnosis, with colchicine-responsive undifferentiated autoinflammation remaining an alternative. Interpretation was limited by absent segregation and functional studies, incomplete variant-level annotation, and incomplete documentation of the exclusion of mimics. This observation does not establish pathogenicity of either variant or an oligogenic mechanism, and the colchicine response does not provide evidence of genetic causality.

items.title: FMF-associated arthritis in pediatric patients: clinical features and management.
items.abstract: Arthritis is a common manifestation of familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) and can affect disease management. The aim of this study was to evaluate the clinical features of FMF-associated arthritis and compare patients with and without joint involvement. Recurrence, distribution, and number of affected joints were assessed, and patients with persistent or difficult-to-treat arthritis requiring advanced therapies were analyzed. This study included patients under 18 years of age who met the Eurofever/PRINTO criteria for FMF, excluding those with arthritis due to other conditions. Demographic information, clinical characteristics, MEFV variants, disease severity (ISSF), and treatment data were retrospectively reviewed; joint distribution, recurrence, and treatments were analyzed in patients with arthritis. Among 1,251 FMF patients, arthritis was identified in 20.3%; 88.5% had acute arthritis and 11.4% had chronic arthritis. The knee (60.2%) and ankle (52.3%) were the most frequently involved joints, and recurrent attacks occurred in 66.5% of patients (median 3 attacks). Compared with those without arthritis, patients with arthritis had longer attack duration but lower annual attack frequency (p < 0.001). Fever and abdominal pain were less common, whereas arthralgia, erysipelas-like erythema, and exercise-induced leg pain were more frequent (all p < 0.001). Moderate-to-severe disease (41.7% vs. 27.8%), M694V homozygosity (40.9% vs. 20.8%), and colchicine resistance (9.4% vs. 4.0%) were more frequent among patients with arthritis. In chronic arthritis, NSAIDs provided partial benefit, and some patients required intra-articular steroids, conventional DMARDs, or biologic DMARDs to achieve disease control. FMF-associated arthritis was characterized by longer but less frequent attacks, higher M694V homozygosity, and increased colchicine resistance. Acute episodes generally responded to NSAIDs and colchicine adjustment, whereas a subset of patients with chronic arthritis required conventional DMARDs or biologic therapy. • Arthritis is a common manifestation of familial Mediterranean fever. • Pediatric data on FMF-associated arthritis remain limited. • Concomitant inflammatory arthritides were excluded, enabling the specific characterization of arthritis directly attributable to FMF. • Arthritis was associated with greater disease severity and M694V homozygosity.

items.title: Immunosuppressants in the Maintenance Therapy of Takayasu Arteritis.
items.abstract: To compare the effectiveness of conventional synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) including mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), methotrexate (MTX) and azathioprine (AZA) monotherapy in the maintenance of Takayasu arteritis (TAK). Patients with stable TAK for more than three months, maintained on a single csDMARD plus glucocorticoids (≤10 mg/day prednisone or equivalent) were prospectively followed until disease relapses or change of treatment due to intolerance or adverse reactions. The primary endpoint was the relapse rate during follow up or at the end of this study. Secondary endpoints included rates of major and minor relapses, drug discontinuation, and vascular imaging stabilization or improvement. A total of 209 patients were included: 92 were maintained with MTX, 61 with AZA, and 56 with MMF. The median follow-up duration was 54.0 (95%CI: 46.8-61.2) months. The cumulative relapse rates at 1, 3, and 5 years were 5.1%, 27.9%, and 39.1% respectively for AZA; 8.3%, 30.0%, and 42.1% respectively for MTX; and 18.1%, 55.0%, and 67.3% respectively for MMF. After adjusting for confounding factors, both MTX and AZA demonstrated significantly lower relapse risks compared to MMF, with hazard ratios of 0.51 (95%CI: 0.31-0.85, p = 0.009) and 0.50 (95%CI: 0.30-0.85, p = 0.010), respectively. AZA and MTX showed comparable effectiveness. Similar trend was observed for major and minor relapses. No severe adverse events were reported. AZA and MTX have been shown to have more favorable effectiveness than MMF in preventing relapse during maintenance therapy of TAK.

items.title: Genome-wide mapping shows coding ITGAM variants drive a reversible interferon-suPAR axis in lupus nephritis.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is a leading cause of kidney failure in systemic lupus erythematosus. Coding variants in ITGAM, encoding the myeloid integrin CD11b, are among the strongest genetic risk factors for LN, yet leave its abundance unchanged. Mapping the locus's trans-regulatory effects in blood from 31,684 individuals, the risk haplotype drove a type I interferon (IFN-I) program in myeloid cells. The locus resolved into two haplotypes, with an R77H-linked coding haplotype driving the trans program without affecting cis-abundance and a regulatory haplotype modulating abundance without any trans regulation. In paired blood and kidney from LN patients, the IFN-I and NF-κB arms were engaged and amplified in R77H carriers, and CD11b+ myeloid cells accumulated at the glomerulus and upregulated PLAUR, coupling the program to suPAR, an effector of podocyte injury. Re-engaging CD11b pharmacologically or genetically suppressed both arms and reversed established disease in LN models, and protected mice engrafted with cells from R77H-carrier patients. A Phase Ib trial is evaluating this mechanism in LN. A genome-wide scan found that this architecture, trans regulation without cis effect on variant's own gene, recurs at 80 disease-associated loci, defining a class of checkpoint variants. Together, these findings suggest that a common coding variant can drive kidney disease without changing expression and is therapeutically targetable.

items.title: Yiqi Qingluo Decoction Represses Rheumatoid Arthritis Progression and Inflammation, Accompanied by Suppression of HOTAIR and the Wnt/β-catenin Pathway.
items.abstract: Yiqi Qingluo decoction (YQD), a traditional Chinese formula, has previously been observed to alleviate inflammation and disease activity in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients in our previous studies. This study aimed to further investigate the effects of YQD on RA progression and inflammation, and the potential involvement of HOTAIR and the Wnt/β-catenin pathway. RA fibroblast-like synoviocytes (RA-FLS) were treated with different concentrations of YQD, and a final dose of 40 µg/mL YQD was selected for subsequent experiments. HOTAIR overexpression, HOTAIR knockdown, and Wnt/β-catenin activation were achieved by adeno-associated virus (AAV), shRNA, and BML-284, respectively. Moreover, collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rats were established and received YQD treatment with or without HOTAIR-overexpression AAV transfection. YQD suppressed RA-FLS viability in a dose-dependent manner, accompanied by a similar reduction in HOTAIR expression. Moreover, YQD elevated cell apoptosis, while reducing cell invasion and inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, and MMP3) in RA-FLS; these effects were attenuated by HOTAIR overexpression. YQD also inhibited the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, whereas HOTAIR overexpression promoted its activation in RA-FLS. Furthermore, HOTAIR knockdown decreased RA-FLS viability, invasion, and inflammatory cytokines, but increased apoptosis; these effects were attenuated by BML-284-induced Wnt/β-catenin activation. In CIA rats, YQD decreased arthritis score, synovial hyperplasia, inflammatory cytokines, HOTAIR expression, and Wnt/β-catenin pathway, while increasing synovium apoptosis. Notably, HOTAIR overexpression had opposite effects and weakened the impact of YQD on the aforementioned indices in CIA rats. YQD alleviates RA progression and inflammation, accompanied by reduced HOTAIR expression and suppression of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway.

items.title: Clinical utility of dual-energy CT-guided gout management: a single-centre retrospective before-and-after study.
items.abstract: Dual-energy CT (DECT) can visualize monosodium urate (MSU) deposition, but evidence is limited regarding potential clinical benefits of DECT beyond diagnosis in gout. To evaluate potential clinical benefits of performing DECT beyond diagnosis in patients with gout. We conducted a retrospective pre-/post-implementation study at the rheumatology outpatient clinic of Jeju National University Hospital, Jeju, Republic of Korea (May 2016-April 2020). DECT was introduced in May 2018. Among patients who underwent DECT, DECT positivity and disease-duration discrimination were assessed using ROC/AUC and cutoffs were explored. For prognostic comparisons, analyses were restricted to patients without clinically apparent subcutaneous tophi at baseline and compared the DECT-performed group with the no-DECT group using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). A total of 722 patients were included (no-DECT n = 506; DECT performed n = 216). Among DECT-performed patients, 110/216 were DECT-positive (50.9%). Disease duration showed limited discrimination for DECT positivity (AUC 0.626). In prognosis analyses (n = 645), IPTW-weighted flare outcomes were similar between groups (any flare: OR 1.26, 95% CI 0.87-1.83; flare count: IRR 1.37, 95% CI 0.94-2.01), and change in serum urate did not differ (β 0.01 mg/dL, 95% CI - 0.32 to 0.34). Renal outcomes favored the DECT-performed group (ΔeGFR β 2.39 mL/min/1.73m2, 95% CI 0.27-4.51; eGFR decline ≥ 10: OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.31-0.95; CKD stage worsening: OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.30-0.90). Clinically occult MSU deposition was detected by DECT in approximately half of scanned patients, and disease duration alone had limited utility for identifying DECT-positive patients. In weighted analyses among patients without clinically apparent subcutaneous tophi, DECT performance was not associated with flare outcomes or serum urate change but was associated with more favorable renal outcomes. Key Points • Dual-energy CT (DECT) detected clinically occult monosodium urate deposition in approximately half of scanned gout patients (50.9%). • In IPTW-weighted analyses among patients without clinically apparent subcutaneous tophi, DECT performance was not associated with 1-year flare outcomes or serum urate change. • DECT performance was associated with more favorable 1-year renal outcomes, including greater ΔeGFR and lower risks of eGFR decline and CKD stage worsening.

items.title: Dual anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP antibody-positivity in suspected immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy: a case-based review.
items.abstract: Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) is a rare autoimmune myopathy characterized by severe proximal muscle weakness and markedly elevated creatine kinase (CK). IMNM is generally classified as anti-signal recognition particle (SRP)-positive, anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR)-positive, or seronegative. Concurrent anti-SRP and anti-HMGCR positivity is exceedingly uncommon, and its clinical significance remains uncertain. A 63-year-old man with prior statin exposure presented with progressive proximal lower-extremity weakness and rhabdomyolysis (CK > 12,000 U/L). MRI demonstrated bilateral symmetric muscle edema and post-contrast enhancement consistent with inflammatory myopathy. Although CK initially declined with intravenous fluids and statin discontinuation, weakness persisted and marked CK elevation recurred. Five days later, he was readmitted and diagnosed with sigmoid adenocarcinoma with nodal metastases. Serologic testing was positive for both anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP antibodies, supporting a presumptive clinical diagnosis of IMNM; muscle biopsy and EMG were not performed. Immunosuppression was initially deferred because of active infection and postoperative instability related to newly diagnosed malignancy. Following clinical stabilization, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) was administered over two days, followed shortly thereafter by methylprednisolone. Gradual functional improvement was observed, and the patient was discharged on a tapering glucocorticoid regimen with planned monthly IVIG. A structured literature search identified six publications describing 11 reported cases of dual anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP antibody positivity, although potential overlap among retrospective cohorts precluded determination of the exact number of unique individuals. This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges associated with this rare serologic profile. Persistent or recurrent proximal weakness and marked CK elevation despite statin withdrawal should prompt consideration of IMNM. Treatment may require individualization when infection, malignancy, or other comorbidities limit conventional immunosuppression. The clinical significance and potential malignancy associations of dual seropositivity remain uncertain and warrant further study.

items.title: Systemic therapies and cardiovascular events in older adults with psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis.
items.abstract: Psoriatic disease is associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Shared inflammatory pathways may allow systemic therapies to influence cardiovascular outcomes; however, evidence in older adults remains limited. To estimate the association between systemic therapy classes and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in older adults with psoriatic disease. We conducted a population-based cohort study using linked administrative health data from Ontario, Canada. We identified adults aged ≥66 years with psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis who newly initiated systemic therapy between April 2007-March 2022. Time-varying exposure classes were methotrexate, other older medications, anti-TNF, anti-IL17, anti-IL12 or 23 biologics and tofacitinib. MACE, the primary outcome, included coronary heart disease, cerebrovascular events, heart failure and peripheral arterial disease. Using Andersen-Gill recurrent-event models, we estimated adjusted rate ratios, comparing current use of each medication class with non-use of that class. Among 8967 older adults, 51.3% were female and the median age at treatment initiation was 71 years (interquartile range [IQR], 68-76). Over a median follow-up of 5.3 years (IQR, 2.8-8.5), participants contributed 53,378 person-years, during which 2942 recurrent MACE occurred. In fully adjusted analyses, compared with the respective medication class non-use, methotrexate use was significantly associated with lower MACE rates (rate ratio [RR], 0.81; 95% CI, 0.71-0.92), as was anti-TNF biologic use (RR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.62-0.98). Estimates for anti-IL12 or 23 (RR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.68-1.08) and anti-IL17 biologics (RR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.57-1.06) were directionally consistent with anti-TNF biologics but imprecise, reflecting limited power. Other older systemic medications (RR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.87-1.19) and tofacitinib (RR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.28-1.68) showed no clear evidence of association. In older adults with psoriatic disease, methotrexate and anti-TNF biologics were associated with lower MACE rates. Estimates for newer biologics were directionally consistent but imprecise, supporting further longitudinal cardiovascular safety evaluation in this high-risk population. Systemic treatments and serious heart problems in older adults with psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis. Psoriasis is a common long‐term inflammatory skin disease that causes red, scaly patches. Some people also develop psoriatic arthritis, which causes joint pain and swelling. These conditions can affect overall health. Older adults with psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis often have a higher chance of serious heart and blood vessel problems. In this Ontario study, we wanted to find out whether different treatments for psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis were linked to serious heart and blood vessel problems in older adults. Using Ontario's health records, we identified 8967 adults aged 66 years or older with psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis who started systemic treatment between 2007 and 2022. Systemic treatments are medicines that work throughout the body and include methotrexate, older non‐biologic medications, biologics and tofacitinib. We followed patients over time to find whether they had serious heart and blood vessel problems, such as heart attack, stroke, heart failure or poor blood flow in the legs. Methotrexate was linked to a 19% lower rate of these serious heart and blood vessel problems. Anti‐TNF biologics were linked to a 22% lower rate. Newer biologic results were in the same direction, but less certain because fewer people used them. We did not find clear evidence of benefit or harm for other older treatments or for tofacitinib. We concluded that some psoriasis treatments were linked to lower rates of serious heart and blood vessel problems in older adults. These findings add to what is known about cardiovascular safety in this population, but more research is still needed.

items.title: Apremilast in rheumatoid arthritis: mechanistic rationale, repurposing challenges, clinical evidence and emerging drug-delivery strategies.
items.abstract: Apremilast (APR) is a US FDA‑approved biopharmaceutics classification system class IV drug used as phosphodiesterase-4 inhibitor for treatment of psoriatic arthritis, psoriasis, and Behçet's disease. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) treatment requires a long-term inflammatory control with lower side effects and reduced doses. APR failed to provide clinical efficacy in patients with active RA despite methotrexate therapy in randomized phase II trial. However, a meaningful safety profile demonstrated in clinical trial and anti-inflammatory activity provides a suitable rationale for further preclinical evaluation. However, the APR potential to resolve clinical failure through oral route in RA is still unproven and needs comprehensive preclinical and clinical validation. Despite phase II failure, a mechanistic approach on APR in RA can aid in a meaningful repurposing. In this review, we have listed the repurposing challenges incurred during APR utility in RA along with future perspectives which can modulate the roadblocks. A section circumventing latest research on APR applicability in RA is also added in the review. The exhaustive literature search was made on Google Scholar and PubMed for apremilast in RA till September 2026. Overall, if APR is successfully repurposed via correct route or any combination, this could open new avenues in RA treatment. Apremilast (APR) is phosphodiesterase (PDE)-4 inhibitor indicated for the treatment of psoriatic arthritis, psoriasis, and Behçet’s disease. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic, chronic autoimmune indication which needs a treatment focusing on cost-effective and long-term inflammatory control with reduced side effects. RA is reported to decrease cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP)-signaling–induced inflammation in preliminary conducted research studies by decreasing various inflammatory mediators. The PDE-4 inhibition leads to increase intracellular cAMP which is reported to increase cAMP response elements (CREB)-mediated signaling via protein kinase activation and reduce Nuclear Factor Kappa-β-derived expression and thereby decrease the activity of various inflammatory cytokines like interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-α. The clinical phase II trial of apremilast had not yield an oral efficacy in RA but was found well tolerated in patients. Although oral efficacy was not achieved but still if mechanistic gaps are correctly addressed and outcomes-based formulation exercises are being carried out, APR could be a repurposed therapy for RA. The various formulation approaches, potential drug combination, and other routes of drug delivery for APR in RA should be researched to minimize the challenges encountered in drug repurposing.

items.title: Coronary involvement attributed to vasculitis in juvenile systemic lupus erythematosus: a systematic review of case-based evidence.
items.abstract: Tocharacterise published paediatric SLE cases in which coronary abnormalities were attributed to vasculitis and to examine their diagnostic evidence, phenotype, management and outcomes. PubMed, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science were searched from inception to 15 November 2025. Reports were eligible when source authors attributed an imaging or pathological coronary abnormality to vasculitis or arteritis in patients diagnosed with SLE before 18 years. Eligibility did not constitute independent confirmation of vasculitis. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251233120). Eighteen publications described 21 (81% female) patients. Fourteen (67%) were adolescents and coronary involvement occurred within 1 year of SLE onset in 10 (59%)/17. Myocardial infarction was reported in 11 (52%)/21 published cases; 4 of these 11 patients had no chest pain. Active SLE was present in all 15 patients with reported disease-activity status usually with multisystem involvement. Coronary disease was multivessel in 16/20 and comprised dilatation or ectasia, thrombosis, wall thickening, aneurysm and stenosis. Fifteen of 18 patients with reported outcomes improved and three died. Complete clinical and imaging resolution was confined to patients with isolated dilatation or ectasia without myocardial infarction. Antiphospholipid antibody results were incompletely reported. Published cases attributed to coronary vasculitis describe a severe phenotype, but the underlying mechanism is often uncertain. Unexplained coronary abnormalities or myocardial injury in active juvenile SLE should prompt multidisciplinary, mechanism-directed assessment. CRD420251233120.

items.title: Predicting Rheumatoid Arthritis Flares Using Wearable Device Data: Deep Learning Study.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) flares are common and unpredictable. Current monitoring relies on episodic clinical visits and laboratory testing, thereby limiting the ability to anticipate disease worsening. Wearable devices may support continuous remote monitoring, but models must account for missing real-world data, heterogeneous consumer devices, and the distinction between symptomatic disease activity and systemic inflammation. The study aimed to develop and evaluate deep learning (DL) time-series models using wearable-derived physiological data to predict symptomatic and inflammatory RA flares up to 28 days in advance. In a prospective cohort study, adults with RA used a smartwatch (Apple Watch; Apple Inc), a wearable fitness tracker (Fitbit; Google LLC), or a smart ring (Oura Ring; Oura Health Oy). Daily wearable-derived heart rate, heart rate variability, and step-count were harmonized across devices and linked with smartphone-based patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and available C-reactive protein results. Symptomatic flares were defined using longitudinal RAPID3 (Routine Assessment of Patient Index Data 3) scores, and inflammatory flares were defined using a prespecified C-reactive protein threshold. Classical machine learning and DL models were trained to predict daily flare vs remission status at 0-, 7-, 14-, 21-, and 28-day horizons. Model evaluation used a temporally ordered 70/30 within-participant train-test split. Performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROCAUC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), and participant-level sensitivity. This prediction-model analysis was not prospectively registered. Forty-nine participants contributed 5624 days of overlapping wearable and clinical data. Participants used Apple Watch (n=31), Fitbit (n=15), or Oura Ring (n=3). DL models outperformed machine learning models using imputed wearable data, with average ROCAUC improvements of 5.3% for symptomatic flares and 18.4% for inflammatory flares, and AUPRC improvements of 9.3% and 44.1%, respectively. For 7-day-ahead prediction, transformer models incorporating wearable-derived physiology and demographic features achieved ROCAUCs of 0.95 for both symptomatic and inflammatory flares, with AUPRCs of 0.92 and 0.91, respectively. Adding daily PRO improved participant-level sensitivity for inflammatory flare prediction from 0.67 to 0.87. Performance remained stable across prediction horizons for up to 4 weeks. Wearable-derived physiological signals analyzed with DL may support personalized forecasting of symptomatic and inflammatory RA flare states weeks in advance. By integrating passive digital biomarkers with PROs, this approach offers a scalable framework for proactive RA monitoring that could help identify disease exacerbations earlier than episodic clinical assessment alone. Further validation in larger, more diverse cohorts and prospective studies is needed to determine whether wearable-guided forecasting improves clinical decision-making, timely intervention, and long-term outcomes.

items.title: Severe Pulmonary Cryptococcosis With Suspected Immune Reconstitution Inflammatory Syndrome in a Patient With Rheumatoid Arthritis Receiving Tocilizumab.
items.abstract: A man in his 70's with rheumatoid arthritis, receiving methotrexate, prednisolone and tocilizumab, presented with a low-grade fever and cough. Chest computed tomography revealed extensive infiltrative shadows in the left lung, suggesting pneumonia. Bronchoscopy led to the diagnosis of severe pulmonary cryptococcosis (PC). During antifungal treatment, the patient continued to have persistent fever, raising concerns about disease progression or immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS). Findings from a follow-up bronchoscopy, together with the clinical course and response to corticosteroid therapy, supported the clinical suspicion of IRIS. A rare case of severe PC complicated by suspected IRIS is reported.

items.title: Circulating Cytokines Associated with Ocular Involvement and Activity in Behçet's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: To evaluate circulating cytokines associated with ocular involvement and inflammatory activity in Behçet's disease (BD). PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through September 2026. Observational studies evaluating circulating cytokines in peripheral blood in BD with ocular involvement were eligible. Quantitative synthesis was restricted to clinically comparable BD with ocular involvement versus BD without ocular involvement comparisons. Weighted mean differences (WMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using REML random-effects models, with leave-one-out, fixed-effects, and converted-data sensitivity analyses. From 877 database records, 728 were screened after duplicate removal; 142 database reports and 6 citation-search reports were assessed for eligibility, and 24 studies were included. Four cytokines were meta-analyzed. No significant pooled differences were found for IL-8 (WMD 15.09 pg/mL, 95% CI - 53.19 to 83.36; p  = 0.665; I 2  = 74.17%), IL-6 (WMD -5.47, 95% CI - 18.65 to 7.71; p  = 0.416; I 2  = 60.34%), TNF-α (WMD 18.96, 95% CI - 117.47 to 155.38; p  = 0.785; I 2  = 93.42%), or circulating VEGF (WMD 15.22, 95% CI - 56.09 to 86.54; p  = 0.676; I 2  = 81.37%). Heterogeneity remained substantial to considerable. After restricting pooling to clinically comparable ocular-versus-non-ocular BD groups, no circulating cytokine showed a robust and consistently directional association with ocular involvement. Current evidence does not support any single circulating cytokine as a standalone biomarker.

items.title: Iron deficiency anemia in systemic lupus erythematosus: Prevalence and outcomes following iron supplementation.
items.abstract: ObjectivesTo determine the prevalence of iron deficiency anemia (IDA) in Indian systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) patients, evaluate the diagnostic utility of soluble transferrin receptor (sTfR) based assays, and assess the effects of iron supplementation on disease activity, fatigue, and flare rates.MethodsWe conducted a cross sectional analysis of 226 anemic patients from the Indian SLE Inception Cohort for Research (INSPIRE). IDA was defined as ferritin <50 ng/mL, or ferritin 50-100 ng/mL with sTfR >3 µg/mL or sTfR index >1.5. In the longitudinal study, 76 SLE patients with IDA received oral or intravenous iron and were followed for 6 months. Outcomes assessed included changes in hemoglobin, serum ferritin, SLE disease activity index (SLEDAI-2k), fatigue assessed using the Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Fatigue (FACIT-F) score, and disease flare rates.ResultsIDA was identified in 70 patients (30.9%). Only one patient was reclassified by sTfR-based criteria. Serum ferritin showed a moderate positive correlation with disease activity (Spearman's rho = 0.48, p < 0.001). In the longitudinal cohort, 61 patients completed the 6-month follow-up. Iron supplementation was associated with increases in hemoglobin (mean change +1.22 g/dL, 95% CI 0.88 to 1.55, p < 0.001), FACIT-F (mean change +3.57, 95% CI 2.47 to 4.67, p < 0.001), and serum ferritin (Hodges-Lehmann median change +12.4 ng/mL, 95% CI 6.2 to 22.1, p < 0.001). SLEDAI-2k scores showed a modest decrease (Hodges-Lehmann median change 0, 95% CI -1 to 0, p = 0.011). Flare rates remained low (0.098 per person-year), with no increase compared with the preceding year (IRR 0.57, 95% CI 0.16 to 2.12, p = 0.40).ConclusionsNearly one-third of anemic SLE patients have IDA. Iron supplementation was associated with improvements in hematological parameters and fatigue over 6 months. No statistically significant increase in disease activity or flare rates was observed. However, the small number of flares, short follow-up duration, and observational design limit definitive safety conclusions. These findings require confirmation in larger controlled studies.

items.title: Major adverse cardiovascular events in interleukin-6 receptor inhibitors versus tumour necrosis factor inhibitors for rheumatoid arthritis: a national cohort study.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). Evidence comparing the cardiovascular safety of tumour necrosis factor inhibitors (TNFi) and interleukin-6 receptor inhibitors (IL-6Ri) remains limited and heterogeneous, particularly among patients with different baseline cardiovascular risk profiles. Using the large UK national BSRBR-RA cohort, this analysis aimed to compare the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) between patients receiving IL-6Ri and TNFi, i) in all patients with RA, and ii) in people with RA with different pre-existing cardiovascular risks. People with RA starting either TNFi or IL-6Ri between 2009 and 2024 in BSRBR-RA were included. BSRBR-RA is linked to Civil Registration of Death data for cause of death. Cox regression with propensity score stratification was used to estimate hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for MACE in patients receiving IL-6Ri versus TNFi. For the primary analysis, a total of 4,053 IL-6Ri and 11,478 TNFi treatment episodes in a total of 12,175 patients were included. The risk of MACE was not significantly different for those on IL-6Ri versus TNFi (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.81-1.48). When stratified by prior CVD: HR for those without prior CVD 0.99 (95% CI 0.72-1.37); HR for those with previous CVD 1.67 (95% CI 0.82-3.39). The risk of MACE was comparable in people with RA treated with IL-6Ri versus TNFi, while the estimate in patients with prior CVD was imprecise and compatible with a potentially clinically meaningful increase in risk. Additional analyses with longer follow-up are needed to assess cardiovascular risk more precisely in people with RA and established CVD.

items.title: Cardiac Rehabilitation for Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis-Associated Eosinophilic Myocarditis: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a rare systemic necrotizing vasculitis often characterized by asthma, hypereosinophilia, and peripheral neuropathy. This case documents exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation (CR) for EGPA-associated eosinophilic myocarditis (EM). A 61-year-old man suffering from heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) due to EGPA-associated EM was referred for exercise-based CR. Initial level of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) was significantly elevated. He received immunosuppressants and optimized heart failure therapy. The 31-day CR included cycle ergometer training, outdoor walks, gymnastics and strength training at moderate intensities. The 6-min walk performance improved remarkably, EF increased to 50%, and NT-proBNP dropped by over 50% at discharge. This case provides first evidence on feasibility and safety of moderate physical activity for EGPA-associated EM. This case suggests that supervised moderate-intensity physical exercise was feasible and well tolerated in this patient with EGPA-associated EM and was accompanied by favorable changes in relevant disease-specific parameters.

items.title: Immunometabolic reprogramming links circadian cytokine signaling to flare-resolution-remission transitions in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis is characterized by persistent synovial inflammation, recurrent flares, and marked daily variation in symptoms. These features reflect two related but distinct temporal dimensions: circadian regulation, which shapes the daily timing of inflammatory activity, and the flare-resolution-remission cycle, which governs changes in inflammatory burden over longer periods. Studies of human rheumatoid synovium and peripheral blood show that inflammatory stimuli can alter clock components, including brain and muscle ARNT-like 1 and period circadian regulator 2; the reciprocal effects of clock components on inflammation depend on cell type and experimental context. Metabolic abnormalities in T cells, glycolytic reprogramming in macrophages and fibroblast-like synoviocytes, hypoxia-related signaling, and metabolite-dependent chromatin regulation can shape inflammatory responses and tissue states. Histone lactylation and acetylation may participate in transcriptional regulation during active inflammation, but current evidence does not establish these marks as independent carriers of relapse susceptibility over weeks or months. More persistent susceptibility may instead involve chromatin and transcriptional states, durable reprogramming of synovial fibroblasts, tissue-resident memory T cells, and local tissue niches, although their relative contributions remain uncertain. Importantly, a relapse-prone state does not determine when a clinical flare will occur. We distinguish circadian optimization of drug administration from intervention tailored to disease phase. Randomized evidence is strongest for modified-release glucocorticoids, whereas evidence for bedtime methotrexate and nocturnal baricitinib remains limited by study design. Metabolic blockade and pro-resolving interventions remain largely preclinical. This review integrates circadian cytokine regulation, immunometabolic reprogramming, and disease-state transitions to define the evidence and translational limits of time-oriented strategies in rheumatoid arthritis.

items.title: Phosphatidylserine-Enriched Nanoliposomes Containing Prednisolone Phosphate for Experimental Rheumatoid Arthritis: Protective Efficacy and Micro-CT Study of Bone Microarchitecture.
items.abstract: Conventional PEGylated liposomes primarily serve as inert carriers for prednisolone; however, they exhibit low passive loading efficiency for the hydrophilic derivative, necessitating higher administered doses. We hypothesized that phosphatidylserine-containing liposomes (PSLs) could achieve potent anti-arthritic efficacy and joint preservation by enhancing drug loading and reducing the required dose of prednisolone phosphate. Prednisolone-loaded PSLs were prepared. Physicochemical characterization, MTT assay, and macrophage uptake by J774A.1 cells were evaluated. In an adjuvant-induced rheumatoid arthritis (RA) model, early intervention with an optimized formulation followed by two boosters i.v. doses were assessed. Paw edema, systemic inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers, immunohistochemistry (TNF-α, CD3, CD68), and micro-CT imaging were evaluated. The optimized F2 formulation (121.8 nm, -11.5 mV, PdI: 0.095) showed high prednisolone encapsulation efficiency (12.8%), nearly three-fold higher than the conventional form (Nanocort, 4.5%). In vitro cytotoxicity assessment indicated no significant cytotoxic effects and measurable J774A.1 cellular uptake. In the adjuvant-induced RA model, 5 mg/kg F2 resulted in 84.5% inhibition of paw swelling on day 21 compared with the RA group (29.5% vs 190.5%, respectively). Systemic inflammatory markers were significantly reduced: CRP by 64.5% (6.58 vs 18.55 mg/L), RF by 45.5% (24 vs 44 IU/mL), and IgM by 38.3% (12.67 vs 20.53 mg/dL) compared with the RA group. Antioxidant markers, SOD and catalase, were elevated by 63.7% and 44%, respectively, while MDA was reduced by 58.8%. Total histopathological scoring revealed a significant reduction in the 5 mg/kg F2 group compared with the RA model group, from ~12 to 2 (p = 0.0117). Micro-CT revealed the preservation of trabecular structure in the F2-treated group, based on structural parameters including BV/TV (28.98% vs 11.9%), BMD (1703 vs 1234 mg HA/mL), Tb. Th (0.19 vs 0.12 mm), and Tb. Sp (0.4 vs 0.8 mm) over the RA group. Notably, drug-free PSL (Lip-F2) also showed intrinsic anti-inflammatory and bone-sparing effects. Our optimized PSL formulation significantly enhances the passive encapsulation of hydrophilic prednisolone while exhibiting intrinsic anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and bone-protective effects. By enabling a 50% reduction in the dose of prednisolone phosphate, this platform offers a promising strategy to mitigate the systemic side effects of corticosteroid therapy in rheumatoid arthritis.

items.title: Predictive Value of Haematological Inflammatory Indices for Disease Activity and Organ Involvement in Systemic Sclerosis.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a heterogeneous autoimmune disease whose activity and severity remain difficult to assess. Although haematological inflammatory indices such as the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR) have been investigated in several inflammatory conditions, data in SSc remain limited. This study aimed to assess their clinical utility as markers of disease activity and severity. Methods: This cross-sectional correlational study included patients diagnosed with SSc who were evaluated for haematological and inflammatory markers, including SII, PLR, NLR, MLR, platelet distribution width (PDW), plateletcrit (PCT), and C-reactive protein (CRP), in relation to disease phenotype, organ involvement, and disease activity, as assessed by a modified European Scleroderma Trials and Research Activity Index (EUSTAR-AI). Group comparisons were performed using independent-samples t -tests on log-transformed data, with multivariable adjustment for age, sex, disease duration, phenotype and immunosuppressive and glucocorticoid therapy, while Pearson and Spearman correlations, linear regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses (with DeLong comparisons of the areas under the curve, AUC) were used to evaluate associations and discriminative performance; multiplicity was addressed with the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Results: A total of 159 patients with SSc were included. Patients with diffuse cutaneous SSc (dcSSc) exhibited significantly higher SII, NLR, and MLR values than those with limited cutaneous disease. SII and NLR were also significantly elevated in patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) and pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Active disease was associated with higher levels of all major inflammatory indices, while SII and NLR showed significant correlations with pulmonary function parameters, the modified Rodnan Skin Score (mRSS), and the EUSTAR-AI score. In the ROC analysis of SII alone, SII showed moderate discrimination of active disease (AUC = 0.72, 95% CI 0.63-0.80), not significantly different from NLR (0.67) or CRP (0.75). In multivariable regression, SII remained associated with EUSTAR-AI but not with mRSS. After adjustment for age, sex, disease duration, phenotype and treatment, SII remained higher in dcSSc and active disease, whereas the associations with ILD and PAH were no longer significant. Conclusions: SII and NLR were associated with disease activity, the diffuse cutaneous phenotype and, in unadjusted analyses, pulmonary involvement in SSc. SII was independently associated with EUSTAR-AI, but its discriminative ability was moderate and not superior to that of NLR or CRP. These indices may serve as exploratory adjuncts to established activity measures; prospective validation is needed.

items.title: Screening of Potential Therapeutic Targets for Rheumatoid Arthritis and the Intervention Effects of Xixian Pill in Collagen-Induced Arthritis Mice with Divergent Phenotypes.
items.abstract: To screen for core targets associated with B-cell activation in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), compare joint structural damage and immune activation in collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mice with different booster intervals, and characterize the chemical constituents of Xixian Pill. Three Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets (25 controls and 28 RA samples) were integrated for weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, consensus clustering, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and Cell-type Identification By Estimating Relative Subsets Of RNA Transcripts (CIBERSORT). CIA was induced in female Kunming mice, which were randomized into control, model 1 (7-day booster interval), and model 2 (21-day booster interval) groups ( n = 7 per group). Ankle pathology, serum cytokines, oxidative stress markers, and joint immune markers were assessed; joint immune markers were examined by immunohistochemistry. The chemical constituents of Xixian Pill were profiled by ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-Q-Exactive Orbitrap tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS), and molecular docking was performed. Ten candidate feature genes were identified. Six of the seven genes differentially expressed between subtypes correlated significantly with memory B-cell infiltration. IGHM (immunoglobulin heavy constant mu) and CXCL13 (C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 13) were the leading B-cell-related contributors to disease prediction. Model 1 showed stronger systemic inflammation, with elevated malondialdehyde (MDA), interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) levels ( p < 0.01), whereas model 2 exhibited more severe joint damage and the highest IGHM positivity (+132.9% vs. control). Among 37 constituents, 12 and 18 had total docking scores > 5 for IGHM and CXCL13, respectively, and darutoside showed favorable predicted binding to both targets. Conclusions: By integrating GEO-based screening with immunohistochemical localization in CIA joints, this study prioritized IGHM and CXCL13 as B-cell activation-related candidate targets in RA. Comparison of CIA models with different booster intervals indicated that the booster interval may influence the relative profiles of inflammatory activation and histological changes suggestive of structural damage, as well as the expression of these candidate targets. Molecular docking further evaluated the predicted binding of Xixian Pill constituents to these targets and generated testable hypotheses for constituents including darutoside. These findings provide a basis for target prioritization and further investigation of the potential active constituents of Xixian Pill in RA.
