items.title: Interleukin-17A as a Key Mediator and Therapeutic Target in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Current Evidence and Future Directions.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by persistent synovitis, cartilage damage and bone degradation. Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) is a cytokine secreted primarily by T helper 17 (Th17) cells and also by CD8 + T (Tc17) cells, γδ T cells, invariant natural killer T cells, mucosal-associated invariant T cells, and group 3 innate lymphoid cells. IL-17A has been implicated in the etiology of RA, both by the association of immunological activation with synovial inflammation and structural joint damage. IL-17A acts on synovial fibroblasts and a range of immune and stromal cells together with inflammatory cytokines, especially tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), to induce the production of cytokines and chemokines, matrix breakdown and Receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand (RANKL)-dependent osteoclastogenesis in RA. IL-17A has been shown to be involved in synovitis and joint destruction in experimental arthritic models. Despite a strong molecular and preclinical rationale, clinical studies of IL-17-targeting therapies in RA have demonstrated uneven and generally limited efficacy. This discrepancy may reflect the molecular and cellular heterogeneity of RA, redundancy of cytokines, differences in disease progression and tissue environment, and the lack of validated biomarkers for IL17A-dependent disease. This review critically examines the signaling of IL-17A, its pathogenic and structural roles in RA, evidence from experimental arthritis models, and the clinical outcomes and limitations of IL-17-targeted therapies. Emerging approaches, including biomarker-guided patient stratification, single-cell and spatial profiling, multi-omics, broader cytokine targeting, and modulation of immune system and metabolic processes and gutjoint pathways, are also discussed. We also discuss current studies which suggest the future clinical relevance of IL-17A in patients with RA IL-17A is a main and therapeutically targetable inflammatory mechanism.

items.title: Mechanistic Study of Xanthohumol Against Rheumatoid Arthritis via Regulation of p38/MAPK Pathway.
items.abstract: To elucidate the molecular mechanism by which xanthohumol (XN) alleviates rheumatoid arthritis (RA), this study integrated network pharmacology prediction, proteomic screening, and molecular dynamics simulation to systematically evaluate the inhibitory effects and targets of XN in TNF-α-induced fibroblast-like synoviocytes (MH7A cells). XN dose-dependently reversed the pathological proliferation and invasive behavior of MH7A cells and down-regulated pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-1β and IL-6, as well as fibrosis/angiogenesis-related factors including TGF-β1 and VEGF. Cross-validation of network pharmacology and proteomics indicated that these effects were closely associated with the inhibition of the p38/MAPK pathway, modulating inflammatory signal transduction to exert anti-RA effects. Molecular docking revealed that XN bound to the ATP-binding pocket of p38α kinase with an optimal binding energy of -7.623 kcal/mol, forming a stable hydrogen-bond network and hydrophobic stacking with the P-loop, hinge region, and catalytic residue Lys53. Molecular dynamics simulation (100 ns) combined with MM/GBSA analysis (ΔGbind = -104.14 kcal/mol) showed that the complex conformation was highly convergent, with significantly reduced RMSF of key residues in the catalytic domain, suggesting that XN induces rigidification of the kinase catalytic domain by stably occupying the ATP site, thereby blocking its phosphotransfer activity. Collectively, these results demonstrate that XN targets p38α kinase to inhibit the p38/MAPK pathway, intervening in RA pathological progression at multiple levels and providing experimental evidence for its anti-RA molecular mechanism.

items.title: Real-World Outcomes of Targeted Therapies in Psoriatic Arthritis: Effectiveness, Persistence, Safety, Associated Factors, and Residual Unmet Needs.
items.abstract: Targeted therapies have expanded treatment options for psoriatic arthritis (PsA), but clinical response, treatment continuation, and patient-perceived recovery may diverge in routine care. This review synthesized observational reports published between 1 January 2005 and 21 August 2026, distinguishing effectiveness, persistence, safety, outcome-associated factors, and residual burden. The available evidence comprised 64 publications, including 14 BIRRA reports. Synthesis retained outcome-specific definitions, analysis populations, and potential cohort overlap. Clinical and patient-reported improvements frequently coexisted with target nonattainment or persistent symptoms, although residual symptoms could not consistently be attributed to active inflammation. No synthesis met the review's requirement for at least three sufficiently comparable independent cohorts. Two exploratory IL-17 inhibitor analyses estimated 12-month persistence at 74.9% (95% CI 17.8-95.3%) and the female-versus-male discontinuation hazard ratio at 1.89 (95% CI 0.10-37.32). These estimates were too imprecise for clinical prediction or treatment ranking. Safety comparisons were restricted by differences in exposure, ascertainment, and denominators. Associations involving sex, obesity, disease burden, and previous treatment were context dependent. Missing original search and screening records and incomplete risk-of-bias adjudication materially limit reproducibility and confidence. The review's contribution is an integrated interpretation of distinct treatment outcomes rather than a therapeutic hierarchy. Molecular profiling offers complementary research directions but does not establish validated treatment-selection biomarkers within this evidence base.

items.title: Computational Analysis of SLC15A4 Nonsynonymous Variants: Potential Implications for Immune Signaling in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) is a multifactorial autoimmune disease with impaired regulation of innate immune response and interferon signaling. SLC15A4 is an endolysosomal transporter playing a crucial role in Toll-like receptor signaling, and mutations of SLC15A4 coding variants might affect its function and influence disease predisposition. We performed an integrated bioinformatics analysis of SLC15A4 nonsynonymous single nucleotide polymorphisms (nsSNPs) using multiple pathogenicity prediction tools, including SIFT, PolyPhen-2, PROVEAN, META-SNP, ESNPs & GO, and AlphaMissense. Predicted nsSNPs were further evaluated for their effect on protein stability using I-Mutant 2.0, MUpro, and DDMut tools. Next, conservation analysis and 3D protein modeling were performed using ConSurf and AlphaFold-based prediction, with visualization by UCSF ChimeraX. Per-Residue Cα Coordinate Displacement was examined using bio3d methods. Population frequencies and interactions within the functional network were assessed using gnomAD and STRING analyses. From 14,927 SLC15A4 SNPs, four missense variants (rs1955878827, rs182703912, rs375529962, and rs202110778) were found to be deleterious and affecting the protein stability and conformation with increased flexibility in the regions of interest. Rs375529962 was the most deleterious nsSNP with the highest overall pathogenicity and instability of protein structure, followed by rs1955878827 and rs182703912, with rs202110778 being the least deleterious variant. Four pathogenic nsSNPs in the SLC15A4 gene were identified. These mutations may affect the structure and function of SLC15A4 with the potential to impair immune regulation and contribute to the aberrant innate and adaptive immune activation characteristic of SLE.

items.title: Proliferative Lupus Nephritis in Patients with Minimal Urinary Abnormalities: A Narrative Review.
items.abstract: The presence of significant histologic inflammatory activity-e.g., proliferative lupus nephritis, LN-in kidney biopsy from patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and minimal or absent urinary abnormalities is increasingly recognized. Available studies report proliferative lesions in a variable but significant proportion of patients with proteinuria below the 0.5 g/day threshold currently recommended by major guidelines for biopsy indication, raising concerns about delayed diagnosis and treatment. In this narrative review, we summarize the available evidence on kidney biopsy findings in SLE patients with low-grade proteinuria, both at initial diagnostic biopsy and at repeat biopsy. We also report, when available, the association of serological markers (e.g., anti-dsDNA antibodies, complement levels) and histological activity in this population, acknowledging limitations and the absence of clear specific cut-offs. Additionally, we address the risk of biopsy-related complications to provide clinicians with a balanced framework for individualized decision-making in this scenario. The cumulative evidence suggests that current guideline proteinuria thresholds for kidney biopsy may be insufficiently sensitive for exclusion of significant histological activity, though prospective validation is needed.

items.title: The Phenotypic Effect of Somatic NLRP3 Variants Across the Kaleidoscopic Spectrum of Cryopyrin-Associated Periodic Syndrome.
items.abstract: Cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome (CAPS) encompasses a 'continuum' of features caused by gain-of-function variants in NLRP3 , ranging from mild familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome to severe neonatal-onset multisystem inflammatory disease. Although NLRP3 variants are traditionally considered germline alterations, increasing evidence has revealed that post-zygotic somatic variants may account for a substantial proportion of patients with CAPS-like phenotypes, particularly among individuals with late-onset atypical or complex manifestations. Importantly, somatic NLRP3 variants are associated with wide clinical heterogeneity, which cannot be explained solely by variant allele frequency. Timing of the mutational event, proportion and distribution of affected cells, lineage restriction, variant-specific functional effects, and subsequent clonal dynamics may all contribute to protean clinical phenotypes. Somatic mosaicism has been identified across the classical CAPS entities and increasingly in patients presenting with nonclassical or nuanced autoinflammatory sceneries with onset in adulthood. Recent longitudinal studies further suggest that mosaic clones may display distinct patterns of stability or expansion, including myeloid-restricted clonal evolution. In this narrative review, we summarize the current evidence on both molecular and clinical consequences of somatic NLRP3 variants, with particular emphasis to genotype-phenotype relationships (when present), cellular distribution, clonal dynamics, diagnostic challenges, and therapeutic implications. Understanding these mechanisms may refine the classification of NLRP3 -associated diseases and improve management strategies for patients with CAPS displaying complex unexplained or treatment-refractory clinical expression.

items.title: Differential Regulation of BAFF Expression and NET-Associated Responses in Neutrophils from Patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: Neutrophils are increasingly recognized as functionally heterogeneous regulators of inflammation in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), yet whether their major effector responses represent coordinated functions or distinct activation programs remains unclear. In the present study, we examined B-cell activating factor (BAFF) expression, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-associated responses, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, and selected intracellular signaling molecules in density-separated neutrophil and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) fractions from healthy donors and patients with SLE. Type I interferon (IFN-I) preferentially induced BAFF expression, whereas Phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA) markedly induced NET-associated extracellular dsDNA release, indicating different stimulus requirements. Confocal microscopy showed intracellular BAFF accumulation following IFNα stimulation and altered BAFF localization after subsequent PMA stimulation. Pharmacological analyses showed that ROS scavenging attenuated IFNα-induced BAFF mRNA expression, whereas diphenyleneiodonium chloride (DPI) reduced PMA-induced ROS production and extracellular dsDNA release. MEK inhibition reduced ROS production, but its effect on extracellular dsDNA release was not statistically significant. Furthermore, serum BAFF (sBAFF) concentrations, NET-forming capacity, ROS production, and clinical parameters showed no consistent pattern of associations across patients with SLE, although exploratory PAD4-based stratification suggested possible subgroup-specific relationships. Collectively, our findings indicate that BAFF expression and NET-associated responses differ in their stimulus requirements and pharmacological sensitivities. These findings provide a basis for further investigation of functional neutrophil heterogeneity in SLE and highlight the need for single-cell and mechanistic studies to clarify the relationship between BAFF expression and NET-associated responses.

items.title: Nutritional Status in Asymptomatic RF-Positive Individuals, Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis, and Controls.
items.abstract: Background: Rheumatoid factor (RF) positivity can emerge several years before the clinical onset of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). While the nutritional status of patients with established RA has been extensively investigated, little is known about the dietary characteristics of asymptomatic RF-positive individuals. This study aimed to compare the nutritional status of asymptomatic RF-positive individuals with that of patients with RA and controls. Methods: A total of 150 participants were included in this cross-sectional study, consisting of patients with RA ( n = 50), asymptomatic RF-positive individuals ( n = 50), and a control group ( n = 50). For all participants, the researcher collected anthropometric measurements, body composition data, and three-day retrospective dietary records. Daily energy and nutrient intake were analyzed using the Nutrition Information System (BeBiS) and evaluated according to the Türkiye Dietary Guidelines (TÜBER-2022). Groups were compared using ANCOVA, adjusted for age and sex (for anthropometry and percentage of requirements met), as well as for energy intake (for absolute nutrient intake); both unadjusted and sensitivity analyses are presented. The plausibility of the reported energy intake was assessed using the ratio of energy intake to basal metabolic rate (EI:BMR). Hematological indices were considered as secondary, exploratory outcomes. Results: The majority of the participants were women (RF+ positive: 86%, RA: 80%, control: 86%). The age- and sex-adjusted BMI was higher in RF+ positive individuals (30.8 kg/m 2 ) than in RA patients (27.1 kg/m 2 ) ( p = 0.005) but did not differ significantly from controls (28.4 kg/m 2 ; p = 0.151). Reported energy intake was 988 ± 377 kcal for the RF+ positive group, 1117 ± 403 kcal for the RA group, and 1370 ± 316 kcal for the control group (RF+ positive vs. control: p < 0.001; RA vs. control: p = 0.002); these values corresponded to 53%, 65%, and 77% of the energy requirements, respectively, according to the Türkiye Dietary Guidelines (TÜBER). Furthermore, 124 out of 150 participants (82.7%) had an energy intake-to-basal metabolic rate (EI:BMR) ratio of <1.0 (group means: 0.63, 0.75, and 0.93), which suggests potential underreporting. When adjusted for energy, age, and sex, there were no significant differences between the groups regarding the intake of protein, fiber, vitamins C and D, folate, magnesium, and iron. As an exploratory finding, vitamin E intake was lower in the RA group compared to the control group ( p = 0.040); however, this finding did not remain significant after the inclusion of additional covariates and adjustment for multiple comparisons. When the percentages of values meeting dietary requirements were also adjusted for energy intake, most of the differences between the groups disappeared. The neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio ( p = 0.036) and the systemic inflammatory response index ( p = 0.008) were higher in the RA group compared to the RF-positive group. Conclusions: Asymptomatic RF-positive (RF+) individuals had a higher BMI and body fat percentage than patients with RA, although not significantly higher than controls after adjustment for age and sex. Reported energy and nutrient intakes were below the Türkiye Dietary Guidelines (TÜBER) reference values in all groups; the lower intakes in the RF+ and RA groups were largely explained by lower total reported energy intake and may partly reflect under-reporting. While assessing nutritional status is important for patients with established rheumatoid arthritis (RA), evaluating the nutritional status of-and implementing lifestyle interventions for-asymptomatic RF+ individuals may also offer an opportunity to improve their overall health. Furthermore, this group of individuals should be examined in greater detail through prospective longitudinal studies.

items.title: Subtotal Gastrectomy in a Patient with Systemic Sclerosis-Associated Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension and an Implantable Treprostinil Pump: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: We describe the perioperative management of an implanted abdominal treprostinil pump during subtotal gastrectomy for gastric cancer in a patient with systemic sclerosis-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Methods: The patient was a 66-year-old woman with chronic hypoxemia requiring home oxygen. Before surgery, PAH therapy had reduced mean pulmonary artery pressure to 19 mmHg and pulmonary vascular resistance to 2.88 Wood units. The pump was localized preoperatively. Laparoscopic exploration was followed by planned laparotomy through an incision that avoided the pump pocket. An external syringe pump and a written conversion protocol were available for backup intravenous treprostinil delivery. Results: The pump remained in situ, with no documented device complication or clinically apparent interruption of treprostinil delivery. Bosentan and sildenafil were resumed on the evening of surgery. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 7 on her usual home oxygen regimen. Conclusions: Preoperative pump localization and incision planning helped preserve the implanted treprostinil system during subtotal gastrectomy, with a contingency plan for external infusion.

items.title: Somatotype and Its Association with Disease Activity and Psychosocial Factors in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives : Body composition has been suggested to influence disease activity and patient-reported outcomes in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). However, the role of somatotype is not well understood. We aimed to evaluate somatotype characteristics in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and examine their associations with disease activity, function, quality of life, sleep, mood, and fatigue. Methods : In this cross-sectional study, 82 patients with RA (ACR/EULAR criteria) were assessed. Somatotype was determined using the Heath-Carter method and categorized as endomorphic, mesomorphic, or ectomorphic. Disease activity (DAS28), functional status (HAQ), quality of life (SF-12), sleep quality (PSQI), mood (HADS), and fatigue (FSS) were evaluated. Group comparisons, correlation analyses, and BMI-adjusted regression models were performed. Results : Mesomorphic (54.9%) and endomorphic (37.8%) somatotypes predominated, while ectomorphy was uncommon (7.3%). Somatotype groups differed significantly in anthropometric parameters ( p < 0.05) whereas no statistically significant group difference were detected in DAS28, HAQ, SF-12, PSQI, HADS, or FSS scores (all p > 0.05). Correlations between somatotype components and clinical measures were weak and none remained significant after adjustment for BMI. Conclusions : Somatotype reflects body habitus in RA. However, no statistically significant associations with disease activity or patient-reported outcomes were identified after adjustment for the measured covariates in this cohort. Given the modest sample size, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and do not exclude potentially clinically relevant relationships.

items.title: Treatment Adherence and Associated Factors in Adults with Familial Mediterranean Fever: A Cross-Sectional Study in Türkiye.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives : Long-term adherence to colchicine therapy is essential for effective management of familial Mediterranean fever (FMF). This study aimed to assess colchicine adherence and examine associated sociodemographic and clinical factors among adults with FMF in Türkiye. Methods : This descriptive, cross-sectional, and correlational study was conducted online between May and September 2025 and reported in accordance with the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) guidelines. A total of 312 adults with FMF who had received colchicine treatment for at least one year were recruited across Türkiye using non-probability convenience sampling through the social media accounts of a patient association. Data were collected using a Participant Information Form and the adult version of the Medication Adherence Scale in FMF Patients (MASIF). Descriptive statistics and exploratory group comparisons were performed. Results : The mean MASIF total score was 63.38 ± 7.77, and 67.3% of participants were classified as having good medication adherence, whereas 32.7% demonstrated poor adherence. MASIF total scores differed significantly according to age, marital status, duration of FMF, duration of colchicine use, living arrangements, and regular follow-up attendance. Conclusions : Approximately one-third of participants demonstrated poor adherence to colchicine treatment, highlighting the importance of routine adherence assessment, individualized patient education, and continuity of follow-up care. Further longitudinal and multicenter studies are needed to clarify factors associated with colchicine adherence and inform targeted nursing interventions.

items.title: Systemic Sclerosis Presenting With Anasarca and Generalized Edema in the Absence of Typical Serological Markers: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a chronic autoimmune connective tissue disease characterized by vasculopathy, immune dysregulation, and fibrosis. While early manifestations typically include Raynaud phenomenon and skin thickening, atypical presentations may occur and delay diagnosis, particularly in seronegative cases. A 44-year-old man presented with progressive generalized edema (anasarca), polyarthralgia, and myalgia over eight months following a viral upper respiratory tract infection. Initial evaluations suggested endocrine and cardiac etiologies, but were unremarkable. Laboratory testing revealed mild inflammatory markers and transient hypoalbuminemia. Extensive autoimmune workup was largely negative. Imaging demonstrated diffuse subcutaneous edema without visceral involvement. Skin biopsy showed dermal fibrosis suggestive of a sclerosing process. Over time, the patient developed sclerodactyly, and the longitudinal clinical evolution together with supportive skin histopathology favored a clinical diagnosis of systemic sclerosis despite negative conventional serology. Treatment with prednisone, mycophenolate mofetil, and methotrexate resulted in resolution of symptoms and normalization of inflammatory markers. This case highlights an unusual presentation of systemic sclerosis with anasarca in the absence of typical clinical and serologic features. Systemic sclerosis should be considered in the differential diagnosis of unexplained generalized edema after exclusion of common causes. Early dermatologic evaluation and skin biopsy may be critical for timely diagnosis and management.

items.title: Vanillic Acid Mitigates Experimental Rheumatoid Arthritis Through Modulation of Inflammation, Immune Responses, and Oxidative Stress.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic inflammatory disorder associated with joint inflammation, progressive tissue damage, and oxidative stress. Vanillic acid, a phenolic compound with reported anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, may have potential in mitigating these pathological changes. This study aimed to evaluate the anti-arthritic and anti-inflammatory potential of vanillic acid in a Freund's complete adjuvant (FCA)-induced arthritic Sprague Dawley albino rat model. Arthritis was induced on day 0 in all rats except the normal control group, and treatment was initiated on the same day following FCA administration. All treatments were administered for 21 consecutive days. Arthritic progression, paw volume, and paw thickness were assessed on Days 5, 9, 13, 17, and 21 using arthritic scoring, a water-displacement plethysmometer, and a digital Vernier caliper, respectively. Histopathological examination of ankle joints was performed using the hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining method. Serum superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, malondialdehyde (MDA), and reduced glutathione (GSH) levels were assessed using spectrophotometric methods to evaluate oxidative stress and antioxidant status. Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) was used to evaluate the expression of interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), and hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α), while hematological parameters were also assessed. Vanillic acid significantly reduced arthritic scores, paw thickness, and paw volume, particularly during the later stages of treatment (all treatment groups, p < 0.001 on Day 21 compared with the arthritic control group). Histopathological examination showed marked inflammatory changes in the arthritic control group, whereas relatively preserved joint architecture was observed in the HDVA group, with comparatively fewer apparent pathological changes in the vanillic acid-treated groups. The arthritic control group showed increased expression of TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, and HIF-1α, whereas vanillic acid treatment significantly attenuated their expression (TNF-α: p < 0.001 at all doses; IL-1β: p < 0.01 at 200 and 400 mg/kg; IL-6: p < 0.05 at 100 mg/kg and p < 0.001 at 200 and 400 mg/kg; HIF-1α: p < 0.05 at 100 mg/kg and p < 0.01 at 200 and 400 mg/kg). Vanillic acid also increased SOD activity and GSH levels while reducing MDA concentrations compared with the arthritic control group (SOD, GSH, and MDA: p < 0.01 at 100 mg/kg and p < 0.001 at 200 and 400 mg/kg). In the present study, vanillic acid demonstrated anti-arthritic and immunomodulatory potential in the FCA-induced rat model of arthritis, associated with attenuation of inflammatory mediators and improvement in measured antioxidant parameters. These findings are limited to this experimental animal model and should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical efficacy in human rheumatoid arthritis.

items.title: Baicalin Alleviates Rheumatoid Arthritis by Suppressing Crosstalk Between RA-FLSs and Synovial Macrophages via the CCL2-CCR2-MAPK/NF-κB Signaling Network.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune inflammatory disorder driven by abnormal interactions between fibroblast-like synoviocytes (RA-FLSs) and synovial macrophages, leading to sustained synovitis. Although transcriptomic evidence reveals that baicalin mainly regulates the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and NF-κB pathways, its role in mediating crosstalk between RA-FLSs and synovial macrophages remains poorly defined. This study aimed to elucidate whether the therapeutic effect of baicalin against collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) is associated with disruption of the crosstalk between RA-FLSs and synovial macrophages via the CCL2-CCR2-MAPK/NF-κB signaling network. In vivo treatment confirmed that baicalin inhibited the signaling cascade and promoted macrophage M2 polarization. CCR2-knockdown (CCR2 KD ) and -overexpressing (CCR2 OE ) macrophage cell lines were constructed using lentivirus. Experiments with CCR2 KD /CCR2 OE macrophages and an RA-FLS co-culture system showed that baicalin downregulated CCL2's release from RA-FLSs, blocking macrophage migration. Both M1 macrophages and RA-FLSs pretreated with baicalin were capable of suppressing proinflammatory cytokine secretion from their respective interacting partners through this signaling axis, showing that baicalin suppressed excessive inflammatory cytokine secretion by disrupting RA-FLS-synovial macrophage crosstalk via a CCL2-CCR2-MAPK/NF-κB signaling network, which may represent the principal mechanism underlying the baicalin-mediated amelioration of RA. These findings offer new insights into baicalin's anti-arthritic mechanism.

items.title: Translational Study on the Effects of Janus Kinase Inhibitors on Interstitial Lung Disease Complicated with Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease (RA-ILD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with rheumatoid arthritis. This study evaluated the 1-year retention rates of Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors in patients with RA-ILD and investigated their effects in experimental pulmonary fibrosis and human lung fibroblasts. One-year retention rates were assessed in patients with RA-ILD treated with baricitinib (BAR), peficitinib (PEF), filgotinib (FIL), upadacitinib, or tofacitinib. Pulmonary fibrosis was induced by bleomycin (BLM) in C57BL/6J mice, followed by treatment with BAR, PEF, or FIL. Survival, body weight, computed tomography findings, and histopathology were evaluated. Normal human lung fibroblasts (NHLFs) were stimulated with the interleukin (IL)-6/IL-6 receptor and treated with each JAK inhibitor. STAT1, STAT3, and STAT5 phosphorylation and the production of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), transforming growth factor-β1, and fractalkine were assessed. JAK inhibitor 1-year retention rates did not differ significantly between patients with and without RA-ILD. In the BLM model, BAR attenuated pulmonary inflammation, preserved body weight, and improved survival compared with PEF and FIL. In NHLFs, BAR most effectively suppressed IL-6-induced STAT3 phosphorylation and VEGF production. These findings suggest that BAR may exert protective effects in experimental pulmonary fibrosis through suppression of the IL-6/STAT3/VEGF axis.

items.title: Urinary Biomarkers of Renal Involvement in Antineutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibody (ANCA)-Associated Vasculitis: Diagnosis, Disease Activity and Relapse Prediction.
items.abstract: Kidney involvement largely determines prognosis in antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV), yet serum creatinine, proteinuria and haematuria cannot reliably separate active vasculitis from chronic damage or flare mimics, and kidney biopsy is invasive and rarely repeated. Unlike recent systematic reviews, which assessed a few soluble serum and urinary markers of overall disease activity, this structured narrative review covers the full range of urinary markers of renal involvement, organises them by clinical question and grades the evidence for each. A PubMed search identified 77 clinical studies. Urinary soluble CD163 is the most extensively validated marker; an accredited assay identified renal flare with an area under the curve of 0.95 in a prospective multicentre cohort. Urinary CD4+ T cells discriminate active glomerulonephritis and, in one prospective study, predicted six-month renal relapse with high specificity but modest sensitivity. Persistent haematuria after induction is the most consistently replicated predictor of renal relapse, whereas persistent proteinuria or albuminuria mainly predicts kidney failure. Urinary MCP-1 supports within-patient monitoring, and complement fragments and markers of tubular injury and fibrosis mainly add prognostic information. No urinary marker is yet ready for routine use, and the validation needed is outlined.

items.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Using Quantitative Computed Tomography Supports the Detection of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives : Systemic lupus erythematosus-associated interstitial lung disease (SLE-ILD) is linked to increased disease burden and adverse outcomes, underscoring the need for its reliable detection. This study explored the use of quantitative computed tomography (CT) to assess pulmonary involvement in SLE-ILD and developed an interpretable machine learning model to identify the disease. Methods : This retrospective analysis included 312 patients with SLE: 135 with ILD and 177 without. It compared quantitative CT parameters, including lung volume (LV), mean lung density (MLD), and the percentage of intrapulmonary vascular volume (PIVV), between the groups. Patients from 2017 to 2022 ( n = 219) formed the training set, whereas those from 2023 to 2025 ( n = 93) formed the temporal test set. Following feature selection using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) in the entire training set, eight machine learning models were developed, with hyperparameters optimized using a separate 10-fold cross-validation procedure. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were assessed through receiver operating characteristic (ROC) and precision-recall curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. The final model's feature contributions to predictions were analyzed using SHapley Additive exPlanations. Results : Compared with the non-ILD group, the ILD group generally showed higher MLD, lower LV, and lower PIVV. LASSO identified nine variables. After considering the performance of all models in both the training and temporal test sets, logistic regression (LR) was selected as the final model. In the temporal test set, the LR model achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.926 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.875-0.977] and an average precision of 0.92 (95% CI, 0.86-0.97). Its accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1 score were 0.871, 0.825, 0.906, 0.868, and 0.846, respectively. This model was implemented as a web-based diagnostic calculator. Conclusions : Quantitative CT enables objective quantification of pulmonary abnormalities in patients with SLE-ILD. An interpretable LR model integrating clinical and quantitative CT features may support the objective identification of SLE-ILD, although its performance requires further validation in independent cohorts.

items.title: Cell-type-divergent redox injury in rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus/lupus nephritis: evidence for ferroptosis-related remodeling and immune amplification.
items.abstract: Persistent immune activation alone does not adequately explain the relationship between chronic inflammation, structural damage, and incomplete tissue recovery in rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus/lupus nephritis. This review uses a cell-type-divergent redox-injury framework to organize how redox imbalance is translated into distinct cellular outcomes. The framework links disruption of SLC7A11-GSH-GPX4 antioxidant defenses to lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative modification of self-molecules, damage-associated molecular pattern release, and neutrophil extracellular trap-immune complex-type I interferon amplification. Its central premise is that similar inflammatory redox pressure may promote the loss or dysfunction of tissue-supporting or inflammation-resolving cells, permit pathogenic proliferative cells to persist through reinforced anti-ferroptotic defenses, and sustain post-injury immune amplification. Rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus/lupus nephritis provide the most developed disease-specific evidence and therefore form the primary focus of this review, whereas evidence in other rheumatic diseases remains heterogeneous and is often indirect, transcriptomic, or model-dependent. Even within RA and SLE/LN, however, the maturity of cell-specific mechanistic evidence is uneven: the macrophage HMGB1-TLR4-STAT3 amplification circuit has been demonstrated in a single mechanistic RA study, whereas individual upstream regulators of podocyte ferroptosis-like injury in LN remain incompletely replicated and predominantly supported by preclinical evidence. Within this framework, oxidative stress, ferroptosis, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, and pyroptosis should not be regarded as interchangeable processes. The framework supports a cell-directed therapeutic logic centered on protecting vulnerable structural cells and selected inflammation-resolving immune-cell states, selectively restoring ferroptotic susceptibility in pathogenic proliferative cells, and interrupting downstream inflammatory amplification while avoiding indiscriminate antioxidant or tissue-wide ferroptosis modulation.

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of cell-bound complement activation product assays for systemic lupus erythematosus: a systematic review and marker-stratified bivariate meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Cell-bound complement activation products (CB-CAPs) are potential diagnostic markers for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Existing studies adopted inconsistent cell types, cutoffs, algorithms, and control groups. This review analyzed distinct CB-CAP markers separately without uniform treatment of different CB-CAP tests. Embase and Web of Science were searched from inception to August 18, 2026, and PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from inception to September 27, 2026. Eligible studies evaluated a blood-cell-bound complement marker or CB-CAP-based algorithm in SLE and non-SLE controls and provided threshold-specific sensitivity and specificity or reconstructable 2 × 2 data. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and performed QUADAS-2 assessment, with disagreements adjudicated by a third reviewer. The primary analysis comprised adult B-cell-bound C4d (BC4d) versus clinical disease controls with one record per independent cohort. A Reitsma-type bivariate random-effects model jointly synthesized logit sensitivity and specificity; post hoc separate univariate random-effects and leave-one-out analyses examined the robustness of the findings to the small number of studies. A total of 10 eligible reports were retained: nine primary diagnostic studies and one 2026 multicohort aggregate report that re-used participants enrolled during 2011-2025 and was therefore not treated as an independent observation. Four adult BC4d studies contributed 611 SLE cases and 602 clinical controls to the primary model. Summary sensitivity was 47.7% (95% confidence interval [CI], 32.7%-63.1%), and specificity was 91.3% (95% CI, 82.6%-95.9%). The approximate positive and negative likelihood ratios were 5.50 and 0.57, respectively. Prediction intervals were wide (sensitivity, 19.0%-78.0%; specificity, 68.7%-98.1%). Separate univariate random-effects estimates were similar (sensitivity, 47.9%; specificity, 91.6%), while leave-one-out estimates ranged from 41.7% to 53.6% for sensitivity and from 85.1% to 94.5% for specificity. All 10 reports had high risk of bias in patient selection; seven had high risk and one had unclear risk in the index-test domain. BC4d exhibits higher specificity than sensitivity for SLE diagnosis. A positive BC4d result raises SLE probability but requires combined assessment of pretest probability and clinical evidence and cannot independently confirm or exclude uncertain SLE cases. Evidence for other CB-CAP markers and combined tests remains limited, requiring further external validation in consecutive patient cohorts.

items.title: Combining a massively parallel reporter assay and human data to elucidate genetic mechanisms driving risk for juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
items.abstract: While progress has been made in identifying the true risk-driving single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPS) on juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) risk haplotypes, the affected cells and target genes largely remain unknown. We used data from a previously published massively parallel reporter assay (MPRA) to query human data in the Database of Immune Cell eQTLs (DICE) and the Gene-Tissue Expression (GTEx) database to identify affected cells and target genes of MPRA-identified SNPs in immune cells and relevant tissues. SNPs identified on MPRA were associated with gene expression levels in a broad range of immune cells in the DICE database, including CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes, monocytes, NK cells, and B cells. MPRA-identified SNPs showed strong associations with gene expression in GTEx whole blood, spleen, and/or EBV-transformed lymphocytes. Our data show the efficacy of combining MPRA and using human cells/tissue expression data to elucidate complex mechanisms driving genetic risk for JIA.

items.title: Arginine vasopressin deficiency in primary Sjögren's syndrome: a case report and literature review.
items.abstract: Arginine vasopressin deficiency (AVP-D) is rarely been reported in primary Sjögren's syndrome (pSS) and may be overlooked because excessive fluid intake can be attributed to xerostomia. A 45-year-old woman presented with xerostomia, polydipsia, polyuria, and nocturia, with a 24-h urine output of 4.4 L. Serum sodium reached 158 mmol/L, with marked plasma-urine osmotic dissociation (plasma osmolality 318, urine osmolality 115 mOsm/kg H 2 O). pSS was diagnosed on the basis of anti-SSA positivity, objective exocrine-gland dysfunction, and focal lymphocytic infiltration on labial salivary gland biopsy with one focus containing more than 50 lymphocytes per 4 mm 2 of glandular tissue (focus score: 1 focus/4 mm 2 ). During supervised water deprivation, serum sodium rose from 148.4 to 154.3 mmol/L, prompting termination at 6 hours in the setting of intolerable thirst and discomfort. Urine osmolality was 292 mOsm/kg H 2 O despite plasma osmolality of 326 mOsm/kg H 2 O; after posterior pituitary injection (5 U), it increased to 441 mOsm/kg H 2 O (+51.0%). These findings supported the diagnosis of AVP-D. Unenhanced MRI showed a partial empty sella with pituitary flattening, without stalk thickening or a sellar/suprasellar mass; the posterior-pituitary bright spot could not be reliably assessed because of anatomical distortion. Desmopressin promptly relieved thirst and polyuria. Given suspected autoimmune hypothalamic-neurohypophyseal involvement, glucocorticoids and mycophenolate mofetil were added. At approximately 1 year, serum sodium was normal and urine output was approximately 2.0 L/day, with desmopressin continued. This case highlights the occurrence of AVP-D in association with pSS, with possible autoimmune hypothalamic-neurohypophyseal involvement. Although the underlying mechanism remains uncertain, disproportionate polyuria and nocturia in patients with pSS, particularly in the presence of hypernatremia, should prompt evaluation for AVP-D rather than being attributed solely to sicca symptoms.

items.title: Clinical effectiveness of Biqi capsule combined with methotrexate in rheumatoid arthritis: an integrated retrospective, meta-analytic, and machine learning study.
items.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) monotherapy provides inadequate disease control in many patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Biqi Capsule (BQC), a proprietary traditional Chinese medicine formulation, is used as an adjunct to MTX, but its clinical benefits remain uncertain. We evaluated Biqi Capsule plus MTX by integrating a retrospective cohort study, exploratory machine-learning analysis, and a systematic review and meta-analysis. The cohort comprised 100 patients who received either MTX monotherapy (n = 50) or Biqi Capsule plus MTX (n = 50). After adjustment for the corresponding baseline values, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody (anti-CCP) levels at week 24 were lower in the combination-therapy group than in the MTX monotherapy group ( P = 0.002), whereas other inflammatory markers and liver and kidney function indices showed no significant between-group differences. Among patients receiving combination therapy, 24 (48.0%) met the prespecified serological response criterion, defined as a ≥25% reduction in anti-CCP levels from baseline. Among the eight algorithms evaluated, the bagged trees model achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC, 0.601; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.445 to 0.752), with blood urea nitrogen (BUN), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-reactive protein (CRP) exhibiting the greatest permutation importance. This meta-analysis included nine studies involving 952 participants. Compared with the controls, BQC-based regimens were associated with significantly lower rheumatoid factor (RF), ESR, and CRP levels, shorter duration of morning stiffness, lower tender and swollen joint counts, and higher overall clinical response rates. The pooled analysis showed no significant between-group difference in the odds of adverse events. Subgroup analyses by treatment regimen showed significant pooled effects favoring BQC plus MTX over the controls for RF, ESR, CRP, morning stiffness duration, swollen joint count, and overall clinical response. Relative to their respective controls, the BQC plus MTX subgroup showed greater pooled reductions in RF and ESR than the BQC monotherapy subgroup, with significant between-subgroup differences. Overall, Biqi Capsule may offer additional benefits alongside MTX. However, residual confounding, modest model discrimination, and between-study heterogeneity limit firm conclusions. Larger prospective multicenter studies and independent external validation are warranted to confirm these findings.

items.title: Preventive Supplementation with Taif Black Mulberry ( Morus nigra ) Attenuates Systemic Inflammation, Hepatic Oxidative Stress and Liver Alterations in Rats with Collagen-Induced Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis involves systemic inflammation, immune dysregulation, and oxidative stress, which may contribute to hepatic injury. This study investigated the effects of preventive oral supplementation with Taif black mulberry ( Morus nigra ) fruit powder on systemic inflammatory, serological, oxidative, and hepatic alterations in rats immunized with type II collagen (collagen-induced arthritis, CIA, model). Thirty-two male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to four groups ( n = 8 per group): healthy controls, untreated collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) controls, and two CIA groups receiving freeze-dried Morus nigra fruit powder at doses of 100 and 200 mg/kg/day, respectively. Treatment was initiated on the day of the first immunization (day 0) and continued for eight weeks as part of a preventive experimental design. Immunization was induced with bovine type II collagen emulsified in incomplete Freund's adjuvant. Serum cytokines, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibodies, and liver enzymes were assessed. Hepatic malondialdehyde and antioxidant enzyme activities were measured, and liver histopathology was examined using hematoxylin and eosin and Masson's trichrome staining. Compared with the healthy controls, the CIA model rats showed higher TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-17, anti-CCP, lower IL-10, increased hepatic MDA and serum ALT, AST, and ALP, reduced hepatic superoxide dismutase, catalase, and glutathione peroxidase (GPx) activities, and hepatic histological alterations. Both doses of Morus nigra lowered TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-17, anti-CCp, ALT, and ALP and increased antioxidant enzyme activities relative to the untreated CIA rats, whereas significant reductions in hepatic MDA and serum AST were observed only with a higher dose. The higher dose also lowered IL-2, whereas neither dose restored IL-10. Anti-CCP and GPx responses were greater at 200 mg/kg/day than at 100 mg/kg/day. Preventive Morus nigra supplementation attenuated systemic inflammatory, autoimmune, oxidative, and hepatic alterations in the CIA rats. These preclinical findings support the protective effect on systemic and hepatic outcomes. However, further mechanistic investigations and clinical studies are required to establish its efficacy and underlying mechanisms of action.

items.title: Intestinal Behçet's Disease Presenting as Recurrent Gastrointestinal Perforation: A Diagnostic Pitfall Mimicking Crohn's Disease.
items.abstract: A 24-year-old man underwent four emergency surgeries for gastrointestinal perforation over a six-year period. Surgical pathology repeatedly suggested transmural inflammation with fissuring ulcers, favoring Crohn's disease. However, the acute onset of each episode and the lack of typical Crohn's disease-related chronic inflammatory symptoms between episodes were incompatible with the chronic course of Crohn's disease. The histopathological finding of a tunnel-like ulcer, together with recurrent oral ulcers and acneiform folliculitis, led to a diagnosis of intestinal Behçet's disease after multidisciplinary review. This case illustrates that when pathological morphology and clinical rhythm conflict, a comprehensive evaluation integrating the clinical history, extraintestinal manifestations, and histopathological findings is essential.

items.title: Pharmacological Effects of Bidirectional Solid-State Fermentation Product of Irpex lacteus and Panax notoginseng on Mice with Lupus Nephritis.
items.abstract: Objectives : Lupus nephritis (LN) is a severe complication of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and remains a critical challenge in clinical treatment. This study aimed to investigate the early-intervention effects and underlying mechanisms of Panax notoginseng fermented by Irpex lacteus (FS) in MRL/lpr mice with LN, to provide a theoretical basis for the medicinal development of FS and clinical intervention for LN. Methods : MRL/lpr mice were administered low-dose and high-dose FS for 8 consecutive weeks. Therapeutic efficacy of FS was systematically evaluated by detecting renal function indicators, autoantibody levels, and inflammatory factor expression. Meanwhile, Western blot (WB) was performed to detect the expression of key proteins in the renal PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling pathway, and 16S rRNA sequencing was used to analyze structural changes in intestinal microbiota. Results : Pharmacodynamic results revealed that, compared with the model group and raw Panax notoginseng group, high-dose FS significantly improved renal function in LN mice, reduced the levels of urine protein, creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, autoantibodies and inflammatory factors ( p < 0.05). Observations from representative histological specimens suggested amelioration of renal pathological manifestations including glomerular proliferation, inflammatory infiltration and renal fibrosis. Mechanistic analyses revealed associations between FS treatment and reduced phosphorylation of proteins within the renal PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling pathway ( p < 0.05), as well as partial shifts in gut-microbiota composition suggestive of improved intestinal microecology. Conclusions : FS exerts anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory and renal-protective effects. Our observations suggest associations between FS treatment, altered PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway activity and shifts in gut-microbiota composition related to the gut-kidney axis. This study provides important theoretical and experimental evidence for the medicinal development of FS and targeted early-intervention strategies for lupus nephritis.

items.title: Integrative Identification of Comorbid Genes Linking ANCA-Associated Vasculitis and Bladder Cancer Using Single-Cell Transcriptomics and Mendelian Randomisation.
items.abstract: Background: Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV) is an immune-mediated inflammatory disorder, and bladder cancer is a common urologic malignancy. Epidemiological evidence shows AAV patients have a markedly higher risk of bladder cancer (OR = 3.84; 95% CI: 2.72-5.42). However, the shared genetic basis of this comorbidity remains unclear. Here, we integrate single-cell transcriptomics and Mendelian randomisation to explore its molecular architecture. Methods: Single-cell RNA-seq data for ANCA-associated glomerulonephritis (GSE303481) and bladder cancer (GSE222315) were obtained from the GEO. We identified overlapping monocyte DEGs after Seurat preprocessing. Mendelian randomisation was conducted using five complementary methods (IVW, MR-Egger, weighted median, and simple and weighted mode) with comprehensive sensitivity tests. Further analyses covered functional enrichment, gene networks, miRNA prediction, and pseudotime trajectories. Results: After stringent quality control, 138,457 and 96,017 cells were retained in the AAV and bladder cancer datasets, respectively. Monocytes displayed the most pronounced transcriptional alterations, yielding 3288 overlapping candidate genes. MR analysis identified 94 genes with putative causal effects on AAV and 80 on bladder cancer, and intersection analysis identified SP1 and GET4 as shared candidate genes, with SP1 showing a protective association and GET4 a risk association for both diseases. Both genes participated in transcriptional regulatory programmes and exhibited extensive miRNA-mediated regulatory interactions. Pseudotime analysis further revealed disease-specific dynamic expression trajectories of both genes during monocyte differentiation in both disease contexts. Conclusions: SP1 and GET4 may represent genetically supported shared susceptibility factors whose dysregulation may contribute to AAV-bladder cancer comorbidity. Our findings provide insights into a monocyte-centric transcriptional programme characterised by disease-specific regulatory dynamics and immunoinflammatory crosstalk that may underlie the pathophysiological basis of AAV-bladder cancer comorbidity. Further experimental and independent studies are warranted to validate these findings.

items.title: Objective-to-Subjective Sleep Discrepancy in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Pilot EEG Study.
items.abstract: Background and Objectives : Sleep disturbance is common in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but the relationship between subjectively perceived and objectively measured sleep duration remains poorly understood. This pilot study aimed to compare objective and subjective total sleep time (TST) and to explore clinical factors associated with each measure and the difference between them. It also examined the relationship between this difference and nocturnal blood pressure regulation. Materials and Methods : Twenty-two hospitalized patients with RA underwent overnight sleep monitoring using a portable single-channel electroencephalography (EEG) device and provided subjective estimates of TST for the same night in response to a question asked the following morning. Sleep discrepancy was defined as subjective minus EEG-derived TST. Associations with clinical variables were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation analysis with false discovery rate correction. Exploratory regression analyses adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index were performed. Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring was available for 20 patients. Results : Subjective TST exceeded EEG-derived TST by a median of 82.75 min ( p = 0.0008), and the two measurements were not significantly correlated (ρ = 0.119, p = 0.598). A more positive signed sleep discrepancy was associated with lower serum albumin (ρ = -0.723, q = 0.0020), higher C-reactive protein (CRP) levels (ρ = 0.624, q = 0.0134), glucocorticoid use ( q = 0.0462), higher DAS28-CRP ( q = 0.0495), and greater functional disability ( q = 0.0495). Associations with albumin and CRP persisted in separate exploratory models adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index. Patients with a conventional dipper blood pressure (BP) pattern had a lower signed sleep discrepancy than those with other nocturnal BP patterns ( p = 0.0087). Conclusions : In this small exploratory study, subjective sleep duration in patients with RA was generally longer than EEG-derived sleep duration. Furthermore, preliminary associations were observed between sleep discrepancy and inflammatory and clinical characteristics, as well as with nocturnal BP patterns. These findings require confirmation in larger studies, and the clinical significance of sleep discrepancy remains uncertain.

items.title: Screening for Primary Sjögren's Disease in Patients with Burning Mouth Syndrome: Clinical, Serologic, and Sialometric Findings.
items.abstract: Background and Objectives : Oral burning is the primary complaint in burning mouth syndrome (BMS), but it can also be an early manifestation of primary Sjögren's disease (pSD). Because BMS is a diagnosis of exclusion, unrecognized pSD may remain undiagnosed and be treated only symptomatically. This study aimed to screen patients with BMS for pSD and to identify clinical, serologic, and sialometric findings that could guide targeted referrals. Materials and Methods : This cross-sectional study included 85 adults with chronic oral burning who met the International Classification of Orofacial Pain (ICOP) criteria for BMS after local and systemic causes were excluded. Patients were evaluated at the Department of Dental Medicine, University Hospital of Split, Croatia. The 2016 American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism (ACR/EULAR) criteria were used to identify pSD. Burning intensity (visual analogue scale, VAS), unstimulated (Qs) and stimulated (Qss) whole salivary flow rates, and hematologic, biochemical, and autoantibody findings were compared between patients with pSD and those with BMS alone. Results : pSD was identified in 5 patients (5.9%; 95% CI, 1.9-13.2%), all women older than 60 years. Patients with pSD were older than those with BMS alone ( p = 0.049). Burning intensity did not differ between groups ( p = 0.575). Both Qs (median: 0.00 vs. 0.20 mL/min, p = 0.005) and Qss (median: 0.20 vs. 0.50 mL/min, p = 0.025) were significantly lower in patients with pSD. Four of the five patients with pSD were anti-SSA negative, and routine blood parameters showed no significant differences. Borderline or positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA) were detected in 17.5% ( n = 14) of patients with BMS and 40.0% ( n = 2) of those with pSD ( p = 0.025). Conclusions : Previously unrecognized pSD was identified in approximately 6% of patients with BMS. Sialometry was a more informative screening tool than burning intensity or routine laboratory tests. Assessment of whole salivary flow may help identify patients with oral burning who warrant rheumatologic evaluation before a diagnosis of BMS is confirmed.

items.title: Anti-signal recognition particle (anti-SRP) antibodies in idiopathic inflammatory myopathy: A descriptive multicenter cross-sectional study from the Myositis Study Group of the Argentine Society of Rheumatology.
items.abstract: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM) are a heterogeneous group of autoimmune diseases. Anti-signal recognition particle (anti-SRP) antibodies are present in approximately 5% of IIM and define a phenotype with severe proximal weakness and a rapidly progressive course. Data on Latin American cohorts are scarce. Descriptive, multicenter, cross-sectional study. Patients with anti-SRP-positive IIM fulfilling the 2017 EULAR/ACR criteria were included from the registry of the Myositis Study Group of the Argentine Society of Rheumatology (GESAR). Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and treatment data were collected. Continuous variables are reported as median and interquartile range (IQR); categorical variables as frequencies and percentages. Of 363 patients with IIM, 17 (4.7%) were anti-SRP positive; 88.2% were women, median age 56 years (IQR 49-69), median diagnostic delay 6 months (IQR 1-18). Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy was the most frequent classification (64.7%). Muscle weakness was documented in 56.3%, dysphagia in 50.0%, articular involvement in 25.0%, respiratory muscle weakness in 17.6%, and interstitial lung disease in 12.5% (all non-specific interstitial pneumonia). No cardiac involvement was reported. Creatine kinase was elevated in 66.7% of patients with available measurements; no additional myositis-specific autoantibodies were detected. Treatments included glucocorticoids (88.2%), methotrexate (47.1%), azathioprine (35.3%), rituximab (29.4%), and intravenous immunoglobulin (23.5%). Hospitalization due to myositis was required in 52.9%. In this Argentine multicenter cohort, anti-SRP-positive IIM was characterized by severe proximal weakness, frequent dysphagia, and a high hospitalization rate. The use of rituximab and intravenous immunoglobulin in nearly one-third of patients reflects the need for treatment-intensive approaches.

items.title: Functional and quality of life characteristics in children with juvenile dermatomyositis during their first outpatient consultation: A descriptive, retrospective study.
items.abstract: To describe the functional capacity, muscle strength, clinical-demographic characteristics, and quality of life and respiratory function of children diagnosed with juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM) during their initial outpatient consultation at the Physical Therapy Unit (PTU). A descriptive, retrospective, and cross-sectional study. The study included 51 subjects under 16 years of age diagnosed with JDM, evaluated between 2018 and 2024, who had completed the full PTU evaluation protocol. Fifty-one children with a diagnosis of JDM were analyzed; the median age was 9.06 years (IQR: 6-12). The Disease Activity Score (DAS) showed a median of 9 (IQR: 5-14). The median Childhood Health Assessment Questionnaire (C-HAQ) score was 0.875 (IQR: 0.25-1.75). The Childhood Myositis Assessment Scale (CMAS) presented a median of 34 (IQR: 21-46). Manual Muscle Testing (MMT) reported a median of 55 (IQR: 44-71). The median Timed Up and Go (TUG) test was 6.66s (IQR: 6.11-8.06). Of the subjects, 56.86% (29 subjects) were able to complete the 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT), reporting a median distance of 345m (IQR: 292.5-397.5). The Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL) for children and caregivers showed medians of 56.98 (IQR: 41.30-87.75) and 60.71 (IQR: 45.40-84.75), respectively. Children with JDM presented moderate impairment of functional capacity, endurance, strength, and cough efficacy during the initial evaluation. The most affected muscle groups were the neck flexors, hip flexors and hip extensors. The majority of subjects exhibited muscular and cutaneous inflammatory activity. No relevant differences were found between the quality-of-life assessments of the children and their families.

items.title: Pharmacological treatment intensity score for rheumatoid arthritis patients (PTIS-RA_1.3).
items.abstract: Research into complementary treatments for rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is expanding. These adjuvant therapies are typically administered alongside conventional treatments, including csDMARDs, bDMARDs and tsDMARDs. Monitoring pharmacological changes is crucial to discern whether clinical improvement is due to adjuvant intervention or medication adjustments. This paper presents a tool (PTIS-RA_1.3) that converts RA pharmacological treatment into a numerical value, reflecting treatment intensity based on drug type and dosage. Each drug is assigned a score based on its pharmacological class and administered dose, strictly aligned with EULAR recommendations. The scoring system was developed using consensus methodology inspired by the Delphi method. To illustrate the utility of the score, we present its implementation in the AIDE-RAP trial (NCT05254223). The tool successfully quantified treatment intensity and modifications over a 12-month period, as shown in the illustrative cases. PTIS-RA_1.3 is a novel system that transforms qualitative medication data into a quantitative variable, facilitating statistical analysis and graphical representation. Furthermore, it serves as an indirect measure of disease aggressiveness by reflecting the therapeutic burden required to maintain clinical control.

items.title: Prevalence of probable central sensitization defined using the Central Sensitization Inventory and its association with clinical outcomes in axial spondyloarthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: This study aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of central sensitization (CS) features defined by the Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI≥40) and quantify its association with disease activity, pain, quality of life, and physical function in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). Systematic searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to April 2026. Observational studies reporting CSI scores and patient-reported outcomes in axSpA were included. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled prevalence and standardized mean differences (SMDs) for BASDAI, pain VAS, ASQoL, BASFI, and ASDAS-CRP, comparing CSI≥40 versus CSI<40 patients. Certainty was assessed using GRADE. Seventeen studies (1278 patients) were included. The pooled prevalence of CSI-defined probable CS (score≥40) was 48.5% (95% CI: 44.1-52.8%; I 2 =55%). Compared with CSI<40 patients, those with CSI≥40 had significantly worse outcomes: BASDAI (SMD=1.76; 95% CI: 1.21-2.31; I 2 =88%), pain VAS (SMD=1.32; 95% CI: 0.91-1.73; I 2 =56%), ASQoL (SMD=1.88; 95% CI: 1.18-2.57; I 2 =90%), BASFI (SMD=1.35; 95% CI: 1.10-1.60; I 2 =77%), and ASDAS-CRP (SMD=1.02; 95% CI: 0.84-1.20; I 2 =0%); all with p<0.0001. Absolute differences on original scales were approximately 3 BASDAI points (0-10), 2-3cm VAS (0-10), 6-8 ASQoL points (0-18), and 1.5-2 BASFI points (0-10). GRADE certainty was low for prevalence and very low for most outcomes due to observational designs and heterogeneity. CSI-defined probable CS features affect nearly one in two axSpA patients and are associated with large, clinically meaningful adverse effects across multiple patient-centered outcomes. These findings suggest that screening for CSI-defined probable CS features may be clinically useful in selected patients, particularly those with persistently high symptom burden despite controlled inflammation. PROSPERO registration: CRD420261380153.

items.title: Real-world data of the PURE-4 scale for diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis in patients with psoriasis.
items.abstract: Approximately 15% of patients with psoriasis followed by dermatologists have undiagnosed psoriatic arthritis (PsA). The progression rate of PsA is significantly higher in patients with established disease of more than two years' duration. Therefore, screening tests for early diagnosis are crucial to prevent joint damage. Our study aims to evaluate the usefulness of the PURE-4 scale in real-world clinical practice for identifying patients with psoriatic arthritis (PsA) among individuals with psoriasis. Retrospective descriptive study of conducted between January 2021 and December 2023. A total of 60 patients with a prior diagnosis of psoriasis were referred by the Dermatology Department for suspected PsA based on the PURE-4 scale. PsA was diagnosed in 34% of patients following rheumatologic evaluation. A PURE-4 score≥2 or the presence of dactylitis alone appears to enhance the sensitivity and specificity of the PURE-4 scale.

items.title: The role of MEFV gene mutations in the therapeutic management of spondyloarthropathies.
items.abstract: The role of MEFV gene mutations in modifying disease course and treatment response in spondyloarthritis (SpA) remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the the clinical and therapeutic implications of MEFV gene mutations. A total of 131 SpA patients were categorized into MEFV negative (n=50), MEFV carrier (n=38), and Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) accompanying SpA (n=43) groups. Pathogenic variant carriers were further analyzed. Clinical features, disease activity scores, and treatment outcomes - including biologic DMARD use and response - were compared across the groups. The FMF accompanying SpA group had a significantly earlier disease onset (p=0.021) and higher amyloidosis frequency (p=0.040). Biologic usage rates were similar across groups (76% vs. 60.5% vs. 69.8%, p=0.295), as were anti-TNF response rates (80% vs. 77.3% vs. 78.6%, p=0.210). No significant differences were found when comparing pathogenic MEFV carriers with MEFV negative patients. While MEFV mutations did not significantly alter classical disease activity measures or response rates to anti-TNF therapy in SpA patients, their presence, particularly in those with concomitant FMF, was associated with an increased risk of amyloidosis and a tendency toward a more complex inflammatory phenotype. Larger cohorts and prospective studies will clarify the impact of MEFV mutations on amyloidosis risk and treatments outcomes in SpA patients.

items.title: Association Between Baseline Modified Novel Fibrosis Index and Subsequent Stroke in Patients with Microscopic Polyangiitis or Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis.
items.abstract: Background and Objectives : This study investigated whether the baseline modified novel fibrosis index (mNFI) could predict subsequent stroke in patients with microscopic polyangiitis (MPA) or granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA). Materials and Methods : This study included 268 patients with MPA or GPA who met the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Clinical data at diagnosis were collected. Baseline Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score (BVAS), Five-Factor Score (FFS), and earliest Vasculitis Damage Index (eVDI) were recorded as MPA/GPA-specific indices, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels were recorded as acute-phase reactants. mNFI was derived by deleting the constant 'N' from the NFI formula and was calculated as follows: serum bilirubin (mg/dL) × (alkaline phosphatase [IU/L]) 2 / platelet count (× 1000/mm 3 ) / (serum albumin [g/dL]) 2 . Results : Among the 268 patients with MPA (70.9%) or GPA (29.1%), the median age was 62.0 years, and 64.6% were women. During a median follow-up of 55.1 months, stroke occurred in 7.1% of patients. Baseline mNFI correlated significantly with age, FFS and CRP, but not with BVAS or eVDI. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis showed that baseline mNFI (hazard ratio 1.079) was independently associated with subsequent stroke alongside CRP levels. Patients with baseline mNFI ≥1.08 had a higher risk of subsequent stroke and a lower cumulative stroke-free survival rate than those with baseline mNFI < 1.08. Conclusions : Baseline mNFI was associated with subsequent stroke in patients with MPA or GPA and may represent a readily available candidate marker for cerebrovascular risk assessment. Further validation is required before its routine clinical application.

items.title: The Role of MACIR Gene in Regulation of Immune Response and Pathogenesis of Disease.
items.abstract: The macrophage immunometabolism regulator (MACIR) gene, also known as C5orf30, has emerged as a potential regulator of immune responses and inflammatory processes. Increasing evidence suggests that MACIR gene expression is associated with macrophage function, cellular metabolism, and inflammatory signalling, potentially contributing to the maintenance of immune homeostasis. Dysregulation of MACIR gene expression has been associated with pathological inflammatory responses and may play a role in the development and progression of autoimmune and chronic inflammatory diseases, particularly rheumatoid arthritis. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the biological functions of MACIR remain incompletely understood. This review summarises current knowledge regarding the structure, expression, and regulation of the MACIR gene, with particular emphasis on its potential role in immune cell function and inflammatory signalling. The involvement of MACIR in rheumatoid arthritis and other immune-mediated diseases is discussed, together with emerging evidence linking MACIR to immunometabolism and disease-associated cellular responses. Furthermore, the potential of MACIR as a biomarker and therapeutic target is considered. A better understanding of the mechanisms regulating MACIR gene expression may provide new insights into the pathogenesis of inflammatory and autoimmune diseases and contribute to the development of novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Anti-Melanoma Differentiation-Associated Protein 5 Antibody and the Risk of Rapidly Progressive Interstitial Lung Disease in Patients with Dermatomyositis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Background: To assess the diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility of anti-melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (anti-MDA5) antibodies for identifying rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (RP-ILD) in patients with classic dermatomyositis (CDM) and clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis (CADM). Methods: We searched PubMed, Ovid MEDLINE, and Embase from 1 January 1991 to 31 January 2022. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Studies with a complete 2 × 2 diagnostic table were synthesized using a bivariate random-effects generalized linear mixed model with exact binomial likelihood, and the equivalent hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) curve was derived. Prespecified subgroup analyses, leave-one-out and study-exclusion sensitivity analyses, univariable bivariate meta-regression, and Deeks' funnel-plot asymmetry test were performed. Results: Seventeen studies with complete 2 × 2 data (1528 patients; 261 with RP-ILD) entered the quantitative synthesis. The bivariate summary sensitivity was 75.8% (95% CI, 59.7-86.8%) and specificity was 88.5% (95% CI, 84.4-91.6%). The derived LR+ was 6.57 (95% CI, 4.59-9.38), LR- was 0.27 (95% CI, 0.16-0.48), and DOR was 24.0 (95% CI, 10.6-54.5). The 95% prediction intervals were wide for both sensitivity (22.8-97.1%) and specificity (68.7-96.4%), indicating substantial between-study variation. Among patients with RP-ILD, 99/261 (37.9%) were anti-MDA5 antibody negative. Prespecified meta-regressions did not show a significant joint covariate effect, and Deeks' funnel-plot asymmetry test did not detect evidence of small-study effects ( p = 0.276). Conclusions: Anti-MDA5 antibody positivity is associated with a substantially increased likelihood of RP-ILD and provides relatively high specificity, but its sensitivity is insufficient to exclude RP-ILD when the antibody is negative. Anti-MDA5 testing may therefore support early risk stratification as an adjunct to clinical and radiologic assessment rather than serve as a stand-alone diagnostic or prognostic marker.

items.title: The Gut Microbiota and Oxidative Stress as Converging Mechanisms in Environmental Chemical-Mediated Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex autoimmune disease (AD) characterized by chronic inflammation and multi-organ damage, driven by a combination of genetic, hormonal and environmental factors. Ample evidence links specific environmental agents, such as solvents, PFAS, microplastics, bisphenol A, mercury, pesticides, smoking and silica, to the development of SLE. Despite growing evidence highlighting the pivotal role of these environmental agents in initiating, modulating or exacerbating autoimmune responses, substantial gaps remain in our understanding of their precise role and mechanisms driving disease pathogenesis. Oxidative stress (OS) plays an important role in the pathogenesis of a variety of ADs, including SLE, and many environmental factors actively participate in this process. Furthermore, with the recent surge in microbiome research, numerous studies have provided insight into how changes in the gut microbiota contribute to the onset and progression of the disease. Importantly, understanding the interplay among OS, gut dysbiosis, and immune dysregulation will not only deepen our insight into environmental pathophysiology but also open new avenues for microbiota-targeted prevention and therapy in SLE. This review aims to provide an updated overview of the existing literature concerning the role of gut microbiome-OS-host interactions in the pathogenesis of SLE, while also exploring potential novel therapies.

items.title: B Cell Interferon-Induced Transmembrane Protein 2: A Candidate Biomarker Associated with Disease Activity in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: Background: Interferon-I (IFN-I) upregulates interferon-induced transmembrane protein 2 (IFITM2) expression, and elevated IFN-I levels are a hallmark of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). This study aimed to evaluate the association between IFITM2 expression and SLE pathogenesis. Given that dysregulated B cell differentiation and autoantibody production are key contributors to SLE and are further potentiated by IFN-I signaling, the involvement of relevant molecular pathways was also investigated. Methods: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were isolated from 15 healthy controls (HCs) and 35 patients with SLE. IFITM2 expression in B cells was quantified by flow cytometry and analyzed for association with disease activity. Univariable analysis and receiver operating characteristic curve analyses were performed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of IFITM2 for identifying active SLE. Results: IFITM2 expression was significantly upregulated in B cells from SLE patients relative to healthy controls (HCs). Patients with active SLE displayed higher IFITM2 levels in total B cells and B cell subsets compared with those in inactive disease, and its expression was positively correlated with the SLEDAI-2K score. IFITM2 expression showed a positive association with concentrations of immunoglobulins, proinflammatory cytokines, and antinuclear antibodies, while inversely correlated with serum complement C3 and C4 levels. Combined assessment of IFITM2 and anti-dsDNA antibody levels enhanced discriminatory performance for SLE. Notably, IFITM2 expression was markedly higher in SLE patients with renal involvement than in those without renal involvement and exhibited a positive correlation with urinary total protein (UTP). Conclusions: B cell IFITM2 expression is closely associated with disease activity in SLE and may serve as a potential biomarker to improve the discriminatory performance of anti-dsDNA testing. Moreover, IFITM2 correlates with renal involvement (defined by proteinuria) in SLE and shows a positive correlation with UTP, suggesting that combined assessment of IFITM2 and UTP may help reflect renal status in patients with SLE. However, these findings are exploratory and require validation in independent cohorts before IFITM2 can be considered a clinically useful biomarker.
