items.title: Genetic Testing of Suspected Intestinal Behçet's Disease to Identify Monogenic Mimics.
items.abstract: Background: Intestinal Behçet's disease is difficult to distinguish from other immune-mediated inflammatory diseases of the gastrointestinal tract such as Crohn's disease. In recent studies, researchers have reported that multiple monogenic autoinflammatory diseases can mimic Behçet's disease, making differential diagnosis more challenging. We aim to retrospectively describe the clinical and laboratory features of six pediatric cases with suspected intestinal Behçet's disease and identify potential monogenic mimics. Methods: This study is a retrospective case series. All patients underwent specialized digestive system evaluation including symptomatology, laboratory examinations, imaging, endoscopy, and pathology. Whole-exome sequencing was conducted to identify potential monogenic mimics. Results: All patients presented with prominent inflammation in the ileocecal region. A likely pathogenic de novo variant in a gene ( RELA ) associated with a mimicking disease phenotype was identified in one out of six patients, while a second patient had a de novo variant of uncertain significance (VUS) in RELA . A VUS in TNFAIP3 gene was identified in a third patient but was inherited from an unaffected parent. The other three patients either had no detected variant (two cases), or a very likely benign coincidental variant (in CCR1 gene). Conclusions: Monogenic autoinflammatory disorders can be mistaken for Behçet's disease. We emphasize the importance of genetic testing in pediatric patients with intestinal Behçet's disease who present with atypical clinical symptoms, but also the importance of using tools to estimate the likelihood of variant pathogenicity, to avoid the overinterpretation of variant significance.

items.title: Recognizing treatment non-response in anti-MDA5-positive rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease: a trajectory-based framework for parallel escalation.
items.abstract: Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 antibody-positive dermatomyositis complicated by rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (anti-MDA5-positive RP-ILD) can progress from inflammatory lung injury to refractory respiratory failure within a short and clinically uncertain interval. Existing literature has largely evaluated individual immunomodulatory regimens, prognostic factors or organ-replacement outcomes, but provides limited guidance on when an inadequate early response should be regarded as clinically actionable treatment failure. This gap is important because persistent disease activity may coexist with infection, drug toxicity, pulmonary vascular events, air-leak syndromes and ventilation-related injury, each of which changes the expected benefit and risk of further immunosuppression. In this narrative review, we distinguish treatment non-response, treatment failure and refractory disease as related but non-equivalent concepts. We then organize evidence on treatment exposure, oxygenation and imaging trajectories, inflammatory activity, competing causes of deterioration, respiratory-support requirements and future treatment eligibility into a T0-T6 trajectory-based framework. The framework treats rescue immunomodulation, diagnostic reassessment, critical-care activation and preservation of advanced-support options as parallel decisions rather than consecutive treatment steps. It is intended as a structured communication and research model, not as a validated staging system or prescriptive clinical guideline. Its principal contribution is to define the questions that should be revisited when continued observation may threaten otherwise feasible treatment options.

items.title: Intestinal microbiota alterations link subclinical inflammation and clinical phenotypes in familial Mediterranean fever.
items.abstract: Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) is an autoinflammatory disease caused by mutations in the Mediterranean fever ( MEFV ) gene. Although FMF is classically associated with serosal inflammation, emerging evidence suggests intestinal involvement. We aimed to investigate subclinical intestinal inflammation in patients with FMF by assessing fecal calprotectin (FCP) levels and intestinal microbial and fecal metabolic profiles. Thirty patients with FMF from three hospitals were stratified into the FCP-high (>94 μg/g) and FCP-low (≤94 μg/g) groups. For intestinal microbiota analysis, patients with FMF were also compared with healthy controls and patients with inflammatory bowel disease unclassified (IBDU) from previous multicenter studies. Elevated FCP levels were detected in 26.7% patients. The FCP-high group had lower hemoglobin levels and a trend toward lower albumin levels. Compared with healthy controls, patients with FMF showed reduced alpha diversity and differences in overall microbiota composition. A higher relative abundance of Bifidobacterium longum and lower relative abundances of Faecalibacterium , Blautia , and Blautia obeum showed exploratory associations with arthritis, as well as lower albumin and hemoglobin levels. The FCP-high group showed greater depletion in the relative abundance of Blautia and nominally higher fecal 2-amino-2-methyl-1-propanol levels. The relative abundance of Lactobacillus , Streptococcus , and Enterococcus showed stepwise increased from healthy controls to the FCP-low FMF, FCP-high FMF, and IBDU with MEFV mutation groups, whereas that of Fusicatenibacter and Agathobacter showed stepwise decreased across these groups. This exploratory study identified associations among FMF, elevated FCP, and alterations in the intestinal microbiota. Elevated FCP in a subset of clinically remitted patients may suggest possible subclinical intestinal inflammatory activity.

items.title: Systemic lupus erythematosus and cutaneous manifestations: emerging treatment approaches.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic and complex autoimmune disease associated with significant morbidity and a relapsing-remitting course. Diagnosis and management remain challenging because of heterogeneous clinical presentations and variable treatment responses, reflecting the underlying immune dysregulation driving disease pathogenesis. Cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE) may occur as an isolated skin disorder or as part of the broader clinical spectrum of SLE. The skin is the second most frequently affected organ system in SLE. Cutaneous manifestations occur in 70%-85% of patients during the disease course and represent the initial presenting feature in up to one-quarter of patients. CLE can occur as a manifestation of SLE or independent of systemic disease. The clinical significance of cutaneous manifestations lies in their diagnostic value, prognostic associations with systemic disease activity, and therapeutic implications for patient management. Cutaneous manifestations frequently present early and can serve as the sole clue to SLE, helping establish diagnosis before systemic involvement. Certain lesions, such as acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus, vasculitis, and bullous lupus, correlate with systemic disease activity and severity, while others, such as discoid lupus erythematosus, may predict more localized disease but carry a risk of permanent scarring. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the spectrum of cutaneous manifestations of SLE, focusing on their underlying pathophysiology, diagnostic relevance, and current management approaches.

items.title: Case Report: Coronary artery involvement and nonvisualization of pulmonary artery branches first detected during follow-up of Takayasu arteritis.
items.abstract: Takayasu arteritis (TA) is a chronic granulomatous large-vessel vasculitis of unknown etiology that can involve the coronary and pulmonary arteries. A 30-year-old woman presented with crushing chest pain and was found to have 95% stenosis at the ostium of the left main coronary artery. Approximately 3.5 months after coronary stent implantation, severe in-stent restenosis occurred, requiring balloon angioplasty. Positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) showed thickening of the ascending aorta and aortic arch wall with increased fluorodeoxyglucose uptake, supporting the clinical diagnosis of TA. She received glucocorticoids and methotrexate and, because of persistent coronary disease, underwent off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting, followed by tocilizumab. During follow-up, C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate remained within reference ranges. In September 2025, echocardiography estimated a mean pulmonary artery pressure of 21 mmHg, whereas an October examination did not report pulmonary hypertension. On October 15, 2025, right heart catheterization measured a pulmonary artery pressure of 39/10 mmHg (mean 20 mmHg), which did not meet the current hemodynamic threshold for pulmonary hypertension. Pulmonary angiography showed nonvisualization of the right upper and middle lobar pulmonary artery branches. Because of the lack of baseline pulmonary vascular imaging or a complete evaluation of alternative causes, the onset and etiology of this finding remain uncertain. Normal acute-phase reactants during tocilizumab therapy should not be regarded as evidence of the absence of vascular disease, and angiographic nonvisualization alone cannot establish active vasculitic occlusion.

items.title: Cohort-aware single-cell analysis of PBMCs identifies an interferon program specific to primary Sjögren's syndrome and limited immune convergence with periodontitis.
items.abstract: Periodontitis (PD) and primary Sjögren's syndrome (pSS) are epidemiologically linked, and shared peripheral immune dysregulation has been proposed. Published comparisons rest on bulk transcriptomes or on tests that treat cells as replicates, and in public data disease is confounded with study. We reanalyzed four public single-cell RNA-seq cohorts of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs; two PD, two pSS) with the donor as the unit of inference and cases compared with same-cohort controls. After removal of eight duplicated samples, 48 donors (24 controls, 10 PD, 14 pSS) and 317,205 cells in 28 subsets were analyzed for composition, pseudobulk expression and consensus regulon activity. A finding was considered replicated when significant in the pooled model (false discovery rate <0.05) and in both cohorts of a disease; differences between the PD and pSS effects were tested directly. PD showed no replicated change in any layer, and its transcriptome-wide perturbation did not exceed the permutation null. pSS showed a type I interferon program across lineages: STAT1(+), STAT2(+), ETV7(+) and IRF7(+) accounted for 25 of 44 replicated regulon-subset pairs, their targets were the interferon-stimulated genes that dominated the replicated differentially expressed genes, and an interferon score separated pSS from PD (area under the ROC curve 0.90-0.95). In the larger pSS cohort, 93% of the PBMC interferon signal arose from higher expression within cells, not from composition. Naive/central memory CD4 + T cells were reduced in both pSS cohorts. Cross-disease concordance was weak but exceeded permutation nulls (regulons, rho = 0.38, P = 0.031; genes, rho = 0.13, P = 0.012) and had two components: fewer CD56dim NK cells and more cells of a mixed T-like/adaptive-like NK subset in all four cohorts, and lower expression of glucocorticoid- and stress-responsive genes in cases across lineages. With pooled controls, the same data yielded "shared" regulons that did not survive cohort-aware testing, and 39%-68% of regulon-subset pairs differed between the controls of the PD and pSS studies. The replicated peripheral immune change is specific to pSS; what the two diseases share is limited to a compositional shift in the NK lineage and a stress-response signature of uncertain origin.

items.title: Factors associated with fatigue in systemic lupus erythematosus: a cross-sectional structural equation modeling analysis of depressive symptoms as a potential mediator.
items.abstract: This study examined physiological, psychological, and environmental factors associated with fatigue in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and assessed whether depressive symptoms statistically mediated the relationships between these factors and fatigue. A convenience sample of 252 patients with SLE was recruited from the Department of Rheumatology and Immunology, Second Hospital of Hebei Medical University, between June 2023 and June 2024. Guided by the Theory of Unpleasant Symptoms (TOUS), candidate variables were classified into physiological (including disease activity on the SLEDAI-2K, anemia, biologic agent use, and sleep disturbance), psychological (anxiety and depressive symptoms), and environmental factors (including employment status and social support). Pain severity and other clinically recorded variables were entered as covariates. Validated measures included the Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS), Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and Social Support Rating Scale (SSRS). Univariate analyses, Spearman correlation analysis, and multivariable linear regression were performed using SPSS 26.0. Structural equation modeling (SEM) and indirect-effect testing based on bootstrapping (2,000 resamples; percentile 95% confidence intervals) were performed in R (lavaan). Sensitivity analyses (robust estimation, a Bollen-Stine bootstrap, and covariate-adjusted and alternative mediator models) were also performed. Social support, depressive symptoms, sleep disturbance, pain severity, biologic agent use, and employment status were found to be independently related to fatigue. Moreover, social support and sleep disturbance each had a significant indirect relationship with fatigue via depressive symptoms. The indirect associations persisted after clinical covariates were specified as predictors of both depressive symptoms and fatigue. However, social support was not independently associated with the binary fatigue outcome (FSS ≥ 4; OR = 0.96 per SD, P  = 0.837). In this cross-sectional sample, social support, depressive symptoms, sleep disturbance, pain severity, biologic agent use, and employment status were associated with fatigue, and depressive symptoms showed a statistically significant indirect association with fatigue through pathways linking social support and sleep disturbance. Because the data are cross-sectional, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory indirect associations that are compatible with, but do not establish, a mediating mechanism, and as hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of causality or treatment effect. Systematic assessment of social support and depressive symptoms, together with dynamic evaluation of sleep disturbance and pain, may inform comprehensive fatigue assessment, while longitudinal and interventional studies are needed before firm clinical recommendations can be made.

items.title: Shifting mortality profiles in rheumatoid arthritis in the United States, 1999-2024: a multiple-cause-of-death study.
items.abstract: Analyses restricted to rheumatoid arthritis (RA) as the underlying cause of death may incompletely characterize mortality involving RA. We examined population-based mortality trends and underlying-cause distributions among U.S. deaths mentioning RA. We conducted a repeated cross-sectional study using CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death data for 1999-2024. Deaths were classified as any mention of RA (RA-AM), RA as the underlying cause (RA-UCD), or RA recorded with another condition as the underlying cause (RA-nonUCD). Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were standardized to the 2000 U.S. population and expressed per million population. Trends were assessed using joinpoint regression. Among 244,813 deaths mentioning RA, 184,537 were RA-nonUCD. The RA-nonUCD proportion increased from 72.60% in 1999 to 82.03% in 2024. AAMRs declined from 36.67 to 23.16 for RA-AM, 10.07 to 4.13 for RA-UCD, and 26.62 to 19.01 for RA-nonUCD, with average annual percentage changes of -1.79%, -3.62%, and -1.39%, respectively. Among RA-nonUCD deaths, circulatory diseases remained the leading underlying cause, although their share declined from 46.75% to 30.05%. Within this category, the ischemic heart disease share decreased from 54.68% to 38.33%. The shares attributed to endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases, mental and behavioral disorders, and diseases of the nervous system increased from 4.47% to 7.77%, 1.38% to 4.72%, and 2.93% to 7.89%, respectively. Cancer and respiratory diseases ranked second and third by cumulative death counts. Population-based age-adjusted mortality rates involving RA declined during 1999-2024, with the largest relative decline observed when RA was the underlying cause. RA-nonUCD accounted for an increasing proportion of deaths mentioning RA. Within this group, circulatory diseases remained the leading underlying cause, while the proportions attributed to endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases, mental and behavioral disorders, and diseases of the nervous system increased.

items.title: 18 F-FDG PET/MRI and PET/CT for muscle and malignancy assessment in dermatomyositis.
items.abstract: Dermatomyositis (DM) requires advanced imaging to assess muscle inflammation and timely malignancy screening. Hybrid positron emission tomography (PET) imaging combines metabolic and anatomical data; however, whether it can comprehensively evaluate DM is unclear. We evaluated the ability of 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and PET/computed tomography (CT) to detect muscle involvement and cancer-associated myositis (CAM) in DM. This retrospective study evaluated 41 patients, including 39 with classic DM and 2 with clinically amyopathic DM (CADM), who underwent PET/MRI (n=27) or PET/CT (n=14). Whole-body MRI was scored for muscle edema, fatty infiltration and atrophy. FDG uptake was quantified using region-based maximum standardized uptake value (SUV max ) ratios (muscle-to-blood pool) and Deauville scores. Imaging parameters (edema scores, SUV max ratios, Deauville scores) and clinical data (muscle enzymes and myositis-specific autoantibodies) were analyzed. The sensitivity of PET/MRI was higher than that of PET/CT for detecting muscle involvement in classic DM (100% [25/25] vs. 78.6% [11/14]; P = 0.04). No muscle involvement was detected in CADM. Total edema scores correlated with creatine kinase (ρ=0.505, 95% CI 0.147-0.747; P<0.01) and lactate dehydrogenase (ρ=0.723, 95% CI 0.466-0.867; P<0.0001). Ten patients fulfilled the temporal definition of CAM (10/41, 24.4%), with nasopharyngeal carcinoma being the most common subtype (4/10, 40.0%). Stratified by modality, 2 malignancies were observed in the PET/MRI cohort (2/27, 7.4%), and 8 malignancies were identified in the PET/CT cohort (8/14, 57.1%). Anti-transcription intermediary factor-1γ antibody grade correlated with the SUV max ratio (ρ=0.452, 95% CI 0.168-0.667; P<0.01). PET/MRI detected muscle involvement more frequently than PET/CT in classic DM, while both PET/MRI and PET/CT contributed to malignancy assessment in this cohort. Hybrid PET imaging may aid disease phenotyping and cancer surveillance in DM.

items.title: Belimumab added to multi-target therapy in lupus nephritis: a retrospective cohort study of efficacy, divergent temporal response patterns, and safety.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is a severe complication of systemic lupus erythematosus. Belimumab, a B-cell-activating factor (BAFF) inhibitor, improves renal outcomes when added to standard therapy, but its efficacy and temporal effects when combined with multi-target therapy regimens containing tacrolimus remain poorly characterized. We compared multi-target therapy plus belimumab with multi-target therapy alone in active LN. In this retrospective cohort study, 28 patients with active LN (14 per group) received multi-target therapy (glucocorticoid, mycophenolate mofetil, and tacrolimus, a calcineurin inhibitor) with (case group) or without (control group) belimumab. The patients were assessed at baseline and 3, 6, and 12 months after treatment initiation. Primary endpoints were 24-hour urinary protein (24hUP), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR). C3, C4, anti-dsDNA, SLEDAI-2K, and IgG/IgA/IgM were the secondary endpoints. Comparisons were conducted using Welch's t or Mann-Whitney U tests (between-group), paired t or Wilcoxon tests (within-group), and Cohen's d effect sizes. Compared to baseline, both groups exhibited significant improvement in proteinuria, SLEDAI-2K, anti-dsDNA, and complement. eGFR remained stable, with no significant between-group differences at any timepoint. Temporal patterns diverged: the belimumab group showed earlier reduction in proteinuria (from 3 months) and IgG/IgA/IgM levels, whereas multi-target therapy alone showed earlier recovery of complement levels, with weak C4 recovery after treatment with belimumab. During twelve months of treatment, adverse events were infrequent and comparable between groups (all p  = 1.00). Both regimens substantially improved renal and serological outcomes over 12 months with an acceptable safety profile. Although the addition of belimumab did not significantly outperform multi-target therapy alone, the two regimens exhibited distinct, mechanistically coherent temporal signatures: inhibition of the BAFF pathway versus broad immunosuppression. These findings warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies.

items.title: The first two principal IL-1 receptor co-expression remodeling in allergic and autoimmune inflammation reveals disease-associated differences.
items.abstract: Interleukin-1 is a central mediator of inflammation, with its activity governed by the opposing functions of the signaling-competent receptor IL-1R1 and the inhibitory decoy receptor IL-1R2. However, comprehensive profiling of IL-1 receptor co-expression across immune cell subsets in diseases with distinct pathogenesis remains limited. We investigated the expression and co-expression patterns of IL-1R1 and IL-1R2 on twelve peripheral blood immune cell populations from patients with rheumatoid arthritis, patients with bronchial asthma, and healthy donors using multicolor flow cytometry. Receptor density was quantified as antibody-binding capacity per cell. Unsupervised clustering and logistic regression were applied to identify disease-associated candidate signatures and to develop exploratory diagnostic algorithms. Exploratory dimensionality reduction suggested separation of the three groups in this cohort, with each disease displaying a distinct IL-1 receptor remodeling pattern. Bronchial asthma was characterized by a global shift toward the double-negative phenotype across most populations, profound decoy receptor deficiency, and a striking predominance of the double-positive phenotype in naive T cells. Rheumatoid arthritis exhibited a less pronounced double-negative shift, selective loss of decoy receptor on monocytes, and mixed cytotoxic T cell profiles with preserved signaling-competent phenotypes. Logistic regression models incorporating three parameters for RA showed high discrimination in this case-control cohort, with apparent and cross-validated performance remaining robust for this disease. These findings indicate that allergic and autoimmune inflammation are associated with distinct, cell-subset-specific IL-1 receptor signatures consistent with their divergent immunopathogenesis. The identified receptor profiles may serve as candidate biomarkers and provide hypotheses for mechanistic studies of interleukin-1 pathway dysregulation in chronic inflammatory diseases. The model requires external validation before any clinical application.

items.title: Pyroptosis in systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis: evidence grading, cellular crosstalk, and translational priorities.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) links persistent immune dysregulation to heterogeneous tissue injury, but the mechanisms that localise damage remain incompletely resolved. Pyroptosis is a gasdermin-mediated, pore-forming process that can connect nucleic-acid sensing and inflammasome activation to mediator release and tissue-cell dysfunction. Here, we evaluate the SLE and lupus nephritis (LN) literature along two independent axes: mechanistic evidence for pathway licensing, inflammasome activation, gasdermin execution, or terminal lysis, and disease relevance across non-lupus models, lupus models, patient-derived cells, human renal tissue, and longitudinal cohorts. Four conclusions emerge. First, execution-level evidence is confined to a few nodes, including oxidised mitochondrial DNA-driven GSDMD oligomerisation, myeloid caspase-11/GSDMD signalling, and GSDME-mediated tubular epithelial injury; most reported lupus "pyroptosis axes" demonstrate licensing or inflammasome activation only. Second, the direction of GSDMD function remains unresolved: pharmacological inhibition ameliorates experimental lupus, whereas genetic deficiency worsens autoimmunity, renal and pulmonary inflammation, and myeloid calcium homeostasis. Third, the tubulointerstitial compartment carries the strongest executor-level causal evidence in the kidney, whereas glomerular studies offer broader regulatory hypotheses but weaker execution-level proof. Fourth, no current biomarker is execution-specific, and no intervention has demonstrated executor target engagement in patients. We therefore present immune-tissue crosstalk as an evidence-graded framework rather than a demonstrated end-to-end circuit and define the spatial, longitudinal, and lineage-specific studies needed for mechanism-guided translation.

items.title: Temporomandibular Joint Involvement in Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis: Can Clinical Examination and Panoramic Radiography Predict MRI Findings?
items.abstract: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) involvement is common in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) and may impair function and craniofacial growth. Although magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the preferred imaging modality, its routine use in children is limited by cost, examination time, and potential sedation requirements. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of clinical examination and panoramic radiography (OPG) compared with MRI. Seventy patients with JIA (52 females; mean age 13.4 ± 2.8 years) underwent standardized TMJ assessment, OPG, and non-contrast enhanced MRI. A composite clinical score (0-7) was calculated based on muscle and TMJ tenderness, mandibular deviation, reduced maximum mouth opening and joint clicking. A score ≥3 was considered positive. MRI served as the reference standard, with TMJ involvement defined primarily by structural or functional abnormalities. At least one clinical sign of TMJ involvement was observed in 41% of patients. MRI-detected TMJ involvement was significantly more frequent among patients with a clinical score ≥3 than among those with a score <3 (92.0% vs. 24.4%; p < 0.001). Clinical examination showed 67.6% sensitivity, 94.4% specificity, 92.0% positive predictive value (PPV), and 75.6% negative predictive value (NPV). OPG findings were positive in 85.3% of MRI-positive patients and negative in all MRI-negative patients ( p < 0.001), corresponding to 85.3% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 100% PPV, and 87.8% NPV. Clinical examination and OPG may help identify patients with a higher likelihood of MRI-detected TMJ involvement who may benefit from further MRI evaluation.

items.title: Bilateral Popliteal Artery Aneurysms as a Manifestation of Vascular Behçet Disease: A Case Report and Literature Review.
items.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance : Popliteal artery aneurysmal involvement is an uncommon arterial manifestation of Behçet disease, and bilateral disease with thrombotic complications is particularly rare. Management is challenging because urgent limb revascularization must be balanced against an inflammatory vasculopathy associated with recurrent arterial events and loss of graft patency. Case presentation: A 50-year-old man presented with Rutherford IIa acute right lower-limb ischemia caused by thrombosis and distal embolization from a 4.4 cm true fusiform distal femoral-to-popliteal aneurysm. Computed tomography angiography also demonstrated a 2.4 cm contralateral true fusiform aneurysm with mural thrombus. Catheter-directed thrombolysis and adjunctive endovascular treatment restored distal perfusion, followed by Viabahn covered-stent exclusion of the right aneurysm. The asymptomatic left aneurysm was electively excluded 5 months later. Within the following year, acute left stent-graft occlusion required endovascular salvage, while right in-stent restenosis was treated with drug-coated balloon angioplasty. Recurrent vascular events prompted rheumatological evaluation, and vascular Behçet disease was diagnosed in 2022, followed by corticosteroid and methotrexate therapy. During approximately 5 years of follow-up, both popliteal stent grafts eventually occluded; however, collateral perfusion preserved limb viability, with only mild intermittent claudication and no rest pain or tissue loss at the latest follow-up. Conclusions: Bilateral popliteal aneurysmal disease with thrombosis may lead to recognition of vascular Behçet disease. Endovascular exclusion can provide immediate limb salvage and aneurysm control, but recurrent thrombosis, restenosis, and late loss of patency remain possible. Long-term management should integrate inflammatory disease control with vascular surveillance while distinguishing anatomical graft failure from clinical limb outcome.

items.title: A Qualitative Study Exploring Foot Pain and Its Impact on Daily Function in Early Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease frequently associated with significant foot pain, even in early stages. This study aimed to explore how patients with early RA perceive foot pain and its impact on daily activities. Semi-structured interviews were developed based on the Spanish Foot Function Index (FFI-Sp) in 25 patients with RA of less than five years' duration. Four key themes emerged: (1) limitations in performing daily activities due to foot-related problems; (2) descriptions of pain, such as burning and throbbing sensations; (3) emotional responses, including frustration and sadness; and (4) perceived changes in mobility, balance, and muscle strength. Patients reported pain as influenced by both intrinsic disease mechanisms and external factors. These findings highlight the early and substantial impact of foot involvement in RA and support the need for multidisciplinary interventions-encompassing orthopaedic care, psychosocial support, and patient education-to improve functional outcomes and quality of life. V (Qualitative study).

items.title: Catastrophic in-stent thrombosis with antiphospholipid syndrome: a case report.
items.abstract: In-stent thrombosis despite morphologically optimal stents remains a diagnostic challenge. Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a rare cause that drives thrombosis via tissue factor-mediated coagulation-a pathway not addressed by dual antiplatelet therapy. A 51-year-old male with cardiovascular risk factors underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention for anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Ten days later, he developed refractory ventricular fibrillation requiring extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation with veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and intra-aortic balloon pump support. Emergency angiography confirmed complete in-stent thrombosis; intravascular ultrasound excluded a mechanical cause. The intensive care course revealed a triad of red flags: unexplained in-stent thrombosis, recurrent extracorporeal circuit clotting despite stepwise heparin escalation, and arterial and venous thrombosis on full anticoagulation. This prompted antiphospholipid antibody testing, which showed persistent moderate-to-high titre anti-cardiolipin IgM-a profile within the 'controversial' zone of the 2023 ACR/EULAR classification criteria. The patient was managed as APS with intensified triple therapy, later transitioning from heparin to a vitamin K antagonist, and was discharged on Day 27 with no events at 3-month follow-up. Antiphospholipid syndrome should be considered in unexplained in-stent thrombosis even when laboratory criteria are not strictly met. The triad of unexplained in-stent thrombosis, anticoagulation refractory circuit clotting, and incident venous thrombosis is a clinically actionable pattern warranting empiric APS-directed management.

items.title: Treatment-Associated Leukocyte-Trafficking Vascular Inflammation in Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Bibliometric and Multicohort Transcriptomic Analysis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) synovitis involves vascular remodeling and leukocyte entry. Research has largely focused on angiogenesis, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), and hypoxia. We examined how these themes have developed and whether vascular-related inflammatory gene expression is reproducible across patient synovial datasets. We mapped RA vascular and endothelial research in the Web of Science Core Collection and analyzed public human synovial transcriptomes. Five predefined modules were scored separately within each dataset. Disease effects were pooled across independent studies using restricted maximum likelihood random-effects models with modified Hartung-Knapp inference. We tested Module C after adjustment for Module E, an endothelial abundance proxy, and assessed its change in paired baseline and week-12 samples from patients receiving anti-tumor necrosis factor (TNF) treatment. The 1568 eligible publications from January 2010 to July 2026 showed sustained growth in the field. Angiogenesis, VEGF, and hypoxia remained central, while terminology describing endothelial heterogeneity became more frequent. Across three independent RA-versus-healthy studies, Module C, representing leukocyte recruitment and trafficking, had the largest pooled disease effect: Hedges g = 1.772, 95% CI: 0.889-2.655, p = 0.0131. After Module E adjustment, β was 1.009, with a 95% CI of 0.623-1.395 and p = 0.00781. In GSE198520, the mean Module C change after 12 weeks of anti-TNF treatment was -0.296; the 95% CI was -0.445 to -0.147, and p = 0.000234. Good responders had a larger reduction than patients with no response, with a between-group difference of -0.530, a 95% CI of -0.838 to -0.223, and p = 0.00156. Module C was a reproducible RA-associated expression pattern in synovial tissue and decreased after anti-TNF treatment. Bulk expression cannot distinguish an endothelial source from immune-cell infiltration or overall inflammation.

items.title: Spinal Gout Presenting with Acute Paraplegia: A Case Report and Literature-Based Diagnostic Framework.
items.abstract: Background : Spinal gout is an uncommon manifestation of chronic hyperuricemia caused by the deposition of monosodium urate (MSU) crystals within axial skeletal structures. Although gout predominantly involves peripheral joints, axial deposition within the ligamentum flavum, facet joints, and epidural space can lead to spinal cord compression and severe neurological impairment. Because clinical and radiological features mimic spinal neoplasms, epidural abscesses, and degenerative disorders, diagnostic delays are common. Case Presentation : A 58-year-old man with an 8-year history of poorly controlled hyperuricemia and essential hypertension presented with progressive lower-limb weakness, severe thoracic back pain, lower-body numbness below the T10 dermatome, and acute urinary retention over two weeks. Neurological examination revealed flaccid paraplegia (Medical Research Council grade 0/5 in both lower extremities), complete loss of pinprick and light touch sensation below T10, absent deep tendon reflexes, and loss of anal sphincter tone, corresponding to American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) Impairment Scale Grade A. Serum uric acid was elevated at 9.5 mg/dL, alongside mildly elevated inflammatory markers. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a posterior extradural mass from T9 to T12 with severe cord compression centered at the T11-T12 level. Multi-sequence MRI demonstrated T1 iso/hypointensity, T2 heterogeneous hypointensity, thick peripheral rim enhancement on post-contrast T1-weighted sequences, and no restricted diffusion on DWI. Emergency decompressive laminectomy was performed, revealing a chalky white mass compressing the dural sac. Histopathological evaluation confirmed monosodium urate crystal deposits surrounded by granulomatous inflammation and multinucleated foreign-body giant cells. Postoperatively, the patient was initiated on treat-to-target urate-lowering therapy with allopurinol alongside short-term colchicine prophylaxis. At the 6-month follow-up, lower-limb motor strength recovered to grade 4/5, cutaneous sensation was restored, voluntary sphincter control was regained (ASIA Impairment Scale Grade D), and serum uric acid was normalized to 5.2 mg/dL. Conclusions : Spinal gout should be considered in the differential diagnosis of acute spinal cord compression, even in patients without active peripheral tophi. Prompt surgical decompression combined with long-term urate-lowering therapy is essential to facilitate neurological recovery and prevent disease recurrence.

items.title: When tuberculosis masquerades as Behçet's: A rare case of recurrent tuberculous lymphadenitis with pseudo-Behçet's syndrome.
items.abstract: Behçet's disease is a chronic, relapsing multisystem vasculitis characterized by mucocutaneous, ocular, and articular manifestations. Pseudo-Behçet's syndrome refers to a clinical presentation that mimics Behçet's disease, but is attributed to an underlying condition such as infection, rather than true systemic vasculitis. Pseudo-Behçet's, though rare, may occur as a hypersensitivity reaction to infectious agents, including mycobacterial antigens. We report a case of a female healthcare worker who presented with recurrent genital ulcers, arthropathy, erythema nodosum, and generalized lymphadenopathy, a constellation of features strongly suggestive of Behçet's syndrome. She also tested positive for HLA-B51, a genetic marker commonly associated withBehçet's. However, given her prior history of tuberculous lymphadenitis, further evaluation revealed a diagnosis of recurrent tuberculous lymphadenitis rather than true Behçet's disease. She showed significant clinical improvement for anti-tuberculous treatment, without the use of immunosuppressive therapy. This case highlights the importance of considering infectious mimics in the differential diagnosis of Behçet-like presentations, especially in tuberculosis endemic settings. It also highlights the rare phenomenon of pseudo-Behçet's syndrome associated with tuberculosis, indicating the diverse clinical spectrum of both conditions.

items.title: Anti-MDA5-associated rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease in clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis with secondary invasive pulmonary Aspergillus flavus infection after aggressive immunosuppressive therapy: a case report.
items.abstract: Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 (MDA5) positive rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (RP-ILD) with clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis (CADM) is a life-threatening condition. Prompt initiation of immunosuppressive therapy is crucial for improving outcomes. However, such treatment strategies substantially increase the risk of opportunistic infections, including invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA), even in patients without typical risk factors. A 59-year-old previously healthy woman reported a four-month history of progressive dyspnea, dry cough, and hoarseness, initially treated as pneumonia without clinical improvement. On admission, the patient presented with tachypnea, hypoxemia, bilateral crackles, and Gottron papules but no muscle weakness. High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) suggested organizing pneumonia, and serological testing revealed strongly positive anti-MDA5 antibodies, raising suspicion for RP-ILD associated with CADM. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid culture grew Aspergillus flavus, which was considered colonization due to non-specific imaging and absence of typical risk factors. From day 7 to day 9 after admission, the patient's condition deteriorated rapidly, with progressive respiratory failure accompanied by a marked hyperinflammatory state. Follow-up HRCT demonstrated worsening ground-glass opacities, consolidations, and traction bronchiectasis. A diagnosis of RP-ILD associated with CADM and positive anti-MDA5 antibodies was established. Aggressive triple immunosuppressive therapy was promptly initiated, including pulse methylprednisolone, cyclophosphamide, and mycophenolate mofetil. Subsequently, the patient developed fever and a positive serum galactomannan assay, raising a strong suspicion of IPA. Combination antifungal therapy with amphotericin B lipid complex and voriconazole was administered. Despite these interventions, respiratory failure continued to worsen, necessitating mechanical ventilation. The patient died on day 17 of hospitalization due to acute respiratory distress syndrome and septic shock. This case highlights the dual challenge of managing anti-MDA5-associated RP-ILD and recognizing opportunistic infections during intensive immunosuppression. IPA may occur as a life-threatening complication caused by A. flavus, even in the absence of classical risk factors or typical radiological features, leading to delayed diagnosis. Routine screening for IPA using serum or bronchoalveolar lavage galactomannan should be considered in patients undergoing potent immunosuppressive therapy.

items.title: Statin-related immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy: a case report.
items.abstract: While the safety profile of statins is generally considered as robust, they are known to be associated with a spectrum of muscle-related adverse effects, most of which are mild and reversible upon discontinuation of statins with some rare but serious exceptions. A 63-year-old Chinese gentleman presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness and markedly elevated creatine kinase levels after 2.5 years of atorvastatin therapy. The diagnosis of immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) was ascertained with muscle biopsy and positive autoantibody of anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase, and his condition responded to immunosuppressive therapy. IMNM is a rare but serious side effect related with statin use with delayed onset. With potential possibility of permanent disability, it is an important side effect that requires primary care doctors to maintain a high level of vigilance. The prompt recognition and immunosuppressive therapy is the key to avoid serious consequences.

items.title: Cannabidiol for chronic pain in rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis: a randomized, placebo-controlled trial with exploratory tetrahydrocannabinol add-on.
items.abstract: Persistent chronic pain remains a major unmet need in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and ankylosing spondylitis (AS), even when inflammatory disease activity is low. Evidence for cannabinoid-based treatment in inflammatory rheumatic disease is limited. We investigated the efficacy and safety of low-dose cannabidiol (CBD) for chronic pain in RA and AS and explored the effects of adjunctive tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) in non-responders. In this multicentre, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, 66 patients with RA or AS and persistent pain despite low inflammatory disease activity were randomized 1:1 to oral CBD or placebo for 12 weeks. The primary endpoint was a reduction of at least 20 points on the pain visual analogue scale (VAS) at week 12. After the blinded phase, non-responders entered a 12-week open-label phase: non-responders in the placebo group switched to CBD, while non-responders in the CBD group received add-on THC. Secondary outcomes included continuous pain VAS, sleep quality measured by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), cognitive performance assessed by the Trail Making Test (TMT) and Digit Symbol Substitution Test (DSST), disease activity measures, and safety. At week 12, the primary endpoint was achieved by 9/32 patients (28%) receiving placebo and 3/30 patients (10%) receiving low-dose CBD. Low-dose CBD did not demonstrate superior pain relief compared with placebo and was associated with poorer sleep quality, while no significant between-group differences were observed for cognitive outcomes or inflammatory markers. In the exploratory open-label phase, 9/23 patients (39%) receiving CBD plus THC achieved the predefined pain response criterion compared with 2/25 patients (8%) receiving CBD alone. The CBD + THC group also showed greater improvements in continuous pain VAS and sleep quality. Low-dose CBD did not yield meaningful pain relief. The addition of low-dose THC was associated with improvements in pain and sleep quality. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in blinded randomized controlled trials. European Union Clinical Trials Register, EudraCT 2017-004226-15, prospectively registered before enrolment of the first participant; Danish Medicines Agency 2018-010018.

items.title: Balloon pulmonary angioplasty in Takayasu arteritis with pulmonary artery involvement: a comparative study between patients with and without pulmonary hypertension.
items.abstract: Takayasu arteritis (TA) is a rare large-vessel vasculitis, and pulmonary artery involvement (PAI) can cause severe stenosis and pulmonary hypertension (PH), markedly impairing exercise capacity and quality of life. Although balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) has emerged as a promising interventional option, its preliminary efficacy and safety in TA-PAI-particularly in patients without PH-remain insufficiently defined. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the preliminary safety and differential clinical outcomes of BPA in patients with TA-PAI, stratified by the presence or absence of baseline PH. We retrospectively analyzed TA-PAI patients undergoing BPA. Hemodynamics, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), exercise capacity, and Quality of Life (QoL) were assessed pre- and post-BPA. Lesion anatomy and procedural complications were recorded. Statistical analyses compared PH and without PH subgroups. Among 33 TA-PAI patients, including 22 with PH and 11 without PH, BPA significantly reduced mPAP (25.41 ± 8.86 to 22.82 ± 7.94 mmHg, P = 0.005) and Pulmonary Vascular Resistance (PVR) from ( 3.06 [1.37,6.04] to 2.17 [1.35, 4.28] WU, P=0.039) in the overall population. In the PH subgroup, significant hemodynamic and functional improvements were observed, including reduced NT-proBNP (P=0.024), increased 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) (P=0.012), and enhanced QoL (all P <0.001). Conversely, the without PH group showed no significant hemodynamic changes (P > 0.05) but demonstrated modest 6MWD increases and significant QoL improvements. Left pulmonary artery lesions were more prevalent in the PH group (42.0% vs. 5.7%, P < 0.001). The procedure was generally safe, with infrequent complications, including vascular dissection (1.6%) and haemoptysis (0.8%), occurring only in a small number of patients. BPA demonstrated acceptable safety and preliminary efficacy for symptomatic TA-PAI. Findings suggest preliminary functional and hemodynamic benefits in patients with baseline PH, whereas benefits in patients without PH were primarily limited to quality of life rather than hemodynamics. Larger controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings.

items.title: Immunosuppressive Drug Use in Limited Systemic Sclerosis: An International Survey.
items.abstract: Current guidelines recommend immunosuppressive treatment for diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis but are less clear on their use in limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc) in the absence of internal organ complications. We conducted an international survey to understand current immunosuppressive drug prescribing patterns in lcSSc. An electronic REDCap survey was distributed to 756 general rheumatologists and 250 national and international SSc experts. A total of 139 participants (14%) responded to the survey (94% were rheumatologists); 58% of respondents reported at least sometimes using immunosuppressive drugs to treat cutaneous symptoms in lcSSc, whereas 42% rarely or never did. Conversely, only 21% reported at least sometimes prescribing immunosuppression to prevent future complications in lcSSc, whereas 79% rarely or never did. Over 70% of respondents indicated that they would likely treat lcSSc in the presence of tendon friction rubs, new areas of skin thickening, increasing modified Rodnan skin scores (mRSSs), or mRSSs of 15 and above. Close to half would likely prescribe immunosuppression in the presence of mRSS of 10 to 14, anti-topoisomerase I antibodies, or anti-RNA polymerase III antibodies. Interestingly, a majority of respondents would likely treat lcSSc in the presence of subclinical organ involvement, including subclinical myocardial, muscle, joint, and lung disease. The top first-line drugs of choice were mycophenolate mofetil (47%), methotrexate (28%), and hydroxychloroquine (20%). This international survey highlights significant heterogeneity among rheumatologists in the use of immunosuppressive drugs in lcSSc. High-quality research is needed to guide and harmonize the approach to management in lcSSc.

items.title: Targeted metabolic reprogramming of CD8 T cells restores immune regulation in lupus.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is characterized by pathogenic humoral autoimmunity, yet the mechanisms linking T cell dysfunction to aberrant B cell responses remain poorly defined. Here, we identify a CD8 + T cell-intrinsic metabolic defect that promotes humoral immune dysregulation in lupus. CD8 + T cells from patients with SLE exhibited elevated CD38 expression associated with reduced intracellular NAD + levels, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired cytotoxic capacity. Pharmacologic inhibition of CD38 with the small-molecule inhibitor MK-0159 restored NAD + metabolism and rescued cytotoxic function in human CD8 + T cells ex vivo. To selectively target this pathway in vivo, we developed anti-CD8 antibody-conjugated nanoparticles encapsulating MK-0159. In lupus-prone MRL/ lpr mice, CD8-targeted delivery enhanced granzyme B expression, improved degranulation, reduced plasmablast responses and autoantibody production, immune complex deposition, and renal pathology. Importantly, targeted delivery restored CD8 + T cell function without broad immune perturbation. These findings identify CD38-driven NAD + depletion as a reversible immunometabolic checkpoint limiting CD8 + T cell cytotoxic competence and support a model in which targeted restoration of cytotoxic fitness contributes to the control of humoral autoimmunity in SLE.

items.title: Keeping psoriatic arthritis case finding simple in the omics era: the continuing role of screening questionnaires.
items.abstract: Advanced imaging and multi-omics are reshaping research on the transition from psoriasis to psoriatic arthritis (PsA), but none currently provides a validated, affordable and scalable solution for routine population-level case finding. This narrative Special Report draws on focused PubMed searches and reference tracking through September 2026, supplemented by a targeted PubMed search run on 10 November 2026. We examine brief questionnaires for PsA case finding, using PURE-4 as a case study, and consider the roles of imaging and emerging molecular biomarkers. A questionnaire is most useful when a named clinical team reviews the result and arranges assessment or follow-up. Pragmatic studies should determine whether this approach leads to earlier confirmed diagnoses and better patient outcomes at a workload and cost that services can sustain, and whether imaging or candidate biomarkers improve decisions in selected patients.

items.title: Diverse clinical presentations of inflammatory myopathy in patients with familial Mediterranean fever: a case series of six patients and literature review.
items.abstract: Inflammatory myopathy has rarely been reported in patients with familial Mediterranean fever (FMF). The available literature is limited to a small number of case reports. In this case series we retrospectively evaluated six patients with FMF presenting with inflammatory myopathy and reviewed the available literature. Five patients were women, and the median age was 48.5 years (range, 27-57). Clinical presentations ranged from localized lower limb pain to progressive proximal muscle weakness. In our study, all six patients had elevated creatine kinase levels (range, 519-3462 U/L), and three had documented proximal muscle weakness. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed muscle involvement in three patients, whereas electromyography showed myopathic changes in five patients. Muscle biopsy, performed in two patients, confirmed inflammatory myopathy. Two patients exhibited dermatomyositis features. All six patients received corticosteroids, and three additionally received disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: methotrexate in two and azathioprine in one. Muscle involvement developed despite ongoing colchicine treatment in five patients; furthermore, one patient required interleukin-1 inhibition due to refractory disease, initially with anakinra and subsequently with canakinumab because of persistent inflammation and recurrent FMF attacks. Clinical improvement was reported in all six patients. This case series highlights that inflammatory myopathy should be suspected in FMF patients with muscle symptoms, particularly when supported by objective findings such as elevated muscle enzymes, imaging abnormalities, electrophysiological changes, or histopathological evidence of inflammation. Differentiation from protracted febrile myalgia syndrome and colchicine-related myopathy is important, as these conditions may require distinct therapeutic approaches. Our case series adds to the limited literature and highlights the variable clinical presentations and treatment responses of inflammatory myopathy in patients with FMF.

items.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and pulmonary outcomes in rheumatoid arthritis: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Pulmonary complications contribute substantially to morbidity and mortality in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), yet preventive strategies remain limited. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have metabolic and anti-inflammatory effects, but their association with respiratory outcomes in RA is unknown. Using electronic health record data from the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, we conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of adults with RA and type 2 diabetes mellitus who initiated GLP-1-based therapy or a DPP-4 inhibitor between January 1, 2016, and January 1, 2025. Primary coded outcomes were incident coded diagnoses of interstitial lung disease (ILD) and pulmonary hypertension (PH) over 3 years, with secondary outcomes including coded bronchiectasis, hospitalization, respiratory failure, mechanical ventilation, and all-cause mortality. Time-to-event analyses used Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models. After matching, 1,656 patients were included in each cohort. Incident ILD occurred in 42 GLP-1RA users versus 54 DPP-4i users with no significant difference (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.57-1.29, p = 0.46). GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly reduced pulmonary hypertension (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.33-0.68, p < 0.001), mechanical ventilation (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.35-0.89, p = 0.013), respiratory failure (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.58-0.96, p = 0.023), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.48-1.00, p = 0.047). No significant differences were observed for bronchiectasis or hospitalization. In patients with RA and T2DM, GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risk of pulmonary hypertension, but not incident ILD, compared with DPP-4i use. Additional reductions in respiratory failure, mechanical ventilation, and mortality warrant further prospective evaluation of GLP-1RAs in RA-related pulmonary disease.K.

items.title: [Unilateral parotid involvement revealing Sjögren's disease: Between inflammation and lymphoma].
items.abstract: Sjögren's disease is a systemic autoimmune disease in which parotid involvement is typically bilateral and symmetrical. Unilateral parotid enlargement is an unusual presentation that should raise suspicion of a lymphomatous complication. We report the case of a 75-year-old woman with a history of Hodgkin lymphoma in complete remission who presented with sicca symptoms associated with painful right parotid swelling. Ultrasonography showed heterogeneous parotid echotexture with ill-defined hypoechoic areas, without a focal mass or lymphadenopathy. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated a "salt-and-pepper" appearance and microcystic changes, without a discrete mass or diffusion restriction. 18F-FDG positron emission tomography (PET/CT) showed no pathological parotid uptake. Histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of Sjögren's disease. This case highlights the importance of an integrated clinical, biological, and imaging approach to differentiate inflammatory parotid involvement from lymphomatous complications, while PET/CT should be reserved for cases with persistent suspicion of lymphoma.

items.title: Diabetes mellitus in systemic sclerosis: clinical phenotype and cardiovascular burden in an international multicentre study.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) and diabetes mellitus (DM) share microvascular injury that may contribute to severe complications. Although DM affects approximately 10% of the general population, its prevalence and clinical phenotype in SSc remain poorly characterised. We aimed to assess the prevalence of pharmacologically treated DM in a large European SSc cohort and to investigate its association with disease phenotype and cardiovascular (CV) manifestations. We analysed 3260 patients with SSc from 9 European tertiary centres. Patients with DM were included only if receiving antidiabetic therapy. Each patient with SSc-DM was matched in each centre with three non-DM SSc controls by age (±5 years). Demographic and disease characteristics were compared at last follow-up. Among 3260 patients with SSc, 109 (3.3%) were receiving pharmacological treatment for DM. Compared with controls, patients with SSc-DM had longer disease duration (12.1 vs 6.7 years, p=0.006), higher body mass index (BMI) (25.8 vs 23.6 kg/m², p<0.001) and more frequent joint involvement (15.3% vs 6.0%, p=0.004). Total lung capacity was lower in patients with SSc-DM (83.5% vs 91.6%, p=0.027) despite similar interstitial lung disease prevalence, forced vital capacity percentage and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide percentage. Telangiectasia and gastrointestinal manifestations were less common in patients with SSc-DM. No differences were observed in digital ulcers, elevated pulmonary artery pressure or scleroderma renal crisis. BMI was the only variable that remained statistically significant in the selected multivariable model (OR 1.15, 95% CI 1.03 to 1.28, p=0.014). Crude mortality was lower in patients with SSc-DM. In this multicentre SSc cohort, 3.3% of patients were receiving pharmacological treatment for DM. Patients with SSc-DM showed a distinct clinical phenotype, with no statistically significant differences in CV burden observed between groups. Prospective studies with standardised metabolic and CV assessments are needed to clarify the relationship between DM and clinical outcomes in SSc.

items.title: Corneal Fourier harmonic analysis across the rheumatoid arthritis dry eye spectrum.
items.abstract: Autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis often affect the cornea through coexisting dry eye disease. Identifying which corneal topographic metrics best detect these changes is important for clinical monitoring and treatment decisions. While corneal Fourier harmonic analysis has been used to examine anterior dry eye surfaces, evaluation of posterior harmonic indices across the rheumatoid arthritis dry eye spectrum remains unexplored. This study compared anterior and posterior Fourier harmonic irregularities, Zernike higher-order aberrations, and standard topographic measures across healthy controls, rheumatoid arthritis without dry eye, rheumatoid arthritis with dry eye but without secondary Sjögren syndrome, and rheumatoid arthritis with secondary Sjögren syndrome. This cross-sectional study included 160 participants, with 40 in each group, who underwent corneal topography using combined Scheimpflug and Placido imaging. Fourier harmonic optical irregularity was measured for both anterior and posterior surfaces, along with Zernike higher-order aberrations. Analysis included analysis of variance with Bonferroni correction, covariance analysis adjusting for disease activity, and bootstrap receiver operating characteristic analysis. Posterior Fourier harmonic irregularity did not distinguish any group (F = 1.58, p  = 0.197, η 2  = 0.029). Anterior Fourier harmonic irregularity showed significant group differences (F = 3.85, p  = 0.011), with secondary Sjögren syndrome significantly elevated versus controls. Zernike higher-order aberrations showed the strongest group effect (H = 33.36, p  < 0.001). All significant findings survived false discovery rate correction. The central keratoconus index was the best single discriminator (area under the curve 0.812, sensitivity 72.5%, specificity 82.5% for secondary Sjögren syndrome versus controls). Zernike higher-order aberrations correlated significantly with dry eye symptom severity ( r  = 0.420, p  < 0.001). After adjustment for dry eye disease duration, the anterior and Zernike group differences were attenuated to non-significance, whereas the central keratoconus index remained significant. Posterior Fourier harmonic irregularity did not differ across the dry eye spectrum in rheumatoid arthritis. Anterior harmonic irregularity and Zernike higher-order aberrations were higher in the more severe groups, although both differences were attenuated after adjustment for dry eye disease duration.

items.title: The Oxford Grading Scale as a practical alternative for ocular assessment in the diagnosis of Sjögren's disease.
items.abstract: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disease in which ocular involvement constitutes a key component of the 2016 ACR-EULAR classification criteria. Standard ocular staining assessment relies on the Ocular Staining Score (OSS) or the van Bijsterveld score (vBS), which require lissamine green and specialized expertise. The Oxford Grading Scale (OGS) is a simple fluorescein-based alternative that may facilitate ocular surface assessment. To evaluate the agreement of the OGS with the OSS and vBS and identify clinically useful OGS thresholds for predicting fulfillment of the ocular criterion of the 2016 ACR-EULAR classification criteria. In this multi-centre cross-sectional study, 120 patients fulfilling the 2016 ACR-EULAR criteria for SjD underwent OGS, OSS, and vBS assessment. Correlation was evaluated using Spearman's coefficient and agreement using Cohen's kappa. OGS thresholds were optimized to maximize agreement with standard positivity criteria. Longitudinal changes were explored in patients with repeated evaluations. An OGS of 0 in both eyes excluded fulfillment of the ocular criterion with a negative predictive value of 100% versus the OSS and 96.9% versus the vBS, whereas an OGS ≥2.5 identified patients fulfilling the ocular criterion with a positive predictive value of 100%. Across ocular surface involvement, the OGS showed strong correlations and substantial agreement with both reference scores. Longitudinal OGS changes correlated with changes in both the OSS and vBS. The OGS offers a practical fluorescein-based triage tool for ocular involvement in SjD, with excellent rule-out performance and high rule-in value when comprehensive assessment is unavailable.

items.title: ABO*A1.02 and ABO*O.01.02 are associated with rheumatoid arthritis risk and are not modified by FUT2 secretor status.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a heterogeneous autoimmune disease. The association between ABO blood groups and RA remains inconclusive, with most studies limited to serological phenotypes and lacking molecular typing, and the modifying role of FUT2 secretor status is unclear. We enrolled 557 R A patients and 1114 healthy controls matched by age and sex. Seven ABO alleles were genotyped by optimized two-dimensional PCR (2D-PCR), and the full-length FUT2 coding region was Sanger-sequenced with an automated double-peak interpretation tool. Conditional logistic regression assessed ABO-RA associations and serological subtype heterogeneity, and tested ABO-FUT2 interaction. The 2D-PCR system achieved 100% signal interpretation across 16 ABO genotypes. FUT2 sequencing revealed seven novel variants (c.92C > G, c.611G > T, c.239G > T, c.819C > A, c.179G > T, c.768delT, and the cis-configured c.921_922insTT + c.924 A > T). Carriage of ABO*A1.02 or ABO*O.01.02 was associated with 34% (OR = 1.34, P = 0.012) and 33% (OR = 1.33, P = 0.015) increased RA risk, respectively (Bonferroni-significant). The ABO*B.01/ABO*O.01.01 genotype showed a suggestive protective signal (OR = 0.66, P = 0.044) but not in the dominant model. Serological stratification suggested suggestive trends in the RF-positive and CCP-positive subgroups, although these did not survive correction. Case-only analysis found no direct association between these genotypes and autoantibody positivity; however, this analysis cannot determine whether ABO influences autoantibody production or acts through other mechanisms. No significant ABO-FUT2 interaction was detected (LRT P = 0.539). Carriage of ABO*A1.02 or ABO*O.01.02 was associated with increased RA risk in this cohort, with suggestive trends in seropositive subtypes, and this association was not modified by FUT2 secretor status. The mechanism underlying this association remains to be determined. These variants may be candidates for future functional studies.

items.title: Impact of targeted biological and synthetic therapies on cardiovascular risk in patients with psoriatic disease or spondyloarthritis: A scoping review.
items.abstract: Patients with psoriatic disease- psoriasis (PsO), psoriatic arthritis (PsA)-and spondyloarthritis (SpA) face elevated cardiovascular (CV) risk driven by chronic systemic inflammation. We aimed to map the CV safety landscape of biological and targeted synthetic drugs (b/tsDMARDs), evaluating reported major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), intermediate metabolic markers, and surrogate indicators of vascular health. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane for randomized trials and extension studies with at least 52 weeks of cumulative exposure in PsO, PsA, and SpA. Altogether, 152 unique studies (reported across 183 publications) were included (PsO: 83; PsA: 41; SpA: 28). MACE and mortality rates remained low, predominantly clustering in individuals with high baseline CV risk. In PsO, interleukin (IL)-17 and IL-23 inhibitors showed a low hard arterial event incidence; exploratory assessments noted improved endothelial function (+2.1% flow-mediated dilation, p = 0.0022) with secukinumab, which cannot be assumed to translate into clinical event reduction. In PsA and SpA, Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors exhibited infrequent MACE reporting, with sporadic adjudicated venous thromboembolism events in selected long-term extensions. Apremilast was associated with moderate weight reduction, while tofacitinib showed dose-dependent lipid increases with a stable total/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio. Most evidence derived from long-term extension studies, carrying an inherent high risk of bias due to uncontrolled designs, patient attrition, and survivor selection. In conclusion, trial data document low absolute MACE rates, yet uncontrolled extension designs preclude definitive causal or comparative inferences. Given the systematic exclusion of multimorbid individuals, individualized baseline risk stratification and prospective cardiovascular-endpoint trials remain essential.

items.title: Hydroxychloroquine dose reduction or withdrawal and the risk of disease flare in systemic lupus erythematosus: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo quantify flare risk with reduced-dose, tapered, or withdrawn versus standard-dose hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).MethodsThis PROSPERO-registered (CRD420261503706) review followed PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science, and registries were searched through July 2026. Randomized and observational studies comparing lower/tapered/withdrawn HCQ with standard dosing and reporting flare by a validated index were eligible; risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2/Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Random-effects meta-analysis pooled estimates harmonized to hazard ratios (HRs), with fixed-effect, effect-measure-stratified, alternative-conversion, and small-sample (Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman) random-effects sensitivity analyses, subgroup analyses, exploratory restricted-cubic-spline dose-response analysis, and publication-bias testing; certainty was rated by GRADE.ResultsEleven studies (3 RCTs, 8 observational; 3,716 patients in the analytical samples) met eligibility; 10 studies reporting flare outcomes (N = 3,472) contributed to the primary synthesis. Lower/tapered/withdrawn HCQ was associated with higher flare risk (harmonized HR 1.69, 95% CI 1.33-2.15; I 2 = 60.3%; 95% prediction interval 0.87-3.27, including no effect), consistent in fixed-effect analysis (HR 1.37, 95% CI 1.23-1.52), with small-sample Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman intervals (HR 1.69, 95% CI 1.28-2.22), and in time-to-event-only (HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.18-1.99) and risk-ratio-scale (RR 1.40, 95% CI 1.19-1.65) sensitivity analyses. The randomized-trial subgroup was inconclusive (HR 1.56, 95% CI 0.89-2.74). Estimates differed across flare-severity strata (P-interaction < 0.001; moderate-to-severe flares, HR 2.47; composite all flares, HR 1.22; hospitalization for SLE, OR 4.20 from a single case-crossover study), but the strata also differed in study design, exposure, and outcome definition. An exploratory dose-response analysis of six studies suggested a gradual increase in flare risk with lower doses (RR 1.23, 95% CI 1.07-1.41, per 1 mg/kg/day decrease), without evidence of non-linearity ( P = 0.72), and could not identify a dose threshold. Nine studies had low risk of bias; GRADE certainty was very low for the overall flare estimate, whose prediction interval included no effect, moderate for moderate-to-severe flares, and very low for hospitalization.ConclusionsReducing or withdrawing HCQ was associated with more flares; although certainty for the overall estimate was very low and its prediction interval included no effect, moderate-certainty evidence indicated increased moderate-to-severe flare risk, supporting individualized, monitored de-escalation over routine discontinuation.

items.title: Severe proliferative lupus nephritis in two transgender women with long-term feminizing hormone exposure.
items.abstract: BackgroundEstrogen is implicated in the female preponderance of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), but sustained exogenous estrogen exposure in a 46,XY individual cannot be studied in a trial, and only three cases of biopsy-proven lupus nephritis have been reported in transgender women on gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT).CasesCase 1, aged 31, had begun GAHT about a decade before presentation and had a first- and second-degree family history of SLE. She had already been lost to endocrine follow-up when lupus-specific antibodies were documented at 25; the rheumatology consultation requested then did not take place, and she continued oral estradiol unassessed for 6 years. She presented with nephrotic syndrome and class IV+V nephritis (NIH activity index 20/24). After remission, an unsupervised switch from transdermal back to oral estradiol was followed within 1 month by a rise in proteinuria from 0.5 to 3.1 g/24 h, which returned to 0.65 g/24 h 3 weeks later with the prednisone taper paused and no other change in treatment. Case 2, aged 38, reported estrogen-progestogen use from the age of 18 for about 15 years, discontinued about 5 years before presentation, at doses she could not specify and with no hormone level available. She presented with oligo-anuric acute kidney injury requiring hemodialysis, polyserositis, hemolytic anemia and class IV nephritis. Microangiopathic hemolysis (schistocytes, haptoglobin ≤10 mg/dL from day 8, normal ADAMTS13 activity, platelets 144 ×10 9 /L at onset) was treated with corticosteroids, rituximab and, from day 14, eculizumab under a working diagnosis of atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome; the biopsy, taken after treatment had begun, showed no microangiopathic lesion. She became dialysis-independent after 36 days and reached partial remission.ConclusionsTwo cases cannot establish a causal role for estrogen: in neither can cumulative exposure be quantified, in Case 2 it had ended about 5 years before onset, and in Case 1 family history, autoantibodies present 6 years before diagnosis and the absence of rheumatological assessment in that interval explain the severity at presentation at least as well. The hypothesis they raise is that gender-affirming estrogen exposure may unmask or accelerate SLE in predisposed individuals. No guideline recommends autoimmune screening before or during GAHT, and both patients had taken estrogen for years without contact with care. Recording a family history of SLE at the start of GAHT, and a low threshold for urinalysis and serology when symptoms appear, might be warranted.

items.title: Add-on DMARDs and interstitial lung disease in methotrexate-treated rheumatoid arthritis: A prevalent new-user design study using a large regional Japanese claims database.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by joint inflammation, destruction, and systemic complications including interstitial lung disease (ILD). We conducted a prevalent new-user design study using the Shizuoka Kokuho Database in Japan to examine ILD incidence after addition of non-methotrexate (MTX) disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) to MTX therapy. Patients receiving sulfasalazine, tacrolimus hydrate, etanercept, iguratimod, bucillamine, or denosumab were compared with time-conditioned MTX controls using propensity score matching. Death was treated as a competing event. Among 63,952 patients with RA, 11,430 who received MTX were included in the source cohort. Gray's test indicated higher cumulative ILD incidence for sulfasalazine, tacrolimus hydrate, and bucillamine than for their matched controls (p = 0.0034, 0.0393, and 0.0477, respectively). Corresponding cause-specific hazard ratios were 1.79 (95% CI 1.21-2.66), 1.53 (1.02-2.31), and 1.75 (0.998-3.07), respectively. These findings are exploratory associations and do not establish drug-specific causality.

items.title: Redox-regulated immunomodulatory mechanisms of mycophenolate mofetil in a lupus-like disease.
items.abstract: Lupus-like autoimmune disease remains a severe, hard-to-manage complication after allogeneic immune cell transfer, with limited targeted therapies. While mycophenolate mofetil shows observable clinical benefit, its immunometabolic mechanisms in tissue-resident macrophages remain poorly defined. In this established murine lupus-like disease model, recipient mice received splenocytes from lupus-prone donors, with parallel comparisons between reactive oxygen species (ROS)-deficient, ROS-normal and conditional APOBEC3 knockout groups. We applied standardized in vivo mycophenolate mofetil dosing and ex vivo mycophenolic acid treatment, alongside high-resolution magnetic particle profiling, flow cytometry, ELISA, histology and RNA sequencing for systematic assessment. Mycophenolate mofetil significantly induced macrophage functional reprogramming, suppressed antigen-specific immune activation, lowered interferon-γ and IgG2b autoantibody levels, and alleviated pulmonary fibrosis, while APOBEC3-mediated cytosine deamination in macrophages was regulated by ROS signaling. These findings indicate that mycophenolate mofetil ameliorates lupus-like autoimmunity via ROS-dependent and independent DNA regulatory pathways, providing a new mechanistic basis for improving inflammation-directed immunomodulatory strategies.
