items.title: Long-Term Effectiveness, Treatment Persistence, and Safety of Upadacitinib in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis in Canadian Real-World Practice: Final Results from the CLOSE-UP Study.
items.abstract: Upadacitinib is an oral, selective Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor proven effective and well tolerated in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in six randomized clinical trials. The objective of the CLOSE-UP study was to evaluate the long-term real-world effectiveness and safety of upadacitinib among Canadian patients with prior exposure to conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARD), biologic (b)DMARDs, and targeted-synthetic (ts)DMARDs in routine clinical practice. CLOSE-UP was a 24-month, prospective, multicenter, observational study in adults with RA treated with upadacitinib 15 mg daily, with the decision to initiate upadacitinib made before study participation. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving Disease Activity Score in 28 Joints using C-reactive protein (DAS28-CRP) < 2.6 at 6 months. Patients were followed for 24 months to assess the long-term effectiveness of upadacitinib on disease activity, pain, fatigue, physical function, and other clinical and patient-reported outcomes. In total, 412 patients were analyzed (47.1% bio-naïve, 41.3% bio-experienced, 10.7% tsDMARD-experienced), of which 309 completed the 24-month study period. At baseline, 87.4% had DAS28-CRP > 3.2. By month 24, 74.7% (210/281) of patients achieved DAS28-CRP < 2.6 and 67.5% remained on upadacitinib treatment. Treatment responses were similar across prior-treatment subgroups and between patients receiving upadacitinib monotherapy and those receiving upadacitinib in combination with csDMARD. Clinically important improvements in pain, fatigue, and physical function were observed. By month 24, 48.8% of patients using corticosteroids at baseline had discontinued them. No new safety signals were identified. This real-world study showed that upadacitinib was effective in reducing disease activity and improving patient-reported outcomes, with responses achieved at 6 months maintained through 2 years. No new safety signals were observed supporting a favorable benefit-risk profile for patients treated with upadacitinib. Response rates were generally similar across prior bDMARD/tsDMARD exposure groups and according to concomitant csDMARD use. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04574492. Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic inflammatory disease that causes joint pain, swelling, stiffness, fatigue, and difficulty with everyday activities. Although many treatments are available, some individuals do not respond to treatment or may lose their response over time. Upadacitinib is a once‑daily oral treatment for rheumatoid arthritis. CLOSE‑UP was a Canadian observational study that followed 412 adults with moderate‑to‑severe rheumatoid arthritis who started upadacitinib treatment in routine clinical practice for up to 2 years. Patients had different prior treatment histories, including no prior biologic therapy and previous biologic or targeted treatments. Upadacitinib was prescribed either alone or with other conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARDs). This final analysis focused on longer-term outcomes after the first 6 months of treatment. Among participants with assessments available at later visits, improvements in disease activity, pain, fatigue, and physical function were observed through 2 years. About two-thirds of participants remained on upadacitinib at 2 years. Among participants using corticosteroids at baseline and with medication information available at Month 24, approximately half had discontinued corticosteroids. No new safety signals were identified during the real-world study. These findings provide additional real-world information on upadacitinib treatment over 24 months in Canadian clinical practice.

items.title: Self-Dissociating Albumin Nanoclusters for Passive Lymph Node-Targeted Inverse Vaccination in a Rheumatoid Arthritis Model.
items.abstract: Engineering lymph node-targeted tolerogenic nanomaterials requires simultaneous antigen-drug coloading and efficient lymphatic transport. However, conventional biocompatible nanoparticles with static architectures often face a size-dependent trade-off: larger particles enable cargo coloading but drain inefficiently to lymph nodes, whereas smaller particles favor lymphatic transport but have limited cargo versatility. Here, a size-transformable, self-dissociating albumin nanocluster inverse vaccine is introduced to address this materials design trade-off. Citrullinated peptide antigens are conjugated to human serum albumin, and rapamycin (RAPA) is coloaded using ball-milling technology to generate 200-300 nm nanoclusters. After subcutaneous injection, the nanoclusters dissociate into sub-10 nm albumin-based units, enabling passive lymphatic transport and accumulation in draining lymph nodes while maintaining coordinated antigen-RAPA codelivery. In vitro mechanistic studies show that the nanoclusters induce a tolerogenic dendritic cell phenotype and promote antigen-specific immune regulation. In a collagen-induced arthritis mouse model, weekly administration attenuates synovial inflammation, humoral autoimmune responses, bone erosion, and cartilage degradation while expanding Foxp3+ regulatory T cells. These findings establish self-dissociation-mediated size transformation as a functional materials strategy for lymph node-targeted antigen-specific immune tolerance and tolerogenic nanomedicine.

items.title: Radiosynoviorthesis in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Although radiosynoviorthesis (RSO) has been used to treat rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for over 70 years, its precise role within contemporary RA treatment algorithms remains variable, particularly in the era of biologic and targeted synthetic therapies. This systematic review evaluated the efficacy and safety of RSO in RA through randomized controlled trials (RCTs). MEDLINE and Embase were systematically searched for RCTs assessing RSO in RA up to January 1, 2026. Eligible studies were summarized according to efficacy and safety outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Collaboration's tool. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251174356). Sixteen RCTs including 834 RA patients were identified. Most studies (N.=10) focused on treatment of the knee joint, and the most frequently used radiopharmaceutical was [ 90 Y]yttrium (N.=9 trials, either as a single radiopharmaceutical [N.=6] or alongside another radionuclide [N.=3]). In seven trials, RSO was administered in combination with corticosteroids. RSO was most commonly compared with intra-articular corticosteroid injections (N.=10) and placebo (saline) injections (N.=3). Of the corticosteroid trials, three reported greater efficacy for RSO, one showed superiority of RSO plus corticosteroids over RSO alone, and six found no significant differences between RSO and corticosteroids. All three placebo-controlled trials demonstrated superior outcomes with RSO. Adverse events associated with RSO were generally mild, transient, and manageable. Available RCTs suggest that RSO is an effective and well-tolerated treatment option for RA. However, the limited number of high-quality trials and the variability of findings underscore the need for further robust, large-scale studies to define its role in clinical practice.

items.title: Dual-morphology nanoparticles attenuating neutrophil recruitment for rheumatoid arthritis mitigation.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease in which neutrophils serve as key regulators of inflammatory progression and represent promising therapeutic targets for RA intervention. Different from conventional single-target interventions, we developed a drug delivery approach based on dual-morphology nanoparticles for neutrophil regulation. Exploiting morphology-dependent biodistribution, discoidal nanoparticles, benefiting from their unique aspect ratio, evaded immune clearance, homed to inflamed joints via sialic acid-mediated targeting, and disrupted P-selectin-mediated neutrophil rolling and spreading. In parallel, rod-shaped nanoparticles are preferentially internalized by neutrophils, releasing piceatannol to suppress Syk phosphorylation and attenuate β2 integrin-associated signaling, thereby reducing neutrophil adhesion and transendothelial migration. In a collagen-induced arthritis mouse model, the simultaneous injection of dual-morphology nanoparticles markedly prevented neutrophil recruitment and mitigated joint destruction. These findings demonstrate that morphology-guided nanoparticle delivery strategies enable coordinated neutrophil behavior modulation and represent a promising approach for RA therapy.

items.title: Surgical Sequencing of Vertebral Column Decancellation Osteotomy and Total Hip Arthroplasty in Ankylosing Spondylitis: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: This article describes the staged use of vertebral column decancellation (VCD) and total hip arthroplasty (THA) in patients with ankylosing spondylitis and combined spinal and hip deformities. The workflow includes preoperative assessment of spinal alignment, pelvic orientation, hip ankylosis, and positioning feasibility; multidisciplinary determination of the operative sequence; procedural planning and performance of VCD and THA; staged postoperative rehabilitation; and standardized radiographic and functional assessment after completion of both procedures. The workflow was retrospectively evaluated in 50 patients treated between January 2012 and December 2021, including 18 who underwent VCD first and 32 who underwent THA first. Postoperative outcomes were analyzed using baseline-adjusted multivariable regression with heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors, with false discovery rate correction applied within prespecified outcome families. Both treatment sequences resulted in substantial improvements in spinal alignment, hip range of motion, and functional scores. After adjustment, the VCD-first sequence was associated with a lower postoperative kyphosis Cobb angle, a lower sagittal vertical axis, and less femoral stem subsidence. In contrast, adjusted differences in pelvic parameters, hip range of motion, and functional scores were no longer statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Complication proportions did not differ significantly between the groups. These retrospective findings demonstrate the application and clinical outcomes of the staged procedural workflow but do not establish the causal superiority or comparative safety of either operative sequence.

items.title: Molecular Docking and Molecular Dynamics-Based Investigation of the Potential Anti-Inflammatory and Cell-Survival Regulatory Mechanisms of Dapansutrile in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterised by persistent synovial inflammation, progressive cartilage and bone destruction, and disability. Existing therapies can be limited by adverse effects and cost, and additional treatment approaches remain of interest. Dapansutrile (OLT1177) is an orally active, selective inhibitor of the NLRP3 inflammasome that has shown anti-inflammatory activity and good tolerability in early clinical studies. Whether dapansutrile might also interact with other RA-related proteins has not been examined specifically in RA. This study used computational approaches to generate hypotheses about the potential mechanisms of dapansutrile in RA. RA-related genes from GeneCards were screened (relevance score ≥23); protein-protein interaction networks were built with STRING and Cytoscape, and gene ontology and pathway enrichment with DAVID. AutoDock Vina docking against 46 key targets identified the four best-scoring proteins (MMP1, NLRP3, TLR4 and SAA1), which underwent 50 ns AMBER molecular dynamics simulations assessing complex stability, hydrogen bonding and MM/GBSA binding free energy. Of 4,877 genes, 82 core and 49 key targets were retained; enrichment yielded 317 gene ontology terms and 70 KEGG pathways (P<0.05) centred on immune and cytokine signalling. Docking scores fell within a narrow range (-2.5 to -4.9 kcal/mol): MMP1 -4.9, NLRP3 -4.6, TLR4 -4.3 and SAA1 -4.1. The NLRP3 and MMP1 complexes remained comparatively stable, whereas the SAA1 and TLR4 complexes did not converge and lost hydrogen bonds. MM/GBSA energies were -38.53 (MMP1), -12.85 (NLRP3), -10.05 (SAA1) and -6.50 (TLR4) kcal/mol, but ligand-efficiency analysis flagged the MMP1 value (4.82 kcal/mol per heavy atom) as an artefact. These computations support an interaction with NLRP3 consistent with the established pharmacology of dapansutrile and raise MMP1 as an untested hypothesis, whereas the predicted interactions with SAA1 and TLR4 remained unsupported. Being purely in silico, all predictions require experimental validation before therapeutic inference.

items.title: Dual positive-feedback loops and a bidirectional lactate rheostat converging on the cGAS-STING pathway in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA), with persistent synovitis and irreversible joint damage, shows one-third primary or secondary non-response to biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. We synthesize evidence and propose two positive-feedback loops (Loop 1: NETosis-inflammation; Loop 3: mtDNA-mitophagy) and a bidirectional lactate rheostat (Loop 2) of unresolved sign, converging on cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING). Loop 1 initiates innate inflammation via neutrophil extracellular trap-derived DNA. Loop 2, the most speculative, proposes that glycolysis-driven lactate remodels cGAS via AARS1/2-mediated lactylation; because this modification can inhibit cGAS or stabilize it by impeding MARCHF5 ubiquitination, its net RA direction is unresolved and may be anti-inflammatory. Loop 2's pro-inflammatory output rests on better-supported lactate-induced mtDNA release fueling cGAS ligand supply (Loop 3 crosstalk); cGAS stabilization remains an unvalidated extrapolation from SLE monocytes, tumors, and in vitro data. Loop 3 may amplify inflammation via TNF-α-dependent repression of PINK1-governed mitophagy, causing cytosolic mitochondrial DNA leakage. An adaptive output-and-reinforcement layer (ACPA/RF, B cells, TPH/Th17 cells, immune complexes) links innate sensing to autoimmune perpetuation. If validated, Loop 1-3 crosstalk with this sign-unresolved rheostat would establish self-sustaining inflammatory machinery explaining chronic progression and anti-TNF non-response. We assess druggability-cGAS-STING antagonists, peptidylarginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) inhibitors, monocarboxylate transporter (MCT) blockers, PINK1 agonists, bromodomain and extra-terminal domain (BET) modulators-and propose biomarker-guided stratified combination pharmacology, hypothesizing that single-loop monotherapy may be vulnerable to compensatory activation. All biomarker cutoffs and combination regimens-including PAD4, MCT, and BET inhibitor triple combination-remain untested in animal models and unvalidated in prospective human cohorts, and none is clinically actionable. Systemic STING blockade may disrupt B-cell tolerance and exacerbate humoral autoimmunity; myeloid-selective strategies and human-validated (non-Cys91) antagonists are therefore favored, though untested. An associated FLS epigenetic imprinting module is a proposed loop-agnostic target in refractory disease.

items.title: Evaluating the association between serum phosphorus levels and MASLD in Chinese adults: focusing on males with gout.
items.abstract: The coexistence and interaction of gout and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) may complicate risk assessment. This study examined the association between serum phosphorus levels and MASLD in men with gout. We conducted a cross-sectional study of 978 hospitalized patients with gout. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the association between serum phosphorus and MASLD, with serum phosphorus analyzed as both a continuous variable and categorical quartiles. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was used to examine the dose-response relationship, and subgroup analyses were performed to assess interactions. The incremental value of serum phosphorus was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC). Higher serum phosphorus levels were associated with a greater prevalence of MASLD. In multivariable logistic regression, serum phosphorus was significantly associated with MASLD (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.09-1.53, p = 0.003). When serum phosphorus was analyzed by quartiles, the OR for the fourth quartile versus the lowest quartile was 2.29 (95% CI 1.45-3.64, p < 0.001). RCS analysis indicated a linear relationship between serum phosphorus and MASLD, with no significant interactions in subgroup analyses. Including serum phosphorus in the basic model increased the ROC AUC to 0.719. These findings indicate a positive association between serum phosphorus and MASLD in male patients with gout.

items.title: Case Report: Coexisting antisynthetase syndrome and malignancy - a focused discussion of possible immunological links.
items.abstract: Antisynthetase syndrome (ASSD) is an autoimmune disorder classified within the spectrum of idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIMs), characterized by specific autoantibodies directed against aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases and variable combinations of interstitial lung disease (ILD), myositis, arthritis, and other systemic features. Current risk-stratification frameworks classify ASSD as a comparatively low-risk phenotype for occult malignancy relative to dermatomyositis. However, this "low-risk" label is derived from population averages and may not adequately capture the risk borne by specific ASSD subsets, particularly older patients with systemic inflammatory features and low creatine phosphokinase (CPK) levels, in whom recent multicenter cohorts report a several-fold increase in cancer incidence. We report two patients with ASSD diagnosed in temporal association with malignancy: a 36-year-old woman with anti-Jo-1-positive inflammatory myopathy and arthritis concurrent with grade 2 infiltrating ductal breast carcinoma (T1c N0 M0), and a 61-year-old man with anti-PL-12-positive ILD, arthritis, mechanic's hands and fever diagnosed in the setting of a poorly differentiated gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (T4N3M0). In the first patient, autoimmune manifestations improved alongside oncological control and relapsed synchronously with metastatic recurrence, only to remit again after oncological retreatment without escalation of immunosuppression - a pattern compatible with a paraneoplastic phenomenon. In the second patient, advanced malignancy and diagnostic complexity culminated in a fatal outcome. These observations do not, in isolation, establish a causal or pathogenic relationship between ASSD and cancer. However, taken together with recent cohort data suggesting that cancer-associated myositis (CAM) may be more prevalent in ASSD than previously appreciated, they argue against an overly reassuring interpretation of ASSD´s malignancy risk. We further discuss, as an explicitly hypothesis-generating avenue, how oncogenic dysregulation of aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase expression, transcriptional control, and non-canonical signaling functions in tumor cells could theoretically create a substrate for immune cross-reactivity - a mechanistic hypothesis that remains open and should be the subject of translational investigation.

items.title: Case Report: Telitacicept therapy for podocytic infolding glomerulopathy associated with Sjögren's syndrome.
items.abstract: Podocytic infolding glomerulopathy (PIG) is a rare ultrastructural glomerular lesion associated with systemic autoimmune disease and has no standardized treatment. Sjögren's syndrome is characterized by B-cell hyperactivity, autoantibody production, and persistent plasma-cell survival. Telitacicept is a fusion protein that neutralizes B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL). A 54-year-old woman presented with nephrotic syndrome, including 24-h urinary protein excretion of 14.841 g, serum albumin of 16.6 g/L, and serum creatinine of 72.3 μmol/L. Longstanding dry mouth and dry eyes, ANA 1:1,000, anti-SSA/Ro, anti-SSB/La, and anti-Ro52 positivity, elevated IgG, and exclusion of relevant alternative conditions supported a clinical diagnosis of Sjögren's syndrome. Objective ocular and salivary-gland tests required for formal fulfillment of the 2016 ACR/EULAR classification criteria were not performed owing to patient refusal and prioritization of renal disease management. Kidney biopsy showed mild mesangial-cell and matrix proliferation with segmental glomerular basement membrane (GBM) thickening; immunofluorescence showed trace granular IgG deposition along glomerular capillary loops, with negative C3, IgG1-4, PLA2R, and THSD7A staining. Electron microscopy demonstrated podocyte swelling, vacuolar degeneration, diffuse foot-process effacement with microvillous transformation, and multiple round membranous structures within the GBM with focal dissolution, supporting PIG. Proteinuria remained approximately 4.3-5.6 g/24 h during the 3 months immediately before telitacicept despite glucocorticoids, tacrolimus, Tripterygium wilfordii glycosides, canagliflozin, and supportive therapy. Telitacicept 160 mg once weekly was added in May 2023 and, after approximately 8 months, was empirically changed to 160 mg once monthly. Proteinuria subsequently declined into the subnephrotic range and serum albumin recovered while glucocorticoids and later tacrolimus were tapered and discontinued. At the final follow-up, proteinuria was 1.235 g/24 h, serum albumin was 38.3 g/L, and serum creatinine was 65 μmol/L. During 32 months of follow-up after telitacicept initiation, no serious infection requiring hospitalization or treatment-limiting adverse reaction was recorded. Telitacicept initiation was temporally associated with proteinuria reduction and albumin recovery maintained during immunosuppressive de-escalation. Because of concomitant therapies and the single-case design, an independent causal effect of telitacicept cannot be established. Telitacicept may have contributed to the observed improvement, and this observation should be considered hypothesis-generating.

items.title: Exploring the relationship between Porphyromonas gingivalis in periodontitis and rheumatoid arthritis severity: a cross-sectional pilot study.
items.abstract: This study aimed to explore the relationship between site-specific Porphyromonas gingivalis ( P. gingivalis ) levels, PSR-defined periodontitis status, and the clinical severity of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). In total, 28 patients with RA were included. The erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) was quantified using the Wintrobe method. Serum levels of C-reactive protein (CRP) and rheumatoid factor (RF) were measured via turbidimetric assay, while anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibodies were determined by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Periodontal diagnosis was performed using a simplified Periodontal Screening and Recording (PSR), assessing bleeding on probing (BOP) and probing depth (PD), detection and quantification of site-specific P. gingivalis were carried out using qPCR. Bivariate analysis revealed a statistically significant difference between groups for ESR, which was higher in the PSR-based periodontitis group than in the non-periodontitis group(26.5 mm/h vs. 21 mm/h, p  = 0.04). Additionally, positive correlations were observed between site-specific P. gingivalis levels and both joint erosion(JE) (rho = 0.45; p  = 0.02), and radiological grade (RG) (rho = 0.42; p  = 0.04). This small pilot study observed exploratory trends suggesting that patients with co-occurring rheumatoid arthritis and PSR-defined periodontitis harboring site-specific P orphyromonas gingivalis may present with elevated disease activity. However, sample size constraints and non-significant associations following multiplicity corrections preclude confirming direct links with joint degradation, requiring validation in prospective studies using full-mouth diagnostic staging and representative microbiological sampling.

items.title: Cutaneous manifestations as a marker of disease activity in relapsing adult-onset Still's disease: Case report: A case report.
items.abstract: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a rare autoinflammatory disorder with variable cutaneous manifestations. We report a case of relapsing AOSD in which cutaneous findings paralleled disease activity. A 54-year-old male presented with recurrent fevers, leukocytosis, and hyperferritinemia, with a history of a transient evanescent eruption. Extensive evaluation was unrevealing. During hospitalization, he developed severe pulmonary hypertension. After meeting Yamaguchi criteria, he was treated with corticosteroids and anakinra, an IL-1 inhibitor. At follow up, lapses in therapy were associated with recurrence of a faint eruption that resolved rapidly with resumption of anakinra, paralleling improvement in systemic symptoms and inflammatory markers. This case highlights the association between cutaneous findings and disease activity in AOSD.

items.title: Combination of labial salivary gland focus score and serum complement 3 for identifying interstitial lung disease in primary Sjögren's disease: A single-center retrospective study.
items.abstract: ObjectiveThis study aimed to assess disease-related variables that could identify the presence of interstitial lung disease in primary Sjögren's disease and evaluate the discriminative performance of a combined model incorporating these variables.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cross-sectional study consecutively enrolled 81 patients with primary Sjögren's disease at Xijing Hospital from January 2022 to March 2025. All patients underwent chest high-resolution computed tomography and labial minor salivary gland biopsy. Demographic data, labial salivary gland focus scores, and serological characteristics, including rheumatoid factor, anti-SSA/SSB antibodies, and complement levels, were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analysis were performed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) 26.0 and R 4.6.1.ResultsAmong the 81 enrolled patients with primary Sjögren's disease, 46 (56.8%) were diagnosed with combined interstitial lung disease based on high-resolution computed tomography. Compared with patients without interstitial lung disease, patients with interstitial lung disease had a higher labial gland focus scores (median 2.0 vs. 1.2, p = 0.009) and a higher serum complement 3 level (p = 0.028). Multivariable logistic regression showed that higher focus scores and higher serum complement 3 levels were independently associated with the presence of combined interstitial lung disease in patients with primary Sjögren's disease (focus scores: odds ratio = 1.381, 95% confidence interval: 1.002-1.902, p = 0.049; complement 3: odds ratio = 1.028, 95% confidence interval: 1.003-1.053, p = 0.029). In the receiver operating characteristic analysis, the combined model incorporating focus scores and complement 3 yielded an area under the curve of 0.733 (95% confidence interval: 0.613-0.852; p = 0.001), numerically higher than that of focus scores alone (0.669) or complement 3 alone (0.681), although the differences were not statistically significant (DeLong p = 0.24 and p = 0.31).ConclusionHigher labial gland focus scores values and serum complement 3 levels were independently associated with concomitant interstitial lung disease in patients with primary Sjögren's disease, and a model combining the two showed moderate discriminative ability.

items.title: Association Between Rheumatoid Arthritis Disease Duration and Periodontal Health: A Retrospective Observational Study.
items.abstract: Background Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory disease that may be associated with alterations in periodontal health and disease. However, the relationship between RA duration and periodontal status remains incompletely characterized. This study evaluated the association between RA duration and periodontal disease. Methodology This retrospective observational study included 180 patients with RA. Patients were categorized according to RA duration as <5 years, 5-10 years, and >10 years, with 60 patients in each group. Periodontal parameters included the plaque index, bleeding on probing (BOP), probing pocket depth (PPD), clinical attachment level (CAL), and the number of missing teeth. Demographic and rheumatologic variables were also extracted. Between-group comparisons were performed using appropriate parametric and nonparametric tests. Multivariable linear regression was used to assess associations between RA duration and continuous periodontal outcomes, while multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate severe periodontitis. Results Patients with RA for a duration of >10 years had significantly higher plaque index, BOP, PPD, and CAL than those with shorter disease duration. The mean plaque index increased from 0.99 ± 0.33 to 1.90 ± 0.29, BOP from 21.49 ± 9.23% to 53.16 ± 9.25%, PPD from 2.44 ± 0.48 mm to 4.11 ± 0.36 mm, and CAL from 1.67 ± 0.57 mm to 5.14 ± 0.85 mm (all p < 0.001). The number of missing teeth increased from 1.20 ± 1.10 to 4.60 ± 1.40 (p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, smoking status, diabetes mellitus, body mass index, plaque index, and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug use, RA duration remained significantly associated with CAL (B = 0.158, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.130-0.185; p < 0.001) and PPD (B = 0.073, 95% CI: 0.056-0.090; p < 0.001). However, RA duration was not significantly associated with severe periodontitis (odds ratio = 1.01, 95% CI: 0.94-1.08; p = 0.761). Conclusions Longer RA duration was associated with progressively poorer periodontal health, particularly greater periodontal pocketing and attachment loss. Regular periodontal assessment may be warranted in patients with long-standing RA. These findings highlight the potential value of integrating periodontal evaluation into the routine management of patients with prolonged RA. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship between RA duration and periodontal deterioration.

items.title: Physical Therapy and Rehabilitation Interventions for Pain and Dysfunction in Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory condition associated with pain, stiffness, impaired physical function, joint damage, and reduced quality of life. Rehabilitation forms an integral part of RA management, with treatment approaches directed toward maintaining mobility, physical capacity, hand function, and participation in daily activities. This systematic review synthesized evidence from randomized controlled trials evaluating contemporary rehabilitation approaches for adults with RA. Searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, PEDro, CINAHL, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library for trials published between January 2016 and June 2026. The date range was selected to focus the review on contemporary rehabilitation approaches and digital health interventions while maintaining coverage of recent clinical evidence. In total, 15 randomized controlled trials met the predefined eligibility criteria. Interventions included aquatic exercise, aerobic and resistance training, high-intensity interval training, individualized exercise programs, hand exercise, manual therapy, mobilization with movement, therapeutic hand massage, and selected digital health and self-management approaches, including telehealth, smartphone-based care, and digital education programs. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) framework. Findings varied according to the intervention, comparator, outcome, and assessment time point. Exercise-based approaches showed benefits in selected measures of physical capacity, fatigue, pain, and function, although effects were not consistently observed across all outcomes. Hand rehabilitation and manual therapy showed improvements in selected measures of hand function, strength, or pain, while some comparisons demonstrated no additional benefit. Digital and self-management approaches showed potential benefits for selected aspects of disease management, patient engagement, and quality of life. Because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity across interventions, populations, comparators, outcomes, and follow-up periods, findings were synthesized using a structured narrative approach rather than quantitative meta-analysis. Overall, the findings indicate that contemporary physical therapy, rehabilitation, and selected digital or self-management approaches may provide potential benefits for selected outcomes in adults with RA. However, variation in intervention protocols, comparators, outcome measures, follow-up periods, and risk-of-bias judgments limits direct comparison across trials. Further well-designed randomized controlled trials with standardized outcome assessment and adequate follow-up are warranted.

items.title: IgG4-related endobronchial lung disease and HIV: a case report and review of the literature.
items.abstract: Immunoglobulin G4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is a systemic inflammatory disorder which typically presents as multiorgan infiltration by polyclonal IgG4-positive plasma cells and responds well to immunosuppression such as systemic corticosteroids. The co-occurrence of IgG4-RD among patients infected with HIV is extremely uncommon and has only been described in a few case reports. We hereby present a 75-years old male with well controlled HIV, who presented with endobronchial mass ultimately diagnosed as IgG4-RD. He received multimodal treatment, which included both local bronchoscopic interventions (cryo-ablation and stent insertion) as well as systemic steroids, with an excellent therapeutic response. Our literature review identified 19 additional case reports of IgG4-RD among individuals with HIV, with significant heterogeneity in clinical presentation, organ involvement patterns, level of HIV control, and serum concentrations of IgG4. Most patients received specific therapy, including steroids, with generally favorable outcomes. This report highlights the possible occurrence of IgG4-RD in HIV patients, despite being immunocompromised, and the possibility of safely treating such cases with immunosuppressive medications.

items.title: Olfactory dysfunction in systemic sclerosis: a cross-sectional study and scoping review.
items.abstract: Olfactory dysfunction has been reported in autoimmune diseases, but its relationship with disease-specific features remains incompletely defined. We aimed to determine its prevalence in systemic sclerosis (SSc), assess clinical correlations and contextualise findings through a scoping review across connective tissue diseases (CTDs). We conducted a single-centre cross-sectional study (January-March 2020) including 56 patients fulfilling the 2013 American College of Rheumatology/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology criteria for SSc. Olfaction was assessed using the European Test of Olfactory Capabilities (ETOC). Sinonasal status was evaluated with the Lund-Kennedy (LK) score and Sino-Nasal Outcome Test-22. Disease severity and activity were assessed using modified Rodnan Skin Score, Medsger scale, revised European Scleroderma Trials and Research Group activity index and Scleroderma Health Assessment Questionnaire, and mood with Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. A scoping review of PubMed and Embase (through September 2025) identified studies on olfactory dysfunction in CTDs. Median ETOC score was 28 (25-30). Hyposmia was present in 41% and anosmia in 2%, both associated with older age and higher LK scores (p<0.05). Olfactory function negatively correlated with age (r=-0.37, p=0.005) and LK score (r=-0.39, p=0.003), but not with disease severity, duration, quality of life or mood.The review included 19 studies (primary Sjögren's disease (pSD) n=12, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) n=5, SSc n=2). Hyposmia prevalence ranged from 15% to 59% and anosmia from 3% to 13%, with associations including age, disease activity, mucosal dryness (pSD), neuropsychiatric involvement (SLE) and depression or brain changes (SSc). Olfactory dysfunction is common in SSc and CTDs and appears to be partly related to age and sinonasal inflammation rather than overall disease severity, highlighting an under-recognised clinical feature.

items.title: Benchmarking gastrointestinal involvement in systemic sclerosis: practical insights and unmet needs from a tertiary referral centre.
items.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) involvement is almost universal in patients with systemic sclerosis (SSc). Our aim was to benchmark and describe GI involvement in SSc, exploring potential clinical associations including in patients with myositis overlap. Retrospective, cross-sectional study. Patients attending a UK tertiary referral centre for SSc in 2024. Adult (n=149) patients with an established clinical diagnosis of SSc (excluding a very early diagnosis of SSc). Subgroup analysis of those with myositis overlap. None; observational study design, including description of prescribed treatments. Relevant patient and disease-related data were obtained from electronic patient record review. We developed a simple clinician-assessed score to assess GI symptoms burden: 0 ('none'), 1 ('effectively managed') or 2 ('unmanaged'). Descriptive statistics and appropriate testing were used to describe the data. We included 149 patients (female, 86%), most (71%) had limited cutaneous SSc and 13% had myositis. Median (IQR) SSc-disease duration was 11.1 (43.0) years. Over half (61%) had current GI symptoms (score 1 or 2); 43% had unmanaged symptoms (score 2). The most common symptoms were reflux (32%) and dysphagia (28%). Proton pump inhibitor use was high (81%). Both anticentromere (p=<0.001) and anti-Scl70 (p=0.01) antibodies were associated with GI symptoms, but not anti-RNA polymerase (p=0.78). No statistically significant association was seen between GI involvement and interstitial lung disease (p=0.06), pulmonary hypertension (p=0.42) or digital ulcers (p=0.84). No association was observed between GI involvement and disease duration (p=0.44). Over half (63%) with myositis overlap had GI involvement. GI involvement is common and often symptomatic in SSc, but not over-represented in patients with myositis overlap. Research is needed to understand natural history, pathobiology and heterogeneity, including early intervention strategies. NCA reference: 25HIP20.

items.title: Systemic sclerosis spectrum from the Egyptian College of Rheumatology: a nationwide observational study.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare, heterogeneous autoimmune disease characterised by vasculopathy, immune activation and progressive fibrosis, resulting in multiorgan involvement and significant morbidity and mortality. This nationwide multicentre cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate the demographic, clinical, serological and therapeutic profiles of Egyptian SSc patients, enhancing understanding of disease patterns, comorbidities and management strategies. A total of 1080 patients fulfilling the 2013 American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism classification criteria for SSc were recruited from rheumatology centres across 18 Egyptian governorates. Data on demographics, clinical features, autoantibody profiles and treatments were collected and analysed. The mean patient age was 40.5±11.5 years, with a pronounced female predominance (88.4%, F: M ratio 7.6:1). Limited cutaneous SSc (lcSSc) and diffuse cutaneous SSc were equally represented, while overlap syndromes occurred in 6.7%, most frequently with rheumatoid arthritis, myositis and systemic lupus erythematosus. Juvenile-onset SSc was identified in 5%, predominantly affecting females. Pulmonary and gastrointestinal involvement were common, including interstitial lung disease and gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Pulmonary hypertension was more prevalent in lcSSc. Autoantibody analysis showed antinuclear antibodies positivity in 57.9%, RF in 6.1%, anti-topoisomerase I (anti-Scl-70) antibody in 28.1%, anticentromere antibody (ACA) in 24.8% and double positivity for anti-Scl-70 and ACA in 6.5%, with notable gender-based differences. Overlap syndrome patients showed higher comorbidity rates and more frequent therapeutic use. Regional variations in disease patterns were also observed. This nationwide study provides a comprehensive profile of SSc in Egypt, highlighting a predominance of female patients with disease onset in the fourth decade of life. We observed significant gender-based differences in clinical manifestations and autoantibody profiles, with prevalent organ involvement including pulmonary and gastrointestinal complications. These findings underscore the importance of early recognition, tailored management strategies, and ongoing research to improve patient outcomes in SSc.

items.title: Phase II randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study of nemolizumab with an extension period in adult patients with systemic sclerosis: THESSALIA study design and rationale.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare, autoimmune, inflammatory and multisystem connective tissue disease, characterised by widespread vasculopathy and abnormal collagen deposition, leading to fibrosis of the skin and internal organs with significant morbidity and mortality. Preclinical and clinical evidence supports a pathogenic role for interleukin (IL)-31 signalling in driving fibrosis. Nemolizumab, a humanised monoclonal antibody targeting the IL-31 receptor alpha (IL-31RA) chain, is expected to confer both anti-inflammatory and antifibrotic effects by reducing skin thickening and slowing the progression of pulmonary fibrosis in SSc-associated interstitial lung disease. THESSALIA (NCT07047690) is a phase II, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study with an extension phase evaluating the efficacy, safety and pharmacokinetics of nemolizumab in adult patients with limited or diffuse cutaneous SSc with active disease. 162 patients are planned to be recruited. Efficacy will be assessed at week 52 by change from baseline in modified Rodnan skin score (primary endpoint). Lung function and the overall disease activity will be assessed via change from baseline in forced vital capacity (FVC) in patients with SSc-associated interstitial lung disease and the revised Composite Response Index in SSc, respectively (key secondary endpoints). Comprehensive safety, pharmacokinetic, immunogenicity and exploratory biomarker assessments and genotyping are also included. The THESSALIA study is currently recruiting patients and is planned to be conducted at approximately 120 sites globally. The sponsor has ensured that the local Institutional Review Board/Independent Ethics Committee in all countries involved approved the study. NCT07047690.

items.title: Improving the patient care pathway in systemic sclerosis: insights from patients and clinicians in Italy.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare autoimmune disease characterised by progressive fibrosis affecting multiple organs. This study was set out to uncover disparities in healthcare access among Italian patients with SSc, identify actionable strategies for improving the patient care pathway and assess the costs of living with SSc. A comprehensive 55-item multiple-choice questionnaire was distributed through the patient association Gruppo Italiano per la Lotta alla Sclerodermia, targeting individuals living with SSc. The survey explored patients' experiences following diagnosis, access to treatments and the financial impact of the disease. An interdisciplinary expert panel convened to interpret the findings and develop recommendations. Out of 256 respondents, 40% had lived with SSc for more than 12 years suggesting a sample bias towards advanced disease stages. While nearly three-quarters (75%) were satisfied with their medical care, only 59% felt well-informed about available treatment options. Non-pharmacological therapies, such as physiotherapy, were underused with fewer than half of respondents reporting access. 61% of patients were responsible for covering their own expenses related to these services, pointing to significant gaps in public healthcare coverage. Economic and logistical challenges were widespread: 39% had skipped care due to long wait times or high costs and unpaid leave was common among both patients (15.5%) and their caregivers (38%). Overall, despite high satisfaction with direct medical care, considerable challenges remain in enhancing disease management, patient education, reducing socioeconomic burden and improving overall quality of life. The findings highlight an urgent need for a structured, interdisciplinary chronic care model tailored to SSc. Priorities include expanding access to non-pharmacological therapies, strengthening patient education and addressing systemic barriers to care. These insights offer a roadmap toward more equitable, patient-centred healthcare for individuals living with SSc.

items.title: Lung ultrasound (LUS) for screening systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD): a radiation-free alternative?
items.abstract: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of lung ultrasound (LUS) in detecting interstitial lung disease (ILD) in patients with systemic sclerosis (SSc), as a radiation-free alternative to high-resolution CT (HRCT). In this cross-sectional study, 18 adult participants with SSc underwent LUS and HRCT within 1 month as part of routine clinical care without previous knowledge of presence or absence of ILD. A 14-zone LUS protocol was applied and B-lines were quantified using two semiquantitative scoring systems. LUS results were compared with HRCT interpreted by a blinded thoracic radiologist. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV) and negative predictive value (NPV) were calculated. Spearman correlation was used to evaluate the association between total B-line counts and HRCT severity. Of 18 participants, ILD was identified by HRCT in 72.2%. Using B-lines cut-off ≤5, LUS demonstrated 100% sensitivity, 40% specificity, 81% PPV and 100% NPV. Using B-lines cut-off ≤10, sensitivity was 92%, specificity 80%, PPV 92% and NPV 80%. B-line counts correlated strongly with HRCT severity (Spearman ρ=0.80, p<0.0001). LUS shows high sensitivity and acceptable specificity for detecting ILD in SSc, particularly when using a higher B-line threshold. Future studies that incorporate LUS as an upfront screening tool are needed for validation of our findings.

items.title: Serum KL-6 and IL-18 as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers in systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease: insights from a 24-month prospective cohort study.
items.abstract: To evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic value of serum Krebs von den Lungen-6 (KL-6) and interleukin-18 (IL-18) in detecting interstitial lung disease (ILD) and predicting disease progression and mortality in patients with systemic sclerosis (SSc) over a 24-month period. Prospective longitudinal cohort study. Single-centre tertiary referral unit for systemic autoimmune diseases. 74 patients fulfilling classification criteria for SSc were included and stratified according to ILD status based on high-resolution CT (HRCT). Participants underwent serial clinical assessments, pulmonary function tests and serum biomarker measurements (KL-6, IL-18 and IL-18 binding protein) at baseline, 12 months and 24 months. Presence and severity of ILD on HRCT, ILD progression (defined by decline in forced vital capacity (FVC) and radiological worsening using the modified Goh score) and all-cause mortality. At baseline, 38% of patients had ILD, increasing to 54% at 24 months. The proportion with ≥20% lung involvement rose from 32% to 43%, and extensive disease increased from 11% to 25% (p=0.03). Serum KL-6 and IL-18 levels were significantly higher in patients with SSc-ILD and correlated inversely with % Forced Vital Capacity (%FVC) (r=-0.51, p=0.0007) and %DLCO (r=-0.38, p=0.001). Longitudinal increases in KL-6 were associated with lung function decline and HRCT progression. An annual increase of +14.18 U/mL predicted progressive ILD (area under the curve (AUC) 0.803, p=0.002; sensitivity 80%, specificity 64%). For mortality, an annual increase of +71.17 U/mL demonstrated high predictive accuracy (AUC 0.91, 95% CI 0.84 to 0.99, p<0.0001; sensitivity 75%, specificity 85%). A decline in diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) of -17% per year was also associated with mortality. In multivariable analysis, changes in KL-6, DLCO, C-reactive protein and anti-Scl-70 positivity independently predicted ILD progression, while immunosuppressive therapy was protective (OR 0.27, 95% CI 0.16 to 0.92, p=0.004). Serum KL-6 and IL-18 are valuable diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers in SSc-ILD. Baseline levels reflect disease presence and severity, while longitudinal changes in KL-6 provide robust prediction of progression and mortality. These findings support their integration into routine clinical practice for risk stratification and disease monitoring.

items.title: Association of IgA Antiphospholipid Antibodies With Lupus Anticoagulant Phenotype and Characterization of T-Cell Immune Deviation.
items.abstract: The serological diagnosis of antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) has long relied on IgG/IgM antiphospholipid antibodies (aPLs), whereas the clinical significance of IgA aPL remains controversial. Meanwhile, the role of T-cell immune imbalance in APS pathogenesis is increasingly recognized, but its association with specific antibody isotypes and the pathway by which it influences the lupus anticoagulant (LA) phenotype have not been systematically elucidated. To evaluate the associations of different aPL isotypes with peripheral blood lymphocyte subsets and coagulation parameters, and to determine whether IgA aPL are independently associated with LA positivity within the measured antibody panel and how this relates to immune deviation. A total of 212 patients who underwent aPL profiling (including IgA isotypes), lymphocyte subset analysis, and LA testing were retrospectively enrolled. Spearman correlation analysis was used to evaluate the correlations among antibody isotypes, immune cell subsets, and coagulation indices. Independent-samples   ∗ t ∗ -test compared lymphocyte subsets between IgA-positive and IgA-negative groups. A bootstrap mediation model was constructed to examine whether IgA aPL mediate the relationship between CD8 + T cells and the LA phenotype. Multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for inflammatory markers, age, sex, and immune cell subsets, was used to identify factors independently associated with composite laboratory LA positivity. Antibody concentrations were log 10 -transformed, and odds ratios (ORs) are expressed per 1-unit increase in log 10 antibody concentration. Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied to exploratory correlation analyses. In unadjusted analyses, IgA aPL correlated positively with the percentage of CD8 + T cells (r = 0.170, p = 0.038) and negatively with absolute CD4 + T-cell count (r = -0.173, p = 0.035) and the CD4/CD8 ratio (r = -0.182, p = 0.026); however, after BH-FDR correction, most lymphocyte-aPL correlations were exploratory, and only the CD19+ B-cell/ACL-IgA correlation was borderline significant (q ≈ 0.050). The absolute CD4 + T-cell count in the IgA-positive group (n = 14) was significantly lower than that in the IgA-negative group (n = 198) (382.42 ± 232.17 vs. 637.72 ± 366.96, p = 0.019). Regarding coagulation, the correlation coefficients between IgA aPL and the LA surrogate marker ndRVVT-R ranged from 0.39 to 0.41 (both p  < 0.01); ACL-IgA showed significant positive correlations with D-dimer (r = 0.20) and fibrin/fibrinogen (Fib) degradation product (FDP) (r = 0.19) (both p  < 0.01), and these remained significant after FDR correction (D-dimer q = 0.0013; FDP q = 0.0064). Mediation analysis revealed no significant mediating effect of IgA aPL on the relationship between CD8 + T cells and the LA phenotype (the 95% CI of the indirect effect included 0). In multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, NLR, and immune cell subsets, β 2 -glycoprotein I (β2GPI)-IgA (OR = 1.101, 95% CI: 1.018-1.191, p = 0.016) and ACL-IgA (OR = 1.078, 95% CI: 1.023-1.137, p = 0.005) were each independently associated with LA positivity in separate models, whereas CD4 + , CD8 + , CD19 + cells, and NLR were not statistically significant. Within the measured antibody panel, IgA aPL were independently associated with LA positivity and showed a distinct immune association pattern characterized by reduced absolute CD4 + T cells and a relative increase in CD8+ T-cell percentage. However, mediation analysis did not support IgA aPL as mediators (Ms) of the CD8 + -LA relationship. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation with Treg phenotyping, apoptotic/PS exposure markers, and aPS/prothrombin time (PT) testing.
